title: Senior Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning Engineer
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning Engineer based in Canada.

This is a senior, hands-on engineering role focused on designing and delivering production-grade agentic AI systems for enterprise environments. You will build autonomous AI agents using an established enterprise AI stack, combining Glean with OpenAI/GPT Enterprise and cloud infrastructure on AWS or GCP. You will own solutions end to end, from architecture and development through production deployment, monitoring, evaluation, and continuous improvement. The role requires treating AI agents as reliable software systems, with careful attention to retrieval, reasoning, permissions, actions, security, and observability. You will work on technically complex initiatives where reliability, scalability, and maintainability are essential. This is an opportunity to apply advanced LLM and agentic AI expertise to high-impact enterprise use cases while working alongside experienced technology professionals.

Accountabilities

  • Design and develop production-grade agentic AI systems that can reliably support real enterprise users and business workflows.

  • Build autonomous agents using Glean as the agent platform and OpenAI/GPT Enterprise as the reasoning layer, deployed within AWS or GCP environments.

  • Own AI agents throughout their full lifecycle, including architecture, implementation, production deployment, monitoring, evaluation, troubleshooting, and iteration.

  • Design robust agent workflows incorporating triggers, retrieval, multi-step reasoning, tool and function calling, actions, permissions, and memory.

  • Implement retrieval-augmented generation and enterprise search capabilities while ensuring high-quality retrieval and appropriate runtime permission enforcement.

  • Establish evaluation frameworks and measurable quality standards to assess agent performance systematically rather than relying solely on manual inspection.

  • Optimize AI systems for reliability, security, maintainability, cost efficiency, and latency at enterprise scale.

  • Apply strong observability and production engineering practices to identify issues, improve system performance, and support continuous iteration.

    • Requirements:

    • Bring 3+ years of hands-on experience building and operating LLM-powered systems in production environments used by real customers or users.

    • Demonstrate practical experience designing agentic AI workflows, including tool and function calling, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), multi-step orchestration, and memory.

    • Have deep hands-on experience with the OpenAI API and GPT Enterprise, including model selection, prompt engineering, structured outputs, function calling, cost and latency optimization, and enterprise data-handling controls.

    • Demonstrate strong prompt-engineering discipline and an evaluation-first mindset, with experience using measurable evaluations to assess and improve agent quality.

    • Have direct, hands-on production experience with Glean, including Agent Builder, Apps, Actions, Model Hub, connectors, and permission-aware retrieval; this is a mandatory requirement for the role.

    • Possess working knowledge of enterprise search and RAG architectures on Glean, including indexing, connectors, retrieval quality, and runtime permission enforcement.

    • Understand how to approach AI agents as production software, with strong awareness of reliability, security, observability, scalability, and maintainability.

    • Demonstrate strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, combined with the ability to work independently on technically complex AI engineering challenges.

    • Communicate effectively with technical and business stakeholders and collaborate within a global, multidisciplinary engineering environment.

      • Benefits:

      • Work alongside highly skilled technology professionals in a collaborative, friendly, and open-door environment.

      • Contribute to large-scale projects with global impact while expanding your expertise in advanced AI and machine learning technologies.

      • Access tailored learning opportunities, including internal meetups, conferences, workshops, Udemy courses, language training, and company-paid certifications.

      • Explore internal mobility opportunities across diverse domains and projects to build hands-on experience with emerging technologies.

      • Benefit from healthcare coverage, Basic Life Insurance, and short- and long-term disability insurance in accordance with the applicable benefits plans.

      • Work remotely from Canada while contributing to enterprise-scale AI initiatives and innovative technology projects.

How Jobgether works:

title: Quality Inspector, CMM
description:
K2 is building the largest and highest-power satellites ever flown, unlocking performance levels previously out of reach across every orbit. Backed by over $1 billion in total funding from leading investors including Altimeter Capital, ICONIQ, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Redpoint Ventures, and T. Rowe Price — and with over $1 billion in signed contracts across commercial and US government customers, we're mass-producing the highest-power satellite platforms ever built for missions from LEO to deep space.

The rise of heavy-lift launch vehicles is shifting the industry from an era of mass constraint to one of mass abundance, and we believe this new era demands a fundamentally different class of spacecraft. Engineered to survive the harshest radiation environments and to fully capitalize on today's and tomorrow's massive rockets, K2 satellites deliver unmatched capability at constellation scale and across multiple orbits.

With multiple launches in 2027 and plans to scale to 100 satellites a year, we're Building Bigger — helping develop the solar system and build toward a Kardashev Type II (K2) civilization. If you are a motivated individual who thrives in a fast-paced environment and you're excited about contributing to the success of a high-growth Series D-funded company, we'd love for you to apply.

The Role

As a Quality Inspector, CMM you will be responsible for dimensional inspection and metrology of precision aerospace hardware supporting satellite manufacturing and integration. You will own complex dimensional inspection using CMMs and other metrology equipment and work closely with Manufacturing Engineering, Quality Engineering, Supply Chain, Production, and suppliers to ensure hardware meets engineering requirements.

This role will also help establish K2’s internal dimensional inspection capability, evaluate supplier inspection capability, and use inspection data to improve supplier performance and optimize K2’s receiving inspection process

Responsibilities

  • Perform dimensional inspection of complex machined and fabricated aerospace hardware using a CMM and conventional inspection equipment
  • Develop, execute, and improve CMM inspection programs
  • Interpret engineering drawings and GD&T requirements to establish appropriate inspection strategies
  • Perform first article, receiving, in-process, and final dimensional inspections
  • Support inspection of large structures and assemblies using laser tracker or other portable metrology equipment
  • Analyze dimensional inspection results and clearly communicate findings to Manufacturing Engineering, Quality Engineering, Production, and suppliers
  • Support machine shop process development through dimensional feedback
  • Partner with Supply Chain and Quality Engineering to evaluate supplier inspection capability and performance
  • Review supplier FAIRs and dimensional inspection reports and help determine when incoming inspection can be reduced based on demonstrated supplier performance
  • Maintain inspection equipment, programs, records, and calibration status
  • Train other inspectors and technicians on dimensional inspection methods

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of dimensional inspection or metrology experience in aerospace, precision machining, or similar manufacturing
  • Strong CMM inspection experience
  • Strong understanding of GD&T and ASME Y14.5
  • Experience inspecting tight-tolerance machined components
  • Ability to independently interpret complex engineering drawings
  • Proficiency with precision measuring equipment
  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills

Nice to Have

  • Experience programming CMMs using Polyworks, Calypso, PC-DMIs, or similar software
  • Laser tracker experience
  • AS9102 FAIR experience
  • Experience with large aerospace structures
  • Experience supporting supplier qualification or source inspection

Additional Requirements

  • Willing to work overtime and weekends as needed
  • Must be able to stoop, bend, crawl, and maneuver in tight spaces
  • Must be able to lift and carry parts or equipment up to 50 lbs. unassisted

Compensation and Benefits:

  • Hourly pay range for this non-exempt role is $33 - $48 + equity in the company
  • Compensation will be based on several factors including, but not limited to: knowledge and skills, education, and experience level
  • Comprehensive benefits package including paid time off, medical/dental/vision coverage, life insurance, paid parental leave, and many other perks

If you don’t meet 100% of the preferred skills and experience, we encourage you to still apply! Building a spacecraft unlike any other requires a team unlike any other and non-traditional career twists and turns are encouraged!

If you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know.

title: Director Privacy Counsel
description:
The Opportunity

Adobe's Privacy Office is hiring an experienced privacy attorney as Director, Associate General Counsel to lead privacy legal support for Adobe's Customer & Experience Organization (CXO) - the business behind Adobe's Digital Experience products and enterprise data platforms. This is your chance to work for a global brand with an unparalleled culture where privacy really matters!


You will lead a group of privacy lawyers and provide main privacy legal guidance to Sales Legal, Product Legal, and Partnerships Legal within CXO. Responsibilities involve offering product privacy counsel, assisting with enterprise deals, and tackling AdTech/MarTech and data platform issues critical to enterprise digital experiences. This position requires both managing the team and actively handling challenging product and commercial privacy concerns.


What you'll Do


Lead the CXO Privacy Legal team

  • Coordinate, mentor, and develop a team of privacy counsel supporting the CXO business.
  • Set priorities and balance coverage across product, sales, and partnerships demand.
  • Take responsibility for the team's operating model, playbooks, PIAs, and knowledge repositories.

Advise product and technical teams

  • Engage with Product Legal, Engineering, Product, Security, and Marketing teams to promote the development and adoption of Privacy-By-Design frameworks for digital marketing solutions and systems to address privacy and security risks while enabling product innovation.
  • Counsel product and engineering teams regarding Privacy-By-Design for data platforms, customer data platforms (CDPs), identity resolution, data collaboration, journey orchestration, and AI-enabled marketing features.
  • Develop, apply, and evaluate privacy impact assessments for Adobe products and technologies, including new AI initiatives. Lead projects to simplify and improve the privacy assessment process.
  • Build and scale product privacy playbooks and templates so mentorship reaches teams without one-off review.
  • Track and implement developments in privacy law, data-broker regulation, AdTech/MarTech enforcement, and AI governance.

Support enterprise deals

  • Support Sales Legal and other legal teams in handling privacy-related negotiations involving customers, partners, and vendors. Deliver regular training, develop templates and playbooks, and give hands-on assistance for strategic deals. Identify and promote improvements to make privacy negotiations more efficient.
  • Be a privacy ambassador on enterprise customer calls and in meetings with external collaborators.
  • Serve as counsel for privacy and data-protection terms in enterprise sales negotiations, providing heightened support during quarter-end and year-end close cycles.
  • Manage advertising and marketing technology along with data-platform privacy
  • Act as a strategic advisor to business leaders to help make privacy a competitive differentiator for Adobe.
  • Serve as a privacy advocate inside Adobe to help grow our culture of privacy (e.g., conduct trainings, represent the Privacy Office in product strategy and development sessions).
  • Advise on privacy and regulatory issues specific to AdTech/MarTech technology. This includes data sourcing and enrichment, data-broker regulation, consent and preference management, and messaging/communications compliance (e.g., TCPA).
  • Structure data integrations and partnerships to manage regulatory-classification risk.

What you need to succeed

  • J.D. degree and membership in at least one state bar.
  • Minimum 10+ years of relevant privacy legal experience, including substantial in-house experience at a technology, SaaS, or data-driven company, and demonstrated people-management experience; management of attorneys strongly preferred.
  • Deep experience advising product and development groups on data platforms, identity resolution, and/or CDP, on the privacy issues raised by generative AI and AI-enabled products, and data-broker regulations.
  • Experience negotiating privacy and data-security terms in B2B/enterprise agreements.
  • Sound, business-pragmatic judgment; able to operate independently on complex matters while raising issues appropriately; strong executive communication skills.
  • Outstanding interpersonal skills with a dedication to integrity.

About Adobe

Adobe empowers everyone to create through innovative platforms and tools that unleash creativity, productivity and personalized customer experiences. Adobe’s industry-leading offerings including Adobe Acrobat Studio, Adobe Express, Adobe Firefly, Creative Cloud, Adobe Experience Platform, Adobe Experience Manager, and GenStudio enable people and businesses to turn ideas into impact, powered by AI and driven by human ingenuity.

Learn more about Adobe life, including our values and culture, focus on people, purpose and community, Adobe for All, comprehensive benefits programs, the stories we tell, the customers we serve, and how you can help us advance our mission of empowering everyone to create.

title: Pressroom Lead- Backup Litho Printing Operator (K&B & KBA Presses)
description:

Hourly Full-Time (Monday-Friday, 10 pm - 6 am)

Conway Graphics

730 Enterprise Ave.

Conway, AR 72032

The Job You Will Perform:

Principle Duties and Responsibilities

· Promote safe work practices and encourage compliance with all safety policies, PPE requirements, and environmental standards.

· Lead by example in maintaining a safe, clean, and organized work area.

· Identify, correct when possible, and promptly report safety hazards, unsafe conditions, and near misses to supervision.

· Provide initial assistance during workplace incidents and promptly notify the appropriate supervisor or manager.

· Support emergency response efforts, including the use of available first aid and emergency equipment, as trained.

· Assist with incident fact gathering and documentation by providing timely and accurate information to leadership.

· Reinforce safety expectations during shift start-up meetings, job assignments, and daily operations.

· Participate in safety observations, audits, inspections, and training activities as assigned.

· Encourage employee involvement in safety initiatives and promote a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.

· Serve as a safety resource for team members by answering basic questions and directing concerns to appropriate leadership.

Operational Leadership & Coordination

· Coordinate pressroom production activities across Prepress, Sheeters, Press, and Stackdown to optimize workflow and efficiency.

· Partner with supervisors to align downstream production expectations, scheduling, and throughput goals.

· Lead pressroom communications, training, and performance expectations for press crews.

· Ensure all jobs meet quality and quantity standards while adhering to customer specifications.

· Manage waste tracking, reporting, and cost control initiatives.

· Maintain documentation including production records, EOS reports, and material usage tracking.

Quality & Continuous Improvement

· Enforce quality control (QC) procedures, including sample pulls and adherence to QC manual standards.

· Evaluate sample sheets and maintain documentation for GMI and ISO compliance.

· Support standardization efforts including color management, consistency, and process control.

Equipment & Technical Oversight

· Troubleshoot lithographic offset press and mechanical issues; escalate to Maintenance or OEM support as required.

· Ensure completion of preventative maintenance (IES/ZES) in accordance with Safety and operational standards.

· Support continuous machine reliability and performance improvements.

Backup Press Operator Responsibilities

· Operate lithographic offset presses as needed to support production and staffing requirements.

· Perform all duties associated with 1st Press Operator role including setup, operation, troubleshooting, and quality control.

Additional Responsibilities

· Lead or participate in special projects, trials, and process improvements.

· Maintain housekeeping standards aligned with 5S/6S practices.

· Complete required training (Safety, OSHA, equipment, SDS, etc.).

· Perform other duties as assigned.

Technical Skills Required

· Ability to perform all functions of a 1st Press Operator.

· Advanced knowledge of lithographic press systems (K&B, KBA) and related mechanical functions.

· Strong troubleshooting capabilities across press systems and print quality issues.

· Proficiency in:

· Color management (Cielab, TVI, dE, G7, grayscale standardization)

· Spectrophotometer usage

· Press control systems and software (Qualtronics, Logotronics, Kiwi FFF)

· Working knowledge of:

· Fountain solution chemistry (pH, conductivity)

· Ink/water balance and emulsification control

· Plate sensitivity, toning, misting, slinging, and dampening systems

· Ability to perform mechanical adjustments including roller settings, bearing replacement, and press calibration.

· Ability to use precision measurement tools (micrometer, durometer, gauges).

· Ability to perform mathematical calculations, conversions, and measurements.

· Ability to visually distinguish primary colors.

Hours of Work

Work hours are dependent on assigned shift and production demands. Overtime and on-call responsibilities may be required

Job Requirements

· Demonstrated leadership and ability to effectively communicate and direct team members.

· Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment.

· Strong mathematical and measurement skills.

· Ability to obtain and maintain forklift certification with a clean driving record.

· Commitment to maintaining a safe and clean workspace in accordance with 5S/6S standards.

· Compliance with all company policies and the International Paper handbook.

· Must be reliable and prepared to begin work at the designated shift time.

The scope includes spillway widening, dam crest raising, berm and spillway re-profiling, right-hand wall strengthening, plunge pool widening and deepening, flip bucket extension, instrumentation upgrades and associated enabling works. It is a rare opportunity to join Seymour Whyte on a technically challenging, high-profile project with major civil, structural, hydraulic and dam safety interfaces, and real long-term community impact.

title: MANAGING DIRECTOR, HEAD OF ADVISOR TRANSITIONS & INTEGRATION
description:
About Cresset

Cresset is a firm built by clients, for clients. As an independent, award-winning multi-family office and private investment firm, we are reimagining the way wealth is experienced. Our purpose is to help ensure that both wealth and life are fully optimized**—integrated, intentional, and aligned with each client’s vision of success.

We provide access to the caliber of talent, ideas, and investment opportunities typically available to the largest single-family offices and institutions. Our approach is personalized, entrepreneurial, and client-first.

Cresset was built to endure. We are creating a 100+ year firm—one focused on delivering an exceptional experience, not only for the families we serve but for the team that serves them. Recognized by Barron’s among the nation’s top multi-family offices,* Cresset is guided by long-term relationships, shared success, and a belief that wealth should serve a life well lived.

Job Description

As Cresset continues to grow through acquisitions, lift-outs, strategic hires, and organic expansion, exceptional onboarding and integration has become a core differentiator of our business. The Managing Director, Head of Advisor Transitions & Integration is responsible for overseeing all aspects of advisor and client transitions from initial due diligence through full integration. This leader will define the strategy, operating model, governance, and execution standards that enable Cresset to deliver a seamless experience for incoming advisors, their team, and clients. While this role is highly strategic, it is equally operational. During periods of advisor onboarding and integration, this leader is expected to be fully embedded with incoming teams, working side by side with advisors, internal Cresset subject matter experts, custodians and 3rd party partners to coordinate resources, remove obstacles, and ensure the successful transition of clients and assets.

This is not a role that leads integrations from afar; it requires a leader who is equally comfortable developing enterprise strategy and rolling up their sleeves to execute alongside the business teams. During onboarding, this leader is expected to be physically present with incoming teams for multiple, consecutive weeks. They will work directly alongside Advisory Practice Management Operations, Client Service, Technology, HR, Compliance, Legal, and other business functions to ensure resources are effectively coordinated and issues are identified and resolved quickly so advisors and their team members can remain focused on serving clients. Success requires calm leadership under pressure, sound judgment, and the ability to rapidly prioritize competing demands while maintaining an exceptional advisor and client experience.

Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as an active partner to Corporate Development and Advisory Leadership during due diligence to assess operational readiness, integration complexity, technology environments, organizational structures, client service models, and transition risks.
  • Evaluate advisor operating models and identify opportunities to accelerate integration while preserving the elements that make teams successful.
  • Lead readiness planning by developing preliminary integration strategies, day one operating models, transition timelines, pre-close checklists, break readiness, resource requirements and alignment internally and with partners, and risk mitigation and contingency plans ahead of break.
  • Quickly build trusted relationships with incoming leadership teams and team members to establish confidence and ensure a seamless transition.
  • Support late-stage conversations by clearly articulating the integration approach and advisor experience
  • Identify critical decisions that must be made prior to onboarding and ensure appropriate alignment internally and with incoming team.

Integration Execution & Delivery

  • Lead day-to-day execution of integration plans post-break, including regular integration meetings / discussions and working sessions to track progress and resolve blockers
  • Drive coordination across operations, client service, compliance, technology, reporting, finance, and HR
  • Translate strategic integration plans into detailed workstreams, timelines, and deliverables
  • Serve as the primary operator ensuring milestones, risks, and dependencies are actively managed
  • Identify and resolve issues early, pulling in subject matter experts to triage and stabilize and senior leaders as needed to support
  • Establish clear ownership and accountability across all integration workstreams

Advisor & Client Transition

  • Own the advisor transition experience from signed agreement through post-integration stabilization.
  • Serves as the face of Cresset's transition experience for incoming advisors and teams across the following activities: Advisor onboarding strategy, client transition planning, asset migration coordination, custodian conversion planning, communications, readiness and scenario planning, training coordination, service model implementation, and issue escalation and resolution.

Systems & Data Integration

  • Oversee integration of technology tools (ex. Salesforce, Addepar, custodian platforms, and financial planning)
  • Coordinate data migration, validation, and reconciliation
  • Identify and resolve system gaps, inconsistencies, and reporting issues

Investment & Platform Integration

  • Support review and mapping of portfolios, securities, and alternative assets
  • Coordinate platform approvals and transitions with investment and operations teams
  • Address custodial setup, pricing discrepancies, and account structure issues

Process & Playbook Development

  • Develop and refine integration playbooks and best practices
  • Conduct post-mortems, document lessons learned and continuously improve workflows
  • Support scaling the integration function as deal volume grows

The Crisis Specialist is responsible for receiving, responding to, and triaging crisis and healthcare requests. Solari is an award-winning nonprofit that operates a 24/7 crisis line serving statewide in Arizona, Oklahoma and Colorado. Our mission is to Inspire Hope through our talented and compassionate staff.

Since 2007, Solari has been providing crisis contact center services and in that short time has helped thousands of individuals and families connect to the help they need. Additionally, in that short timeframe, Solari has grown to expand services to a peer-run Warm Line, Serious Mental Illness (SMI) determinations, mobile team dispatches, crisis transportation services, emergency room-based assessments, Department of Child Safety (DCS) rapid response and crisis stabilization services, telephone follow-up to those who need it, tragedy support lines and other in-kind services to the community.

title: Senior QA Engineer

title: Lifestyle Director
location: The Preserve at Spring Creek - Garland, TX 75040
description:
Frontier Senior Living is seeking an outstanding Lifestyle Director to develop and promote a strong activity program for The Preserve at Spring Creek community located in Garland, TX. Demonstrated success as a leader in similar settings is required of the Lifestyle Director.

Frontier Senior Living's portfolio of communities spans throughout the United States with each community sharing a commitment to superior service and quality lifestyle for our residents within their own unique setting. Frontier's mission is to provide an enriched and meaningful experience for our residents, team members, and community partners. If you are as committed and passionate about serving the needs of our senior residents as we are, we encourage you to apply and experience the Frontier Difference.

The Lifestyle Director will be responsible for the planning, implementation, and supervision of the day-to-day social, educational, recreational, spiritual, therapeutic individual and group activities, and entertainment and transportation services for the residents living at the community. This includes managing group activities, entertainment and providing transportation services for the residents living at the community. The Lifestyle Director must also be flexible and willing to work shift assigned, weekends, and holidays. Ability to work independently with minimum supervision; problem-solving, conflict management, budgeting.

Primary Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Plan, implement and supervise activities to suit a variety of interests and skill levels for the residents using resident comments and input. Activities may include, but are not limited to: parties, games, weekly exercises, church services, book reading and clubs, crafts, baking and cooking, outside entertainment, travel and transportation, special activities at holidays, fundraisers for specific projects, and resident's birthdays and anniversaries
  • Effectively encourage and actively promote resident participation in activities/social services through internal, formal and informal communication networks
  • Plan "In-community" seminars or lecture series' quarterly for residents, families, and friends
  • Involve and assist the Residents Council and Resident Meetings by playing a key role in their monthly meetings
  • Participate in local activity planners association. Cooperate and exchange ideas and calendars with Lifestyle Directors in affiliated retirement communities
  • Develop programs, activities, seminars, and lectures for the monthly calendar. Print, mail and post the activities calendars to keep all residents and the community aware of the activities going on at the community. Edit and publish the monthly newsletter. Distribute and mail to all residents, prospective residents, family members, community contacts, and employees to keep them informed of things going on at the community
  • Assist at the front desk and cover for missing staff members when necessary
  • Represent the community by giving tours and marketing the community as needed
  • Perform such other tasks as may be required from time-to-time

Frontier Senior Living offers a competitive salary and a work environment that encourages initiative and fosters respect. Frontier Senior Living offers medical, dental, vision, life/AD&D, Flexible Spending Account, Short Term Disability, Accident Insurance, Critical Illness Insurance, and Hospital Indemnity Insurance. We also offer a 401(k) plan with a competitive Match program. To discover more about the Frontier Management team, please visit our site at www.frontiermgmt.com

  • 100명 이상 되는 대규모 개발 조직 & 언리얼 엔진을 사용한 프로젝트에서 개발 PM 역할을 수행하신 분
  • 개발 프로세스 제안 -> 도입 -> 활용 -> 개선까지 경험이 있으신 분

title: Clinical Pharmacy Specialist - Pediatric Hospital Medicine - Abercrombie
description:
We are searching for clinical pharmacy specialists. In the clinical specialist position, you will manage and promote activities appropriate to ensure the medication use process, to serve as mentor to pharmacists who provide services to the medical specialty, and to assist in direct patient care activities to promote optimal drug therapy and resolve medication use problems in a manner developmentally appropriate for the ages of patients served.

Responsibility A: Utilizes practice knowledge and skills to serve as Clinical Practitioner.

• Actively participates in multi-disciplinary rounds with medical specialty services.
• Identifies patients with special medication needs and oversees coordination of activities to ensure proper delivery of drug therapy, including patients requiring extracorporeal therapies.
• Serves as member of patient care committees for medical specialty service. Makes recommendations and implements change to improve patient care
• Performs outcome-directed therapeutic drug monitoring for patients according to guidelines.
• Monitors therapies for drug-drug, drug-nutrient, and drug-laboratory interactions and discusses interactions with appropriate health care professionals to help ensure patient safety and compliance.
• Performs outcome-directed pharmacokinetics monitoring for patients according to guidelines and discusses recommendations with appropriate medical professionals to help provide the best care for the patient.
• Participates in Quality Improvement initiatives to enhance and ensure patient safety for all patients.
Responsibility B: Ensures the medication use process.
• Creates and maintains appropriate and useful policies and procedures affecting areas of responsibility. Makes recommendations as to how services, methods, and procedures can be improved. Establishes action plans to implement appropriate changes.
• Promotes the use of the formulary and follows procedures to obtain non-formulary medications.
• Identifies opportunities for improvement for area of practice; seeks to accomplish these improvements.
• Identifies and suggests agents to be added, deleted, or modified to/within the formulary and database.
• Investigates, follows-up, and takes appropriate action for medication incidents and adverse drug reactions.

Responsibility C: Participates in the education of parents/patients, caregivers, pharmacists, and pharmacy residents and students.


• Participates in the education and training of pharmacy employees, pharmacy students, pharmacy residents, and non-pharmacy personnel. Develops an educational program and a plan and incorporates into pharmacist’s routine increasing their clinical knowledge.
• Provides correct and timely drug information to medical, nursing, and pharmacy staff as needed.
• Perpetuates self-development through publications and/or presentations at a professional society level each year.
• Demonstrates current professional, managerial, and technical knowledge and skills.
• Coordinates performance improvement or quality improvement activities to contribute to improved patient outcomes.
• Develops educational programs, both practice-area specific and general education for pharmacists to ensure good patient care.
• Serves as a preceptor to pharmacists, pharmacy residents and students.
• Actively participates in the development of evidence-based clinical guidelines group to ensure appropriate provision of medical therapy in TCH guidelines.
• Attends one pharmacy or service based professional meeting each year.
• Provide medication education to patients/parents/caregivers as requested by the medical team.


Responsibility D: Communicates with others.


• Collaborates effectively with other members of health care disciplines to provide comprehensive care to patients.
• Communicates positively and appropriately to work effectively as a team.
• Utilizes appropriate skills to help develop a care plan.

title: Floating Case Planner Enhanced Family Foster Care
company: Seamen's Society for Children and Families
description:
This position is eligible for a pay increase upon successfully completing the 3-month orientation period.


The Floating Case Planner is responsible for promoting the safety, permanency, and well-being of children placed in foster care through Seamen’s Society by providing case coverage and support as needed. This role requires flexibility in managing a frequently changing caseload across the Staten Island and Brooklyn locations.

Under the direction of program leadership, the Floating Case Planner provides immediate case coverage, ensuring timely completion of critical tasks, service planning activities, documentation, and follow-up responsibilities. Working collaboratively with children, families, foster parents, and service providers, the Floating Case Planner serves as the primary coordinator of service planning efforts and leads the development, implementation, and monitoring of individualized case plans.


Duties and Responsibilities:

· Provide case coverage and support for assigned cases within the Enhanced Family Foster Care (EFFC) program as directed by program leadership.

· Review assigned cases immediately upon notification from program leadership to assess case status, identify critical needs, and initiate necessary case planning activities.

· Establish timely contact with children, families, foster parents, and service providers to ensure continuity of services and compliance with required casework contacts.

· Manage and complete time-sensitive tasks, follow-up activities, and service coordination responsibilities to maintain effective case oversight.

· Engage families in service planning and begin required contacts and interventions promptly upon assignment.

· Monitor child safety, well-being, and permanency through regular casework contacts, home visits, and ongoing assessment of family functioning.

· Partner with families to develop, implement, and monitor service plans that address identified strengths, needs, and permanency goals.

· Collaborate with interdisciplinary team members and community providers to support each child's medical, mental health, educational, housing, and vocational needs, as applicable.

· Maintain accurate and timely documentation of all case activities in CONNECTIONS in accordance with agency and regulatory requirements.

· Participate in Family Team Conferences (FTCs), Family Assessment and Service Plan (FASP) meetings, and other service-planning activities within established timelines.

· Attend Family Court proceedings for assigned cases and provide written reports and verbal testimony regarding family progress and service-plan outcomes.

· Prepare and submit court reports, permanency hearing reports, and other required documentation in accordance with agency standards and deadlines.

· Support and facilitate meaningful, consistent family visitation and communication to strengthen family relationships and advance permanency goals.

· Identify and address barriers to reunification, kinship placement, adoption, or other permanency outcomes through assessment, advocacy, and service coordination.

· Participate in treatment planning, Trauma Systems Therapy (TST) meetings, and other multidisciplinary forums to support child and family well-being.

· Engage in ongoing professional development, training, and job-related learning opportunities.

· Performs other duties/responsibilities as assigned within the scope of position

title: Quantum Engineer
description:
At Atom Computing, we build quantum computers using arrays of optically trapped neutral atoms that will empower customers to achieve unprecedented computational breakthroughs. Join a world-class team of scientists, engineers, and business professionals to advance the state-of-the-art in quantum computing.

We are looking for Quantum Engineers to work on all aspects of neutral atom quantum computing. As a Quantum Engineer at Atom Computing, you will join a team of talented scientists and engineers who are working to translate fundamental atomic physics to a scalable, fault-tolerant quantum computer.

We welcome applicants from a diverse set of backgrounds, but are specifically interested in candidates with experience in the following fields: Trapping and manipulation of cold atoms; Coherent control of quantum systems (for example: neutral atoms, trapped ions, NV- centers, nuclear magnetic resonance, superconducting qubits); Quantum characterization, verification, and validation (QCVV) techniques.

Responsibilities

  • Design and construct the scientific hardware and control interfaces (both hardware and software) that are the essential backbone of the quantum computing platform.
  • Generate intellectual property related to the design and operation of neutral-atom-based quantum computers.
  • Distill and communicate findings internally, and as appropriate, in external publications and presentations.
  • Capable of lifting and moving objects that weigh up to 25 pounds.

Experience & Education

  • PhD in Physics, Chemistry, Engineering, or a related field.

Required Qualifications

  • Extensive knowledge of the state-of-the-art techniques used in atomic physics and quantum computing research
  • Deep understanding of the fundamental interactions between light and matter.
  • Ability to effectively communicate and collaborate with a diverse team of experimental physicists, hardware, and software engineers.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Familiarity with Python and Git software version control
Atom Computing provides a wide variety of perks and benefits, including fully paid medical, dental, and vision insurance for our employees and their dependents. Additionally, we offer unlimited paid time off, 401K company matching, short- and long-term disability, FSA, dependent care benefits, and life insurance. We also offer drinks, snacks, and catered team lunches in our offices, every day!
The base salary range for this position is between $160,000 - $275,000 commensurate with experience and hiring level: Quantum Engineer, Senior Quantum Engineer, Principal Quantum Engineer and Senior Principal Quantum Engineer. In addition, we offer a 20% annual bonus, sign-on bonus, additional bonus potential and incentive stock options for equity in the company.

title: DESKTOP ENGINEER
description:
We are seeking a Desktop Engineer who is passionate about supporting clinical operations through strong technical execution and a thoughtful, methodical approach to problem solving.


StrideCare is a multi-specialty physician group focused on delivering comprehensive lower extremity care across Texas. Our expert doctors specialize in the treatment of foot and ankle problems, lower extremity care, wound care, vascular and vein care. Our physicians and surgeons offer multi-disciplinary treatment for common and complex conditions including diabetes, peripheral arterial disease, neuropathy, diabetic foot ulcers, venous insufficiency, and wounds.

StrideCare is headquartered in Dallas, Texas with practices across the state.


Job Summary:


StrideCare is seeking a skilled Desktop Engineer to serve as a senior technical resource for end-user computing across our growing clinic network. This is not a script-following help desk role. The ideal candidate is a hands-on technician who can independently diagnose problems across endpoints, identity, networking, and cloud platforms, then implement and document durable fixes. The Desktop Engineer reports to the Infrastructure Manager and works directly with our infrastructure team to support day-to-day operations and contribute to integration projects as StrideCare acquires new practices.


Job Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Serve as Tier 2 escalation point for endpoint, identity, M365, and connectivity issues across all StrideCare locations.
  • Diagnose and resolve complex Windows endpoint issues including profile corruption, Group Policy and Intune policy conflicts, driver and peripheral failures, performance degradation, and application compatibility.
  • Administer Microsoft Entra ID and Intune at the operational level: user and device lifecycle, Conditional Access troubleshooting, compliance policy issues, Autopilot enrollment, and configuration profile deployment.
  • Manage M365 workloads (Exchange Online, SharePoint, Teams, OneDrive) including mailbox configuration, distribution and security group management, sharing and permission troubleshooting, and license assignment.
  • Configure and troubleshoot cloud phone system (UCaaS) users, queues, and call flows; coordinate number porting and provisioning for new sites.
  • Provide endpoint support for clinical applications and peripherals including scanners, label printers, signature pads, and clinical imaging equipment and the workstations that connect to it, including standalone devices.
  • Image, deploy, and decommission Windows endpoints using Intune and Autopilot; maintain hardware standards and asset records.
  • Troubleshoot network connectivity issues at the endpoint and clinic level including DNS, DHCP, wireless authentication, VPN clients, and basic LAN diagnostics.
  • Use PowerShell to perform routine administrative tasks across Entra, Exchange, and endpoint management; modify existing scripts and write straightforward new ones when needed.
  • Document configurations, procedures, and known issues in OneNote and internal knowledge bases.
  • Support integration activities for newly acquired clinics including user provisioning, endpoint migration, and on-site cutover assistance.
  • Participate in IT projects and initiatives as assigned.
  • Adhere to HIPAA regulations and security policies to maintain patient confidentiality and data security.

Qualifications and Education Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 5 years in a desktop engineering, endpoint engineering, or senior help desk role supporting at least 200 users across multiple sites.
  • Minimum of 5 years supporting Windows 10 and Windows 11 in a domain or Entra-joined environment, including the Microsoft 365 stack (Entra ID, Exchange Online, SharePoint, Teams, OneDrive) and Microsoft Office.
  • Demonstrated hands-on experience administering Microsoft Intune, including policy creation, app deployment, compliance and Conditional Access, and Autopilot.
  • Working knowledge of PowerShell sufficient to run, modify, and troubleshoot administrative scripts against Entra, Exchange Online, and endpoints.
  • Practical understanding of DNS, DHCP, TCP/IP, 802.1X, and VPN concepts at a level sufficient to triage endpoint connectivity issues without escalation.
  • Experience supporting a UCaaS or cloud phone platform, including user and call flow administration.
  • Experience with RMM and remote support tooling.
  • Experience supporting a cloud-based EHR or other clinical application in a healthcare environment.
  • Strong written communication skills, including the ability to produce clear technical documentation and ticket notes that another engineer can act on.
  • Ability to work independently, prioritize across competing demands, and exercise judgment on when to resolve, escalate, or pause for input.
  • Availability to travel up to 25% to clinic locations, primarily within Texas with occasional travel to other states as the company expands, and availability for occasional after-hours or weekend work during practice integration cutovers.

title: Director of Investor Relations
description:
Overview

Working at Atlassian

Atlassians can choose where they work – whether in an office, from home, or a combination of the two. That way, Atlassians have more control over supporting their family, personal goals, and other priorities. We can hire people in any country where we have a legal entity. Interviews and onboarding are conducted virtually, a part of being a distributed-first company.

Your future team

The Investor Relations team sits at the heart of Atlassian’s long-term strategy, operating with the mission to drive Atlassian’s long-term narrative to connect investors, employees, and customers with our mission. We own the strategic story the company shares with the global investment community, shaping how our strategy, business model, and performance are understood across Wall Street and internally.

As the Director of Investor Relations, you will serve as a senior IR leader and key partner to the Head of Investor Relations. In this high-impact, highly visible role, you’ll help lead the day-to-day execution of the IR function, represent Atlassian in deep interactions with the investment community, and partner closely with executive leadership. You’ll be the connective tissue between Wall Street, Finance, Legal, Communications, and Product – translating complex financials and technical product strategies into compelling external narratives.

Responsibilities

What you'll do

  • Drive strategic narrative & external messaging: Lead the articulation of Atlassian’s long-term strategic and financial narrative across the investment community, connecting business-model evolution, product milestones, and market dynamics.

  • Lead earnings & financial disclosures: Own the strategy, preparation, and execution of the quarterly earnings cycle – Shareholder Letter, earnings call script, Q&A prep, and investor presentations. Partner with the Disclosure Committee and Legal on 10-Q/10-K filings and ensure rigorous adherence to compliance and selective disclosure standards.

  • Advise and brief executives: Act as a trusted advisor to the CEO, CFO, and Executive Team – preparing detailed briefing documents, anticipating market reactions, and delivering insight ahead of conferences, roadshows, and earnings.

  • Manage investor & analyst engagement: Serve as a primary spokesperson for Atlassian, leading and participating investor meetings, including non-deal roadshows, fireside chats, and major investor conferences.

  • Deliver signature IR events: Spearhead the planning and execution of flagship moments, including Investor Day and other buy-side events, ensuring cohesive content alignment across product, go-to-market, and finance leadership.

  • Own market sentiment & feedback loops: Conduct proactive investor perception analyses and surveys to gauge how Atlassian's strategy and key bets land with the Street, synthesize feedback into actionable recommendations for the C-suite.

  • Lead cross-functionally: Be a leader and partner across Finance, Strategy, Corporate Development, Legal, Data Science, and Corporate Communications to align internal teams, help drive the business, and ensure consistent messaging across all stakeholders.

Compensation

At Atlassian, we strive to design equitable, explainable, and competitive compensation programs. We follow consistent hiring practices and account for each candidate's skills, knowledge, and experience when setting base pay within the range.

Please visit go.atlassian.com/payzones for more information on which locations are included in each of our geographic pay zones. However, please confirm the zone for your specific location with your recruiter.

This role may also be eligible for benefits, bonuses, commissions, and equity.

Pay Ranges

In The United States, we have three geographic pay zones. For this role, our current base pay ranges for new hires in each zone are:

Zone A: $213,300 - $278,475

Zone B: $191,970 - $250,628

Zone C: $177,039 - $231,134

Qualifications

Your background

  • Experience: 10+ years of relevant experience across sell-side equity research (covering software/SaaS or internet), in-house Investor Relations, and/or Corporate Development at a high-growth public technology company.

  • Executive presence & communication: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with the poise, polish, and credibility to represent Atlassian with institutional investors, analysts, and C-level executives.

  • Industry acumen: Deep understanding of software business models, enterprise technology trends, and SaaS operational and financial metrics.

  • Wall Street credibility: Proven track record of managing relationships with top-tier institutional shareholders and sell-side analysts.

  • Leadership & execution mindset: A self-starter who balances strategic vision with a willingness to dive into execution, with the capacity and readiness to grow and mentor a team.

Benefits & Perks

Atlassian offers a wide range of perks and benefits designed to support you, your family and to help you engage with your local community. Our offerings include health and wellbeing resources, paid volunteer days, and so much more. To learn more, visit go.atlassian.com/perksandbenefits.

About Atlassian

At Atlassian, we're motivated by a common goal: to unleash the potential of every team. Our software products help teams all over the planet and our solutions are designed for all types of work. Team collaboration through our tools makes what may be impossible alone, possible together.

We believe that the unique contributions of all Atlassians create our success. To ensure that our products and culture continue to incorporate everyone's perspectives and experience, we never discriminate based on race, religion, national origin, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, or marital, veteran, or disability status. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

To provide you the best experience, we can support with accommodations or adjustments at any stage of the recruitment process. Simply inform our Recruitment team during your conversation with them.

To learn more about our culture and hiring process, visit go.atlassian.com/crh.

In line with local law, identity verification (which may include use of biometric data) is a condition of employment with Atlassian for employment fraud purposes.

title: Commercial Director, Public Health (Vector Control)
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Commercial Director, Public Health (Vector Control) based in United States.

This senior commercial leadership role will drive growth in the U.S. vector control and public health market, with a particular focus on invasive Aedes mosquitoes and associated disease risks. You will lead market development, pipeline generation, contracting, and strategic partnerships across mosquito control districts and public health organizations. The role combines commercial strategy with hands-on business development, requiring strong knowledge of government procurement and public-sector funding environments. Based in Florida or a region with proven Florida commercial experience, you will help translate policy momentum and public health priorities into sustainable programs. You will work closely with commercial, policy, product, science, regulatory, and operations teams to ensure solutions are both commercially viable and operationally deliverable. This is an opportunity to shape an emerging market and contribute directly to innovative approaches to protecting communities from mosquito-borne diseases.

Accountabilities

  • Translate the U.S. commercial strategy into actionable market and account plans, prioritizing opportunities according to disease risk, available budgets, customer readiness, and potential for adoption.

  • Own the commercial pipeline from initial opportunity through signed contract, delivering against revenue targets while maintaining accurate forecasting and disciplined opportunity management.

  • Develop pricing strategies and commercial models, including multi-year vector suppression programs, in collaboration with Product, Finance, and other relevant teams.

  • Monitor market developments, competing approaches, customer needs, and emerging opportunities, translating market intelligence into recommendations for product, operational, and commercial planning.

  • Contribute to the medium- and long-term U.S. business strategy by identifying priority markets, customer segments, commercial models, and growth opportunities.

  • Bring customer and market insights into the development of next-generation vector control solutions designed for the U.S. public health market.

  • Build senior-level relationships with mosquito control districts, state, county, and local health departments, federal agencies, professional associations, and other relevant stakeholders.

  • Coordinate federal engagement with policy colleagues, including potential relationships with agencies such as the CDC, EPA, and other government departments.

  • Develop customer-focused delivery and technology partnerships with clearly defined success measures and pathways toward sustainable, multi-year contracts.

  • Represent the organization at industry conferences, mosquito control district board meetings, public forums, and other relevant events to strengthen market presence and relationships.

  • Lead proposals, bids, contracting, and negotiations across federal, state, county, and local procurement processes, including cooperative agreements and special-district funding cycles.

  • Identify and pursue supplemental funding opportunities, including federal cooperative agreements, state appropriations, and philanthropic funding sources.

  • Partner with Operations, Science, and Regulatory teams to ensure commercial commitments are deliverable, compliant, and aligned with the standards expected by public-sector customers and communities.

    • Requirements:

    • Bring at least 10 years of experience in commercial leadership, business development, account management, or related roles, including at least 5 years in a senior-level position, ideally within government, public health, or another highly regulated environment.

    • Have a strong understanding of the U.S. mosquito control and public health landscape, including how mosquito control districts and health departments plan, budget, procure, and implement programs.

    • Demonstrate a proven track record of winning and scaling multi-year public-sector contracts through complex procurement processes, funding cycles, and stakeholder environments.

    • Bring established relationships across U.S. vector control, public health, biosecurity, government, or related professional communities.

    • Have experience developing go-to-market strategies, commercial pipelines, pricing models, and market-entry approaches, ideally within a technology-led, innovative, or start-up environment.

    • Knowledge of sterile insect techniques or other innovative vector control technologies is highly desirable.

    • Be a credible and persuasive communicator who can effectively engage community stakeholders, mosquito control district boards, healthcare and public health leaders, and federal officials.

    • Demonstrate strong commercial judgment, negotiation skills, persistence, and the ability to turn complex opportunities into sustainable business partnerships.

    • Be proactive, resourceful, and comfortable creating processes and commercial strategies in an evolving environment where established playbooks may not yet exist.

    • Demonstrate resilience, urgency, adaptability, and a collaborative approach when working across an international and multidisciplinary organization.

    • Be comfortable adapting working patterns when needed to support colleagues, customers, and partners across different time zones.

    • Professional-level Spanish is an advantage.

    • Hold a BA/BS degree or equivalent; an MBA, MPH, or degree in entomology, biology, public health, or a related field is beneficial.

    • Be based in Florida or another region with demonstrated professional experience in Florida, be legally authorized to work in the United States, and be willing to travel extensively across the country as required.

      • Benefits:

      • Senior commercial leadership opportunity with direct responsibility for U.S. market growth and revenue development.

      • Opportunity to shape emerging vector control markets and contribute to innovative public health programs addressing mosquito-borne disease risks.

      • High-impact work at the intersection of public health, biosecurity, technology, science, and government.

      • Exposure to senior stakeholders across mosquito control districts, public health organizations, government agencies, professional associations, and strategic partners.

      • Opportunity to collaborate with multidisciplinary teams spanning commercial, policy, science, technology, regulatory, and operations.

      • Dynamic, international, and mission-driven working environment with significant autonomy and ownership.

      • Opportunity to help influence the adoption and commercialization of next-generation vector control technologies across the United States.

      • Full-time, remote role with Florida-based market responsibility and extensive U.S. travel.

title: DevOps Engineer ITSM - ServiceNow
description:
Are you the bridge between business and IT, with a passion for data, regulations, and the banking domain of Treasury and Funding within the public sector?

  • Samenwerken met stakeholders binnen IT, security en business teams

Platform & End User Automation richt zich op gestandaardiseerde, schaalbare en veilige dienstverlening voor eindgebruikers en platformen, met de nadruk op automatisering, voorspelbare levering, security en stabiele operatie.

Je rapporteert aan de Manager Workplace. Je maakt deel uit van de afdeling Workplace.

De afdeling Workplace bestaat uit ongeveer 13 medewerkers, waaronder IT Supportmedewerkers, Config & Asset Managers, DevOps Engineers, de Manager Workplace en een Product Manager. Je werkt voornamelijk samen met je eigen team en met procesmanagers binnen je team en andere teams.
