title: Full-Time Traveling Audiologist-Long Term Care
description:
Join ExcelHealth Group as a Full-Time Traveling Audiologist
ExcelHealth Group is seeking a full-time, patient-centered Audiologist to provide high-quality hearing healthcare services to residents in long-term care and skilled nursing facilities throughout the state. This role is ideal for a licensed provider who values clinical independence, enjoys working in different care settings, and wants to make a meaningful difference for residents who may have limited access to audiology services.


Why This Role Stands Out

As a Traveling Audiologist, you will visit assigned long-term care and skilled nursing facilities to evaluate hearing needs, perform audiologic testing, support hearing aid services, and help residents maintain communication, independence, and quality of life. You will work independently while remaining connected to a supportive administrative and scheduling team. This position offers the ability to build a stable, full-time career while delivering essential hearing care directly to patients in the long-term care setting. Full state coverage is required, and company support is provided for approved travel-related needs.

The right candidate will be comfortable managing a mobile schedule, communicating professionally with facility teams, and providing compassionate, clinically appropriate care to residents with varying hearing healthcare needs. This is an excellent opportunity for an audiology provider who wants a role with purpose, flexibility in daily workflow, and the ability to serve communities across the state.


What You’ll Do

· Evaluate, diagnose, and support treatment of hearing conditions for residents in long-term care and skilled nursing facilities.

· Conduct otoscopic exams, hearing screenings, diagnostic hearing evaluations, and other clinically appropriate audiology services using mobile equipment.

· Recommend appropriate hearing care plans, follow-up needs, referrals, and communication support based on patient presentation and test findings.

· Dispense, program, adjust, maintain, troubleshoot, and coordinate repair of hearing aids and related assistive devices as applicable.

· Identify changes in patient condition and communicate concerns to appropriate facility staff, families, or care team members as needed.

· Maintain accurate, complete, and timely documentation for each patient encounter.

· Coordinate with the internal scheduling team to support efficient routing, facility visits, and patient care coverage.

· Represent ExcelHealth Group professionally when interacting with residents, families, facility staff, and care partners.

· Stay current with audiology best practices, compliance expectations, licensure requirements, and continuing education standards.


What We’re Looking For

· Doctor of Audiology degree or other state-approved audiology credential required for licensure.

· Valid state license to practice audiology, or ability to obtain required licensure before starting.

· Valid malpractice coverage or ability to obtain coverage.

· Ability and willingness to travel statewide to assigned long-term care and skilled nursing facility locations.

· Experience with hearing evaluations, otoscopy, hearing aid fitting, programming, maintenance, and patient education preferred.

· Strong clinical judgment and comfort working independently in a mobile healthcare environment.

· Excellent communication skills and the ability to collaborate respectfully with patients, facility staff, families, and internal team members.

· Strong organizational skills, including the ability to manage documentation, scheduling expectations, equipment needs, and travel responsibilities.

· Commitment to delivering compassionate, ethical, and high-quality hearing care to long-term care residents.


Benefits and Support

· Full-time employment with consistent patient care opportunities

· Paid time off

· Paid company-recognized holidays

· Health insurance reimbursement

· Malpractice reimbursement

· Continuing education support

· Basic vehicle maintenance support for approved work-related travel

· Company-issued credit card for approved travel expenses

· Relocation assistance available for qualified candidates


Work Environment

This position involves travel to long-term care and skilled nursing facilities throughout the state and requires comfort working in resident care environments. The Audiologist should be prepared to work independently during facility visits while maintaining consistent communication with the administrative, scheduling, and support teams. The role requires professionalism, reliability, proper care of mobile audiology equipment, and a strong commitment to patient-centered hearing healthcare.

title: Quality Associate
description:
Anteris® Technologies is a global structural heart company dedicated to revolutionizing cardiac care. With offices in Minneapolis, MN, US; Geneva, Switzerland; and Brisbane and Perth, Australia, we have a growing and inclusive team.

Our mission is to forge new frontiers in cardiac care by pioneering science-driven and measurable advancements to restore heart valve patients to healthy function. Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR) technologies were originally designed for older, high-risk patients. Today, younger, more active patients need a better solution that will not just open and close but restore healthy heart function. We seek to restore healthy blood flow patterns by creating the world’s first biomimetic TAVR valve, DurAVR® THV. This cutting-edge valve, incorporating our proprietary ADAPT® anti-calcification technology, is designed to mimic the natural function of a healthy heart valve.

The Quality Associate supports the effective operation of Quality Assurance and Quality Control activities at the Malaga site, contributing to the manufacture and release of safe, compliant, and high-quality medical devices.

This individual will perform defined Quality Control activities associated with final product inspection, bioburden reduction, and external sample testing, alongside Quality Assurance activities including batch record review, document control, controlled document and label issuance, and review of GMP records. The Quality Associate also supports the ongoing effectiveness of the Quality Management System through quality investigations, internal auditing and continuous improvement activities.

Working collaboratively with Manufacturing and the broader Quality team, the role ensures Quality activities are completed accurately, efficiently, and in accordance with approved procedures, GMP, and applicable Quality Management System requirements.

Main Responsibilities:
• Perform visual inspection of final product in accordance with approved procedures, specifications and acceptance criteria.
• Perform the bioburden reduction process for final product in accordance with approved procedures, ensuring appropriate handling, identification, traceability and documentation.
• Coordinate preparation and shipment of samples to approved external laboratories for required testing, ensuring appropriate sample identification, documentation, traceability and follow-up.
• Review completed batch manufacturing records for accuracy, completeness, compliance with approved procedures and resolution of identified discrepancies prior to progression through the batch release process.
• Generate, print, issue and control approved batch manufacturing records and product labels for in-process and final product manufacturing activities.
• Support document control activities including issuance, distribution, maintenance, archival and control of Quality Management System documents and records.
• Review GMP records for completeness, accuracy and compliance with applicable procedures and good documentation practices, identifying and escalating discrepancies as required.
• Identify and appropriately document quality issues, non-conformances and deviations and support their investigation and resolution in accordance with the Quality Management System.
• Participate in CAPA investigations, including gathering and evaluating information, supporting root-cause analysis, identifying appropriate corrective and preventive actions and documenting investigation outcomes.
• Train and qualify as an internal auditor and conduct internal audits in accordance with the approved audit program, documenting observations and supporting follow-up of identified actions.
• Support internal and external audits by preparing documentation, providing records and information and assisting with audit activities as required.
• Work collaboratively with Quality, Manufacturing and other functions to resolve quality and documentation issues and support site operational requirements.
• Identify and contribute to opportunities to improve Quality processes, documentation, compliance and efficiency.

Skills, Knowledge, Experience & Qualifications
• Relevant qualification in Science, Laboratory Techniques, Quality, Medical Device Manufacturing or a related discipline, and/or relevant experience within a medical device, pharmaceutical or other regulated manufacturing environment.
• Working knowledge of GMP, good documentation practices and Quality Management System requirements, with an understanding of the importance of traceability, document control and accurate quality records.
• Demonstrated ability to accurately perform and document Quality Control inspection and processing activities and review manufacturing and GMP records against approved requirements.
• Strong attention to detail, analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify discrepancies, gather and evaluate information and contribute to quality investigations and root cause analysis.
• Strong organisational and document-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple Quality activities and maintain accurate controlled records.
• Sound communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to communicate quality concerns constructively, participate in audits and work effectively across Quality, Manufacturing and other functions.
• Proficient computer skills and the ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.

title: Plant Operator Trainee
description:
Salary Range: $19.00/hour - $26.92/Hour Salary Grade: 8 FLSA: Nonexempt

Purpose of Classification:

The purpose of this classification is to operate water and wastewater treatment facilities in compliance with federal, State and Local regulations for the operation of water treatment, distribution, storage facilities and/or wastewater collection, lift stations or treatment facilities.

This classification is safety sensitive, subject to random drug testing in accordance with the County’s Drug & Alcohol Policy.

Essential Functions:

The following duties are normal for this position. The omission of specific statements of the duties does not exclude them from the classification if the work is similar, related, or a logical assignment for this classification. Other duties may be required and assigned.

Performs all aspects of operation, sampling, monitoring, and testing required to maintain compliance with federal, State and Local regulations that govern water treatment and wastewater operations; performs laboratory analysis; and physically checks equipment to ensure correct operation feed, dosages, and calibrations necessary to properly operate facilities and systems.

Assists in the performance of regular and unscheduled repairs and maintenance on plant equipment and machinery; conducts weekly checks of the treatment plant; rotates equipment; changes and connects chlorine and other specialized water treatment plant equipment; monitors chemical feed equipment, operates solids processing equipment; and operates load lugging trucks.

Collects potable water and wastewater samples and performs laboratory analysis such as pH, turbidity, chlorine levels, fluoride levels, dissolved oxygen levels, and total suspended solids, total volatile solids, and temperature on grab samples; and calibrates lab equipment and instruments.

Monitors the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition systems for any changes that may impact the plant processes such as pressure changes, chemical pumps faulting out, distribution storage tank levels, chemical tank levels, turbidity levels, and filter function.

Prepares reports and records testing results; completes forms and various paperwork; enters data into the computer; and receives telephone calls and responds to customer complaints.

Maintains a safe and clean work environment (both inside the facilities and on the grounds) per OSHA and DeKalb County standards.

Participates in continuing education classes and testing to qualify for the Georgia and DeKalb County certification and licensure requirements.

Minimum Qualifications:

High school diploma or GED required; previous experience in a water or wastewater utility or coursework in Biology, Chemistry, Engineering, or a related field is preferred; or any equivalent combination of education, training, and experience which provides the requisite knowledge, skills, and abilities for this job will be considered.

Specific License or Certification Required: Must possess and maintain a valid Georgia driver’s license; must obtain a Georgia Class III Water or Wastewater Operator License within one year of hire.

title: Strategic Finance Manger, AI & Forecasting
description:
Location: Palo Alto, CA (hybrid)

Small business owners don't have a risk department. They spend their time and energy starting and growing a business. NEXT's mission is to help entrepreneurs thrive, and we're using AI to make business insurance simple, fast, and affordable enough that it never costs them a day of work.

We're an AI technology company that happens to also be a fully licensed insurance carrier. Because we're a full-stack carrier, AI isn't a layer bolted onto someone else's product. It's in the underwriting, the pricing, the classification, and increasingly in how the product itself gets built. We're rebuilding the core judgment loops of a hundreds-of-years old industry, and doing it with a lean team, which is exactly why AI matters.

We underwrite our own risk, build our own systems, and own the entire value chain, so the product decisions made here show up directly in what a customer pays and how fast they get covered. Since 2016 we've insured hundreds of thousands of small businesses across the country. As a subsidiary of Munich Re and ERGO, our growth is backed by the financial strength of one of the world's leading reinsurance and insurance groups.

About the role:

ERGO NEXT is building its Finance organization to be AI-native — starting with reinventing how we forecast the business from the ground up. We're looking for a Strategic Finance Manager, AI & Forecasting to help lead this transformation: someone with strong core strategic finance fundamentals who is equally excited to redesign forecasting, planning, and reporting workflows around AI/LLM-based tools rather than layering AI on top of legacy spreadsheet processes. Reporting to the Head of Revenue & Growth FP&A, this is a high-visibility, high-impact role at the intersection of strategic finance and applied AI, with the mandate to define what "AI-native FP&A" looks like at ERGO NEXT.

What You’ll Do:

  • Lead the redesign of the topline revenue forecasting process from the ground up, using AI/LLM-based tools and workflows in place of legacy manual, spreadsheet-driven approaches
  • Partner with Finance and Data Science to identify, evaluate, and implement AI tools and agentic workflows that improve the speed, accuracy, and scalability of forecasting and planning
  • Drive long-range and annual planning process while building repeatable, AI-assisted modeling and reporting frameworks
  • Spearhead strategic finance activities applying AI-driven analysis to accelerate diligence and scenario modeling
  • Partner cross-functionally to define and automate KPI tracking, using AI to surface insights and recommendations faster than traditional analysis allows
  • Prepare Board materials and executive presentations, incorporating AI-generated analysis and scenario modeling to sharpen the narrative
  • Act as an internal champion and educator for AI adoption within Finance, documenting playbooks and mentoring team members as new tools and workflows are rolled out

What We Need:

  • BA/BS in finance, accounting, economics, or a quantitative discipline
  • 4–6 years of finance experience in a fast-paced environment with a track record of success (background in investment banking, corporate development, or strategic finance a plus)
  • Genuine enthusiasm for AI tools (e.g., LLM-based agents, AI-powered modeling/analysis platforms) and a track record of adopting or building workflows around them — prior hands-on use of tools like Claude, ChatGPT, or similar in a finance/analytics context strongly preferred
  • Ability to break down and solve complex, ambiguous problems with strong business acumen and data-driven techniques, including comfort redesigning a process rather than just operating an existing one
  • Basic technical fluency (e.g., SQL, Python, or low-code/AI tooling) sufficient to prototype or evaluate AI-driven finance workflows a plus, though not required
  • Excellent attention to detail and organizational skills, with the ability to manage competing and shifting priorities in a fast-paced environment
  • High degree of reliability and integrity, with sound judgment operating in a newly-defined, ambiguous role
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to bring both technical and non-technical stakeholders along on a change-management journey

We have become aware that there may be fraudulent recruiting attempts being made by people posing as representatives of ERGO NEXT Insurance. These scams may involve fake job postings, unsolicited emails, or messages claiming to be from our recruiters or hiring managers.

title: Reimbursement Coding & Strategy Director
description:
The Reimbursement Coding and Strategy Director leads the development and execution of U.S. coding strategies for new and existing in vitro diagnostic products. The role assesses coding pathways and gaps, defines evidence and documentation requirements, and integrates coding considerations into product development, launch readiness, and lifecycle planning. Working cross-functionally with Market Access, Medical Affairs, Regulatory Affairs, HEOR, Marketing, Government Affairs, and global teams. Alongside working with VP Market Access North America, this position translates complex coding requirements into clear recommendations, implementation plans, and customer-facing resources. The role serves as the organization’s subject-matter expert for diagnostic coding strategy and monitors changes that may affect product access, reimbursement, and commercial execution.

Position Duties

Coding Strategy and Pathway Development

  1. Lead the development of U.S. coding strategies for pipeline, launch, and on-market diagnostic products.
  2. Assess available coding pathways, including CPT, PLA, HCPCS, and ICD-10 considerations, and recommend the pathway that best supports the intended use, site of service, and reimbursement objective.
  3. Identify coding gaps, risks, dependencies, and decision points early in product development and translate findings into actionable recommendations for governance and product teams.
  4. Develop long-range coding roadmaps, including key milestones, evidence needs, submission timing, ownership, and contingency approaches.
  5. Evaluate when existing codes may be appropriate and when a new or revised code may be needed, documenting the rationale, business impact, and implementation considerations.
  6. Adjust coding strategies for existing products in response to product changes, utilization patterns, coding updates, or reimbursement barriers.

Coding Applications, Evidence, and Documentation

  1. Lead or coordinate the preparation of coding applications, supporting narratives, technical documentation, and evidence packages in partnership with Government Affairs, Medical Affairs, Regulatory Affairs, HEOR, and other subject-matter experts.
  2. Define the clinical, technical, utilization, and economic evidence needed to support coding objectives and incorporate those requirements into evidence-generation plans.
  3. Ensure coding submissions and supporting materials accurately reflect product characteristics, intended use, clinical utility, and the applicable diagnostic pathway.
  4. Maintain a centralized record of coding decisions, assumptions, submission history, status, risks, and outcomes to support continuity and organizational learning.
  5. Coordinate internal review and approval of coding materials in accordance with company requirements and applicable standards.
  6. Represents and attends the following: AMA, ADLM, ACLA, CAP, AMP

Product Development and Launch Integration

  1. Represent Market Access and coding strategy in U.S. go-to-market, pipeline, and lifecycle governance processes.
  2. Integrate coding considerations into product profiles, evidence plans, launch sequencing, pricing and reimbursement planning, and commercial readiness activities.
  3. Provide U.S. coding insights to global teams and adapt global market access tools to address U.S. coding requirements.
  4. Partner with brand and commercial teams to develop coding-related launch plans, customer resources, internal training, and objection-handling tools.
  5. Assess the operational implications of coding decisions for laboratories, providers, revenue cycle teams, sales teams, and customer support functions.

Coding Intelligence, Governance, and Enablement

  1. Monitor coding publications, code-set updates, application cycles, and industry developments that may affect pipeline or on-market products.
  2. Analyze potential business and access impact, communicate findings to relevant stakeholders, and recommend response plans.
  3. Establish coding governance tools, decision frameworks, standard operating practices, and performance measures to improve consistency and execution.
  4. Develop and maintain approved coding guides, reimbursement resources, training materials, and internal reference tools.
  5. Serve as an internal expert and educator on diagnostic coding concepts, pathways, limitations, and appropriate use of coding information.
  6. Collect field and customer insights related to coding barriers and use those insights to refine product-level strategies and close access gaps.
  7. Perform all work in compliance with company quality procedures and standards.
  8. Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Education and Training

title: Psychologist, Road to Recovery Aftercare
description:
Salary

The salary range for this position is CAD $56.02/Hr. - CAD $69.98/Hr.

Job Accuracy Posting Flag

The hours of work, including start and stop times, days off, work area and work site may be subject to change consistent with operations requirements and applicable provisions of the Collective Agreement and statutes. **Testing may be required. ***A criminal record check may be required

Summary

Recovery doesn’t end when treatment does. Come be part of a team helping people build what comes next.

Road to Recovery is now hiring a temporary part-time 0.6 FTE Psychologist to join their Aftercare team. Working with clients who have completed treatment and are transitioning back into community, you’ll provide ongoing psychological assessment and counselling as part of a wraparound, recovery-oriented model that recognizes that recovery is rarely linear. You’ll work alongside an interdisciplinary team to help clients navigate the challenges that can come after treatment, strengthen the skills and supports that sustain recovery, and reconnect with care when setbacks or changing needs arise. This is an opportunity to build on a strong foundation created by the team's incumbent Psychologist while continuing to grow the psychological services offered through Aftercare, including individual and group programming.

This position is currently scheduled to end January 31st 2028, or the return of incumbent.

What is R2R?

The R2R initiative strives to better address treatment of substance use issues by providing the right support to each client at the right time. People who use substances deserve the same access to evidence-based care as anyone else, free from stigma. As with all of our services at PHC, R2R delivers care in a way that strives to be person-centred, trauma-informed and culturally safe. Launched in 2023, the R2R supports clients at every phase of their wellness and recovery journey by coordinating seamless care, even if there are setbacks or relapses along the way.

The R2R continuum of services in operation today includes 25 detox beds located at St. Paul's Hospital, 20 transitional care beds for clients awaiting space in a treatment program or long-term housing, and the Aftercare Team, which launched in Fall 2024, providing outreach aftercare in the community. The initiative is rolling out in steps, with additional treatment services to come soon, including a ~50 bed off-site treatment center.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Provide ongoing psychological assessment and counselling: Complete psychological assessments, develop individualized treatment approaches, and provide evidence-based individual and group psychotherapy to support clients as they transition from treatment into community living.
  • Support recovery in the community: Work with clients on the challenges that emerge post-treatment, helping strengthen coping strategies, mental health, relationships and other factors that support sustained recovery and wellbeing.
  • Coordinate care across the continuum: Collaborate with the Aftercare team and other health and community partners, participate in case planning and interdisciplinary meetings, and support continuity of care as clients navigate changing needs, including setbacks or relapse.
  • Help grow psychological services: Contribute to the ongoing development of Aftercare through group programming, program planning and evaluation, education, research, and improvements to psychological care and service delivery.

What You Bring

Education, Training and Experience

  • Ph.D. or Psy.D. in Clinical Psychology from an accredited University plus one year of supervised internship.
  • One year’s recent related experience with patient/client population or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience.
  • Current full registration as a Psychologist with the College of Health and Care Professionals of BC (CHCPBC) or eligible to obtain registration within twelve (12) months of employment.

Skills and Abilities

  • Knowledge of therapeutic, diagnostic and consultation techniques.
  • Knowledge of psychology assessment and treatment methods and tools.
  • Knowledge of evidence based psychological practice.
  • Ability to function as a team member, leader and facilitator.
  • Ability to communicate with and deal effectively with co-workers, clients and their families, both one-on-one and in groups.
  • Ability to work independently and in collaboration with others.
  • Ability to teach and provide clinical supervision.
  • Ability to establish workload priorities in collaboration with others.
  • Physical ability to perform the duties of the position.
  • Ability to operate related equipment including personal computer and related word processing, digital medical chart software, telehealth and spreadsheet software.

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary: $56.02 - $69.98 CAD per hour, depending on experience
  • Growth opportunities: We welcome individuals at all stages of their career, offering opportunities for professional development and growth.
  • State-of-the-art facilities: The new St. Paul’s Hospital and health campus will be the most innovative approach to the delivery of integrated care in B.C. and Canada, designed to appropriately address the future health needs of patients, families, and our communities. From hospital care to primary and community health solutions, the new St. Paul’s Hospital and health campus will continue to lead innovations in care, research, and teaching. The new St. Paul’s Hospital is expected to open in 2027.
  • Inclusive culture: We respect the diversity, dignity and interdependence of all persons. We value the cultural richness that our diverse workforce brings to the care of our equally diverse population of patients and residents.
  • Meaningful impact: You will have the opportunity to work for an organization that is deeply committed to safeguarding of our surrounding environment by contributing to high quality care while promoting sustainable practices in your everyday work.
  • A comprehensive health benefits package including dental, vision, and life insurance as well as pension.

Who we are:

Providence Health Care is one of the largest faith-based health care organizations in Canada. For the people at Providence, living our Mission, Vision and Values means providing British Columbians with compassionate, socially just, exceptional and innovative care every day.

From our humble roots 129 years ago, Providence Health Care has grown into a globally recognized leader in research, teaching, and care. As individuals within a mission-driven organization, we choose to be part of PHC because we value its long-standing dedication to social justice and compassionate care, its active efforts to advance environmental sustainability and planetary health, and its meaningful engagement in the process of Truth and Reconciliation with Indigenous Peoples.

Curious about working at PHC and the culture of our teams? Check out the videos below to learn more and meet some of the members of the team you'd be joining:

2026 Innovarium Mission Award: Road to Recovery (R2R)

Your Day to Day:

  • In collaboration with program leadership and Professional Practice Leader, plans and organizes the provision of services for specified program areas or patient/client group(s).
  • Completes psychological assessments of referred patients/clients through methods such as reviewing client history, gathering information from the referral source/patient/client/other relevant persons, interviewing patients/clients, conducting or supervising testing and developing/determining most effective methods of treatment to improve patient/client health status.
  • Provides individual and group psychotherapy to patients/clients within the program including developing and implementing didactic and experiential group modules.
  • Participates in activities related to coordinating the inter-disciplinary team as required for the clinic/program psychological service delivery.
  • Functions as a primary Psychology contact for treatment teams, individuals or persons serving identified patient/client groups.
  • Makes recommendations for program planning and/or evaluation and the revision of criteria and procedures for referrals, needs assessment and case documentation.
  • Liaises with external agencies in the care of patients/clients throughout the healthcare continuum by methods such as following up with outside agencies including education institutions, health care facilities and related agencies. Organizes treatment plans, participates in case management and attends internal and external interdisciplinary meetings to ensure continuity of care of patients/clients.
  • Attends clinical/case conferences as a member of an interdisciplinary team for patient/client reviews, admissions and discharges. Duties include providing input from a psychology perspective on a variety of care issues related to the patient/client, and program effectiveness to ensure proper and effective treatment of the patient/client.
  • Maintains patient/client records through methods such as documenting participation in the program, most effective treatment, charting patient/client information and psychological findings, preparing progress notes and psychological reports in accordance with established standards, and policies and procedures to meet regulatory requirements and document for future reference.
  • Provides instruction and guidance to colleagues, physicians, hospital personnel and community care providers regarding psychological assessment, treatment modalities, patient care issues, and the performance of clinical interventions. Establishes priorities and provides guidance and clinical advice to ensure program standards are met and safety procedures are followed. Forwards information on unresolved work issues to the program’s manager for action.
  • As required, provides clinical teaching and clinical supervision to residents, post-doctoral fellows and other applicable students as required from a psychological perspective by performing duties such as planning and organizing area assignment, monitoring clinical teaching and skill development, and providing evaluations to appropriate individuals to facilitate a conducive learning environment and professional expertise.
  • Prepares and delivers in-service presentations to department and hospital staff and academic teaching to medical and health care learners/staff as requested.
  • Promotes the services of the department to the public, community and professionals’ groups as requested by the Program Director, Professional Practice Leader or designate and in collaboration with the Clinic/Patient Care Manager (if applicable).
  • Maintains knowledge of current developments in psychology services, by methods such as reviewing literature, consulting with clinical and community experts, evaluating clinical practice and referral systems, and attending professional development activities to meet regulatory requirements of the College, recommend new practices, and contribute to improvement in care.
  • Participates in team research activities through methods such as identifying research questions and participating in collecting relevant data for inclusion in research papers.
  • Attends a variety of meetings and rounds to provide input and/or receive information and participate in decision-making.
  • Performs other related duties as assigned.

We acknowledge that Providence Health Care and the new St. Paul’s Hospital site is located on the traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Coast Salish Peoples, including the territories of the xʷməθkwəy̓əm (Musqueam), Skwxwú7mesh (Squamish), and Səl̓ílwətaʔ/Selilwitulh (Tsleil-Waututh) Nations.

title: Marketplace Data Specialist
description:
Marketplace Data Specialist (Wayfair, eBay, Walmart, Lowe's & Home Depot)


About the Role

We’re looking for a detail-oriented Marketplace Data Specialist to manage and maintain product data and listings across major online marketplaces, including Wayfair, eBay, Walmart, Lowe’s, and Home Depot.

In this role, you’ll ensure product and catalog data is accurate, complete, and aligned with each marketplace’s requirements. You’ll work extensively with large product/data files, marketplace portals, and internal systems to maintain catalog accuracy, resolve listing issues, and support marketplace operations.

This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys detail-heavy work, is highly proficient in Excel, and has hands-on experience working with marketplace portals and large product catalogs.

What You’ll Do

  • Create, upload, and maintain product listings across Wayfair, eBay, Walmart, Lowe’s, and Home Depot marketplace portals

  • Enter and update product data, including titles, descriptions, images, attributes, pricing, and inventory

  • Work with large product catalogs and bulk data files, including CSV and XLSX templates

  • Perform bulk uploads and updates while maintaining a high level of data accuracy

  • Monitor listings for errors, suppressions, policy violations, content issues, or data mismatches and resolve them promptly

  • Ensure product content meets each marketplace’s specific formatting, category, data, and compliance requirements

  • Reconcile inventory, pricing, and order data between internal systems and marketplace platforms

  • Track and troubleshoot listing and catalog issues, including content errors, inventory sync issues, and other marketplace-related problems

  • Coordinate with merchandising, fulfillment, customer service, and other internal teams to keep marketplace data aligned with source systems

  • Generate and maintain reports related to listing status, catalog health, data accuracy, and marketplace performance

  • Stay current on marketplace portal, policy, and data requirement updates

  • Support marketplace data projects and other catalog-related initiatives as needed

What We’re Looking For

  • 2+ years of experience in data entry, e-commerce operations, marketplace operations, or catalog management

  • Direct experience with at least one of the following marketplace/vendor portals is strongly preferred:

    • Lowe’s Vendor Gateway

    • Home Depot Supplier Portal

    • Rithum Order Streaming

    • Wayfair Partner Home

    • Walmart Seller/Supplier Center

    • eBay

  • Candidates without direct experience in the marketplaces above may still be considered if they have strong marketplace, catalog, and product data experience and can learn new platforms quickly

  • Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets is required, including VLOOKUP, pivot tables, data manipulation, and bulk file uploads

  • Demonstrated experience working with large product catalogs and large-scale data projects

  • Excellent attention to detail and a strong commitment to data accuracy

  • Comfortable working with bulk data files, marketplace templates, and platform-specific data requirements

  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple marketplaces, projects, and deadlines simultaneously

  • Clear written communication skills for coordinating with internal teams and marketplace support


Nice to Have

  • Experience with multiple marketplace platforms or vendor portals

  • Experience with Lowe’s Vendor Gateway, Home Depot Supplier Portal, Rithum Order Streaming, or Wayfair Partner Home

  • Experience with PIM or catalog management systems

  • Experience with NetSuite

  • Familiarity with marketplace APIs or EDI processes

  • Basic knowledge of SEO best practices for product listings

  • Experience troubleshooting buy box, content compliance, inventory synchronization, or marketplace data issues

Responsibilities include:

  • Clean grain silos, storage bins, and industrial vessels using specialized equipment.
  • Transfer materials using powerful industrial vacuum systems.
  • Remove compacted materials through scraping, shoveling, and vacuum operations.
  • Operate hand tools, power tools, pressure washers, and industrial equipment.
  • Work safely in confined spaces and elevated work areas.
  • Follow OSHA safety standards and company procedures.
  • Wear and properly maintain required PPE.
  • Inspect equipment and report job progress to supervisors.
  • Work independently and alongside experienced crews.
  • Occasionally assist with emergency response and industrial cleanup projects.

title: Data Engineer
description:
We’re looking for two Data Engineers to join a large-scale customer data environment and help build and improve data products used across the organisation.

This particular role focuses on customer classification and unified customer profiles, combining hands‑on data engineering with data quality, governance and stakeholder management.

You’ll be working closely with Data Engineers, Data Stewards, Product Owners and Software Engineers to build reliable data products, improve engineering standards and help establish better ways of working across the data landscape.

What you’ll be doing

  • Build, improve and maintain data ingestion and transformation pipelines using SQL and Python
  • Work with technologies including BigQuery, dbt and Databricks/PySpark
  • Develop production‑grade data solutions across cloud environments in GCP
  • Improve processes around coding, testing, reviews and infrastructure
  • Help define and implement standards around data quality, data contracts and data engineering
  • Review data models, mappings and data contracts to ensure they meet agreed standards
  • Investigate data quality issues, identify root causes and work with stakeholders to resolve them
  • Support ad‑hoc analytics and data investigations where required
  • Present data quality, governance and data product concepts to technical and business stakeholders
  • Work closely with Product Owners, Software Engineers, Data Stewards and other Data Engineers
  • Help promote data product principles and improve data engineering practices across the organisation

What we’re looking for

  • Strong hands‑on experience with SQL and Python
  • Experience building pipelines using dbt
  • Production experience working with cloud platforms, ideally GCP
  • Hands‑on experience with BigQuery or Databricks/PySpark - (if you have both that would be a huge plus)
  • Understanding of CI/CD, infrastructure‑as‑code and containerisation
  • Experience with data quality - defining rules, writing tests and investigating failures
  • Strong understanding of data models, databases, data warehouses and how data flows between systems
  • Comfortable working with stakeholders and navigating complex or sometimes ambiguous requirements

Nice to have

  • Experience working with customer data, including profiles, purchases and customer interactions
  • Experience with customer classification or unified customer profiles
  • Knowledge of data governance, metadata management and data cataloguing
  • Experience with Data Studio / Looker Studio or Power BI
  • Experience using AI effectively to improve development, testing and review processes

The person

This isn't a role for someone who only wants to write code and work in isolation.

You’ll need to be comfortable asking questions, challenging existing processes, working with different stakeholders and helping shape solutions where everything isn’t already defined.

The environment is evolving, so we’re looking for someone who is proactive, pragmatic and comfortable with ambiguity.

If you’re a strong Data Engineer who enjoys combining hands‑on engineering with data quality, governance and stakeholder interaction, this could be a great assignment.

Details:

Duration: 6 months (will extend for at least another 6 months)

Rate: 80 - 90 per hour / 85K-110K Gross

You also receive 25 days paid leave, significant pension, sick/parental cover, expenses.

title: Director of Supply Chain
description:
Who We Are

Image Solutions designs, sources, manufactures, and distributes custom uniforms for regional and national organizations across a wide range of industries. Our mission is to make our customers, team members, and partners look and feel great at work. We’re known for personalized service, a strong team culture, and giving back, including donating 10% of our annual profits to charity.

The Role

The Director of Supply Chain leads the strategy and execution of our end-to-end supply chain, including planning, inventory, sourcing, procurement, production, product commercialization, and logistics.

As a member of the Leadership Team, you’ll partner across the business to build a supply chain that supports growth, strengthens product availability and service, manages cost and working capital, and reduces operational risk.

This role is a great fit for a leader who can move comfortably between strategy and execution. You use data to make decisions, create clarity and accountability, develop strong teams and supplier partnerships, and build processes that help the organization move faster and operate more effectively.

This is a hybrid position based in Long Beach, CA, with three days per week in the office and periodic international travel, including to Asia and Central America. The role reports to the President.

What You’ll Own

Supply Chain Strategy & Performance: Set the direction for the supply chain and establish the processes, priorities, and performance measures needed to support growth, profitability, customer service, and scalability. Identify risks and opportunities early and translate them into clear action.

Planning & Inventory: Lead demand and supply planning and inventory strategy to improve product availability while managing working capital. Create visibility into inventory health, backorders, supply gaps, purchasing needs, and capacity constraints so the business can make proactive decisions.

Sourcing & Supplier Management: Own domestic and international sourcing, procurement, supplier strategy, and negotiations. Develop a strong supplier network that delivers the right balance of cost, quality, capacity, lead time, reliability, and supply continuity.

Product Development & Commercialization: Lead the Product Development function and ensure new products move effectively from concept through commercialization and production readiness. Provide direction and oversight to the Product Development team, ensuring clear priorities, strong development processes, and accountability for quality, cost, manufacturability, and timelines. Partner with Design, Sales, Account Management, and suppliers to resolve issues and ensure products meet customer and business requirements.

Logistics & Distribution: Set transportation and distribution strategies that balance customer service, speed, and cost. Continuously evaluate freight, routing, consolidation, supplier, and operational decisions for opportunities to improve performance.

Team & Cross-Functional Leadership: Lead and develop the Supply Chain team with clear priorities, ownership, and accountability. Build strong partnerships across Operations, Sales, Account Management, Design, Finance, and other functions to ensure supply chain decisions support broader company goals.

What Success Looks Like

  • Performance is measured against established company and functional OKRs, including key supply chain measures such as OTIF, inventory health, supplier performance, cost, and quality.
  • Customers have the products they need when they need them, with fewer preventable backorders and supply disruptions.
  • Inventory supports customer demand while maintaining appropriate working capital and minimizing excess or obsolete product.
  • Supplier performance improves across cost, quality, lead time, capacity, and reliability.
  • Supply chain risks, constraints, and performance are visible early enough for the organization to take action.
  • New products move from concept to production with clear ownership, strong quality, appropriate cost, and reliable timelines.
  • Logistics and supply chain decisions consistently balance service, speed, cost, and business needs.
  • The Supply Chain team operates with clear priorities, accountability, strong processes, and the capability to support the company's growth.
  • Cross-functional partners have confidence in supply chain data, communication, commitments, and execution.

What You Bring

  • Significant leadership experience across supply chain, planning, procurement, sourcing, or related functions; 10+ years preferred.
  • Broad understanding of apparel and promotional products, including sourcing, procurement, production, demand and supply planning, inventory management, and logistics.
  • Proven experience leading and developing teams and driving accountability across functions.
  • Experience with international sourcing and production, particularly within Asia and/or Central America.
  • Strong supplier relationship management and negotiation experience; apparel, uniforms, or textiles experience strongly preferred.
  • Strong analytical and financial acumen with experience using data to guide inventory, sourcing, cost, and operational decisions.
  • Experience leading or overseeing product development and commercialization, with a strong understanding of the apparel development lifecycle from concept through sampling and production.
  • Experience with ERP, demand-planning, PLM, workflow, or supply chain reporting systems; NetSuite or similar ERP experience preferred.
  • Ability to balance long-term strategy with hands-on leadership in a fast-moving environment.
  • Bachelor's degree preferred, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
  • Ability to travel internationally as needed to support supplier and factory relationships.

What’s In It for You?

  • Competitive base pay and annual bonus opportunity of up to 20% of base salary based on achievement of established goals and objectives
  • Tuition reimbursement
  • Matching 401(k), milestone rewards, and the opportunity to make a meaningful impact at a growing organization that gives back to its community
Pay Range
$185,000—$205,000 USD

title: Specialist, Supplier Quality Engineering, Mechanical
description:
L3Harris is dedicated to recruiting and developing high-performing talent who are passionate about what they do. Our employees are unified in a shared dedication to our customers’ mission and quest for professional growth. L3Harris provides an inclusive, engaging environment designed to empower employees and promote work-life success. L3Harris is the Trusted Disruptor in defense tech. With customers’ mission-critical needs always in mind, our employees deliver end-to-end technology solutions connecting the space, air, land, sea and cyber domains in the interest of national security.

Specialist, Supplier Quality Engineering, Mechanical (L3)
Reference #42366
Waterdown, ON

About The Role

The Supplier Quality Engineering Specialist role is responsible for ensuring that external suppliers consistently deliver products and services to consistently meet Wescam’s supplier quality requirements. This role partners closely with engineering, supply chain, program management, operations and suppliers to drive quality performance, mitigate risk, and ensure product compliance throughout the lifecycle. Lead continuous improvement activities, including the review of supplier capabilities and perform supplier audits to drive measurable improvements against defined quality metrics.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Supplier qualification and management
  • Understanding the requirements, work with Engineering and the Buyer to assess the technical capability and roadmap of the supplier
  • Perform supplier audits for risk and capabilities
  • Identify gaps and opportunities for supplier development using ZDP (zero defect plan) and QIP (quality improvement plan)
  • Determine and assign capable, qualified supplier(s) to parts on Teamcenter and ERP, ensuring alignment with technical requirements, quality standards, and organizational sourcing strategies.
  • Specifications/document/product compliance and alignment
  • Verify compliance to all product specifications, acceptance testing
  • Align product verification/test between supplier and the internal factory
  • Look for and analyze trends for issues
  • Analyze SINs (Supplier Initiated Non Conformances) & NCRs (Non Conformances) to ensure that trends are identified and resolved
  • Ensure link to the shop floor, supply chain, CSG (Customer Service Group) and EFFA (Early Field Failure Analysis)
  • Drive (RCCA) Root Cause Corrective Actions, SCARs (supplier Corrective Action Review) and NCRs to closure
  • Report trends at applicable reviews and execute plans to action
  • Create project plans to close out issues
  • Perform FAI (First Article Inspection) per AS9102 requirements and part inspections at source and at incoming
  • Participate in the Quality Alert, Corrective Action Board & containment processes
  • Responsible for defining and communicating material handling and traceability requirements from the supply chain through to internal storage at Wescam ensuring proper preservation, identification, and handling of all sourced materials.
  • Actively participate in all internal and external technical reviews with cross‑functional teams to ensure specification compliance, design for manufacturability, testability, and cost‑effectiveness of sourced parts and assemblies.
  • Perform supplier process assessments at the source
  • Ensure the suppliers build & test processes are robust and repeatable
  • Ensure that the product can be produced in the most economic, efficient and effective way
  • Utilize techniques such as PFMEA, 8D RCCA , Fishbone, 5 why analysis
  • Perform additional responsibilities related to supplier quality and cross‑functional support as assigned by the Manager to meet departmental and organizational objectives.

Desired Skills And Knowledge

  • Strong critical thinking and analytical skills and ability to analyze supplier or vendor data along with internal metrics.
  • Highly technical mindset and thorough knowledge of technical elements of manufacturing and engineering with the ability to identify process variability, as well as making informed judgement and recommendation within the supply chain.
  • Quality assurance skills with the ability to inspect products and identify gaps in manufacturing processes.
  • Ability to lead projects to improve supplier quality.
  • Continuous improvement mindset
  • Excellent technical communication skills, both written and verbal.
  • Dynamic, resourceful and known for sense of initiative (leadership, innovative, problem solver).
  • Extensive experience with Precision-machined components, Castings, forgings, Mechanical assemblies, and structural components. Proven ability to rapidly acquire a high level of competence in new technical areas.
  • Knowledge of AS9100, AS9102, NADCAP requirements and GD&T per ASME Y14.5 – 2009 (or newer)
  • Lead 8D root cause, project or quality improvement plans, APQP, PPAP
  • Green Belt Certification or equivalent industry lean experience an asset, but not required
  • ASQ CQE or CSQP is an asset
  • P.Eng. designation an asset, but not a requirement
  • Experience with supplier audits
  • Practical knowledge of project management is an asset, but not a requirement
  • Eligibility to obtain CGP clearance
  • Experience in Aerospace, Defense, Automotive or highly regulated manufacturing environments combined with supporting design/manufacturing of mechanical components and/ or assembly.

Education And Experiences

  • Requires proficient knowledge of job area.
  • May have practical knowledge of project management.
  • Bachelor’s Degree and minimum 4 years of prior relevant experience.
  • Graduate Degree and a minimum of 2 years of prior related experience.
  • In lieu of a degree, minimum of 8 years of prior related experience.
  • This posting is for a current vacancy. In the province of Ontario, Canada, the pay range for this position will be $80,000 to $100,000

L3Harris is committed to treating all employees and applicants for employment with respect and dignity and maintaining a workplace that is free from unlawful discrimination. description:
Join Blue Sky Bank's dedicated team as a Commercial Credit Analyst III!


Drive smart lending decisions. Strengthen financial partnerships. Grow your career.


Blue Sky Bank is seeking a detail-oriented and proactive Credit Analyst III to join our team in Dallas, Texas. In this role, you will play a critical role in the credit decision-making process by performing comprehensive financial and risk analysis for commercial lending relationships. You'll work independently on complex credit requests, monitor portfolio risk, and assist lenders in maintaining a safe and sound loan portfolio while ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements and bank policy.


Why Blue Sky Bank?

  • Hybrid Work Arrangement - Achieve more with a hybrid work schedule that promotes flexibility, connection, and success.
  • Benefits – Enjoy a comprehensive benefits package that includes a starting accrual of three weeks of paid time off, a 401(k) plan with employer matching, and medical, dental, and vision insurance. Additional benefits include a Health Savings Account (HSA), Flexible Spending Account (FSA), Dependent Care FSA, voluntary accident and critical illness coverage, and 100% employer-paid short-term Disability, long-term disability, and group life/AD&D insurance, as well as optional voluntary life/AD&D coverage.
  • Growth Opportunities – Gain exposure to advanced credit analysis and a diverse loan portfolio.
  • Collaborative Environment – Partner with experienced lenders, credit professionals, and bank leadership in a culture that values teamwork and expertise.
  • Meaningful Influence – Play a critical role in maintaining a safe, sound, and successful loan portfolio.


What You'll Do

  • Perform comprehensive financial and credit analysis for new and existing commercial lending relationships
  • Evaluate borrower financial statements, cash flow, repayment capacity, and overall creditworthiness
  • Assist lenders in structuring credit facilities and identifying appropriate risk mitigation strategies
  • Prepare and maintain detailed, high-quality credit memorandums and underwriting recommendations
  • Monitor commercial loan relationships and identify emerging credit risks
  • Recommend risk rating and grading changes based on ongoing portfolio performance
  • Evaluate collateral, covenant compliance, and financial trends to support ongoing credit monitoring
  • Analyze industry data and market conditions to enhance risk assessments
  • Assess collateral quality and support appropriate loan structures and approval parameters
  • Review and analyze: Accounts Receivable Aging Reports, Borrowing Base Certificates, Rent Rolls, Loan Covenant Compliance, Financial Statements and Cash Flow Analysis, and On-site Collateral Inspections, as needed.
  • Provide meaningful analysis regarding collateral values, inherent risks, and mitigation strategies
  • Partner closely with lenders to facilitate loan approvals, renewals, extensions, and ongoing monitoring
  • Coordinate the timely collection of financial information and clearance of loan exceptions
  • Support efficient credit administration processes and portfolio maintenance efforts
  • Collaborate with departments across the bank to ensure a seamless lending process
  • Ensure compliance with bank policies, regulatory requirements, and fair lending standards
  • Maintain consistency and quality within the credit underwriting process
  • Demonstrate leadership through sound judgment, professionalism, and constructive collaboration
  • Serve as a trusted resource for lenders and internal business partners

title: Toolset Designer

Job Description\:

As a Toolset Designer, you will design, configure and support Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) solutions used across advanced military aircraft programmes. Working primarily with Siemens Teamcenter Enterprise and Unified, you will develop workflows, lifecycles and engineering application solutions, translating business needs into functional designs.   • Collaborate with solution providers and engineering users to ensure PLM functionality integrates effectively across the end-to-end product lifecycle

  • Technical experience across areas such as IT support, software testing and SQL scripting, with the ability to investigate and resolve multi-faceted system issues.
  • Knowledge of ITIL terminology and experience supporting applications or systems throughout the software development and service lifecycle.
  • Analytical approach to translating business and engineering requirements into technical solutions, working with users and wider technical teams to support successful implementation.

You will join a collaborative IT community responsible for the governing, maintenance, and optimisation of the PLM software, applications, and infrastructure aiding developers to build, test, and deploy. The team works closely with delivery, business and technology stakeholders to enable successful change. This role plays a key part in strengthening PLM capability and working cross-functionally with hundreds of end users within the engineering function.

With lifelong learning and meaningful work, this is a place where you can grow your career with certainty and be empowered to be your best. In an environment embracing sustainable ways of working and with a robust sense of shared purpose, our supportive culture is a place you can feel you belong and proud of the difference you make.

We welcome applications from all suitably qualified people, who are BAE Systems employees and have been in their current role for 12 months or longer.

title: Senior SRE Engineer
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior SRE Engineer based in Switzerland.

This is a high-impact SRE role focused on building reliable, scalable infrastructure for an international gaming platform.
You’ll help shape DevOps and SRE practices while contributing to technical strategy and a strong engineering culture.
The role combines hands-on infrastructure engineering with observability, automation, cloud architecture, and incident management.
You’ll work closely with development teams to improve reliability, scalability, deployment processes, and CI/CD practices.
As a senior engineer, you’ll also mentor teammates and promote Kubernetes-native approaches across the engineering organization.
The environment values autonomy, proactive problem-solving, continuous improvement, and practical automation over bureaucracy.
It’s an opportunity to take meaningful ownership of reliability engineering while working with modern cloud-native technologies.

Accountabilities

  • Build and evolve DevOps and SRE practices, helping establish scalable approaches to reliability, infrastructure management, and operational excellence.

  • Contribute to the team’s technical strategy and engineering culture, promoting robust, maintainable, and automation-first practices.

  • Partner closely with development teams to improve system reliability, scalability, CI/CD, and change delivery processes.

  • Mentor engineers and share Kubernetes-native practices, helping raise technical standards across the wider engineering community.

  • Contribute to architectural decisions and cloud infrastructure evolution, balancing performance, reliability, scalability, and operational simplicity.

  • Investigate incidents and technical issues systematically, focusing on root-cause analysis and long-term prevention rather than short-term fixes.

    • Requirements:

    • Deep hands-on expertise with Kubernetes and container orchestration, including operating and scaling production environments.

    • Strong experience with Terraform and Infrastructure as Code, with an emphasis on reproducible and maintainable infrastructure.

    • Proven experience designing and supporting high-availability infrastructure and production systems.

    • Practical experience working with both SQL databases, particularly PostgreSQL, and NoSQL technologies.

    • Strong knowledge of observability stacks, including Prometheus, Grafana, exporters, and alerting systems.

    • Confident scripting and automation skills using Python and Bash.

    • Solid understanding of CI/CD, GitOps, and platform engineering principles and practices.

    • Strong systems thinking, with the ability to identify root causes, anticipate reliability risks, and develop sustainable solutions.

    • A proactive approach to improving processes, automation, infrastructure, and overall reliability engineering practices.

    • Strong communication and collaboration skills, with experience working closely with software engineering teams.

    • Experience with Oracle Cloud is a plus.

    • Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) certification is desirable.

    • Experience with AWS or GCP is beneficial.

    • Ability to read and understand JavaScript/TypeScript or Ruby code is an advantage.

      • Benefits:

      • Fully remote working model, with the option to work from dedicated hubs in Kyiv or Warsaw.

title: (771) Security Task Lead
description:

Physical security & access control oversight

Oversee access control administration support, system audits, and monthly audit log delivery;

Security program reviews, assessments, and corrective actions

Desired Qualifications:

description:

title: Program Mgr - First Mile Ops, Easy Ship, AMZL
description:
Are you passionate about designing the planning engine behind one of Amazon Japan's fastest-growing delivery programs? Do you want to define how packages move from sellers into Amazon's network—turning routing, cost, and capacity decisions into measurable performance for sellers and customers?

Amazon Logistics Japan is seeking a Program Manager to join the EasyShip Operational Planning, Cost Optimization & Enablement team. In this role, you will own First Mile routing methodology, budget planning, and operational playbooks that scale EasyShip across new sellers, categories, and geographies. This is a hands-on role where you'll build plans from the ground up—establishing routing constraints, defining surge standard operating procedures, and transforming recurring issues into standardized processes or system fixes. You'll serve as the First Mile liaison and partner closely with transportation, supply chain, and account management teams to solve complex operational challenges.

At Amazon, you'll work alongside the latest AI and GenAI tools that are increasingly woven into how teams operate: from AI-powered capabilities that accelerate decision-making, to Generative AI that helps you focus on work that truly matters. You'll have opportunities and resources to develop AI fluency at your own pace, with continuous learning built into the culture.

Key job responsibilities
Design and establish First Mile routing methodology and constraints, including surge application standard operating procedures, route quality analysis, and coordination with partner teams to ensure route plans are executed and shared with transportation teams
Manage and prioritize program lifecycles for forecasting, routing, and truck dispatch schedules across peak and business-as-usual periods, proactively coordinating with cross-functional stakeholders to ensure reliable transportation arrangements for sellers
Lead new seller onboarding and operational readiness initiatives, including bag and label distribution, and drive First Mile enablement for category expansion and geographic expansion across domestic and out-of-catchment areas
Partner with stakeholders across the organization to align routing, capacity, and cost plans with execution, converting recurring operational pain points into permanent process improvements or system fixes
Handle operational escalations, configure service area polygons, optimize forecast accuracy, and assign tasks to team members to ensure smooth execution of daily operations

A day in the life
Your day begins with monitoring routing performance and seller readiness metrics. You'll analyze data to identify trends, then collaborate with transportation partners to resolve capacity constraints or adjust routes for upcoming demand changes. Mid-day, you might lead a cross-functional meeting to align on a new category expansion, working through operational readiness requirements and timeline dependencies. You'll spend time building or refining standard operating procedures based on recent escalations, ensuring that lessons learned become embedded processes. Throughout the day, you'll field questions from team members, provide guidance on complex routing scenarios, and maintain clear communication with stakeholders across the EasyShip ecosystem.


About the team
The EasyShip Operational Planning, Cost Optimization & Enablement team is the strategic planning backbone for one of Amazon Japan's most dynamic delivery programs. We're redefining how EasyShip builds, standardizes, and scales First Mile operations to deliver exceptional experiences at scale. Our team works at the intersection of routing science, operational execution, and business strategy—deciding how routes are built, trucks utilized, network costs managed, and new sellers onboarded.

We foster a culture of innovation and continuous improvement, where analytical problem-solving meets hands-on execution. You'll collaborate with transportation specialists, supply chain experts, and seller services teams who are equally committed to operational excellence and customer impact. As EasyShip continues to expand into new categories and geographies, our team is positioned at the forefront of shaping the future of seller logistics in Japan.

title: Senior Electrical Characterisation Engineer
description:
About The Role and Team

Quantum Motion is a fast-growing quantum computing scale-up based in London founded by internationally renowned researchers from UCL and Oxford University with over 40 years’ experience in developing qubits and quantum computing architectures. Bringing together state-of-the-art cryogenic facilities and an outstanding interdisciplinary team, we are developing quantum processors based on industrial-grade silicon chips, with the potential to radically transform computing power in areas such as materials modelling, medicine, artificial intelligence and more.


Our Team


Since 2021 our team has been listed every year in the “Top 100 Startups worth watching” in the EE Times in 2021 and 2022, and our technology breakthroughs have been featured in The Telegraph, BBC and the New Statesman. Our founders are internationally renowned researchers from UCL and Oxford University who have pioneered the development of qubits and quantum computing architectures. Our chairman is the co-founder of Cadence and Synopsys, the two leading companies in the area of Electronic Design Automation. We’re backed by a team of top-tier investors, and we have recently closed our Series C funding of $160 million.

We bring together the brightest quantum engineers, integrated circuit (IC) engineers, quantum computing theoreticians and software engineers to create a unique, world-leading team, working together closely to maximise our combined expertise. Our collaborative and interdisciplinary culture is an ideal fit for anyone who thrives in a cutting-edge research and development environment focused on tackling big challenges and contributing to the development of scalable quantum computers based on silicon technology.

This is a rare and exciting opportunity to be an employee at a scale-up shaping the future of quantum computing. There are vast opportunities for professional growth and to make an impact within the company.

Our team of 100+ is based across London, Oxford, San Sebastián and Sydney, with our primary hub in Islington (London).

We are looking for a Senior Electrical Characterisation Engineer to join our Process Integration team and play a key role in understanding, qualifying and improving the silicon devices at the heart of our quantum processors.

You will sit at a fascinating intersection between semiconductor manufacturing and quantum hardware, working closely with foundries, process engineers and quantum engineers.

You will use electrical characterisation and large-scale data analysis to understand manufacturing variability, identify the root causes of device behaviour, and feed those insights directly back into the semiconductor fabrication process.

This is an opportunity to have a tangible impact on the yield, quality and scalability of quantum processors, working with some of the most advanced silicon technology being developed for quantum computing.


Functions of the Role

  • Drive electrical characterisation of fabricated silicon devices, developing and continuously improving high-throughput screening methods to assess key device parameters including threshold voltage, gate oxide reliability and channel mobility.

  • Turn electrical data into manufacturing insight, identifying patterns, variability and device failures and connecting them back to semiconductor process steps such as photolithography, etching, oxide growth, CMP and doping.

  • Develop automated measurement and test infrastructure, creating robust Python-based test routines and instrument-control workflows across room-temperature and, where appropriate, low-temperature wafer probing environments.

  • Analyse large-scale electrical datasets using statistical process control, yield analysis and other data-driven techniques to monitor wafer uniformity, defect density and process drift.

  • Work directly with semiconductor foundries and process engineers, providing clear, actionable feedback that can be used to improve device performance, consistency and yield.

  • Build scalable characterisation processes, establishing testing standards, calibration procedures, SOPs and data pipelines that allow information to flow effectively between semiconductor process integration and quantum engineering teams.

  • Help shape how we characterise the next generation of our technology, bringing your expertise and ideas to continuously improve our measurement capability as Quantum Motion scales.

  • We are looking for someone who combines strong semiconductor device knowledge with a practical, data-driven approach to electrical characterisation.


Experience - Essentials


  • Master's or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Microelectronics, Semiconductor Physics, Materials Science or a closely related discipline.

  • 3+ years' experience in semiconductor device testing, reliability engineering, electrical characterisation or yield analysis within a foundry, IDM or semiconductor R&D environment.

  • Strong understanding of silicon CMOS fabrication processes, semiconductor device physics and foundry workflows.

  • Hands-on experience with semiconductor parameter analysers, SMUs and wafer probe stations, including DC and/or RF electrical testing.

  • Strong Python skills, particularly for instrument control, automation and automated test execution.

  • A highly analytical approach and the ability to work with large datasets to identify trends, anomalies and root causes.

  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across semiconductor, process, hardware and quantum engineering teams.


Experience - Desirable

It would be particularly valuable if you also have experience in:

  • Quantum device physics, including quantum dots, single-electron transistors (SETs) or charge-stability mapping.

  • Cryogenic electrical characterisation and low-temperature measurement systems.

  • Semiconductor yield improvement, process control or statistical analysis.

  • Automated wafer-level testing and high-throughput characterisation.

  • Working with advanced or emerging semiconductor technologies.


Benefits

  • Be part of a creative, world-leading team

  • Competitive salary and share options scheme

  • Contributory pension scheme

  • Group private medical insurance scheme

  • Life Assurance

  • Cycle-to-work Scheme

  • Central London location


EEO Statement

Quantum Motion is committed to providing equal employment opportunity and does not discriminate based on age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, race, colour, religion, disability status, marital status, pregnancy, gender reassignment or any other protected characteristics covered by the Equality Act 2010.

description:
ABOUT VEG

In 2014, VEG was born with a mission to help people and their pets when they need it most. This meant challenging the status quo and fixing everything that was wrong with the ER experience. Since then, we’ve expanded rapidly, with hospitals nationwide open 24/7, 365 days a year, and created a better emergency experience—not only for people and their pets, but also for everyone who works here—our VEGgies!

At VEG we find a way to say yes to the career you want in veterinary emergency medicine. This means transforming how ER works, from our open-concept hospitals, where you can handle emergency cases of every kind (even exotics!) to our immersive, customer-focused experience, which helps us give people and their pets the care they deserve.

This also means saying yes to creating the greatest experience possible for our VEGgies. Yes to working in an environment where you can find your place and feel valued for the amazing work you do. Yes to having unparalleled opportunities for learning and mentorship so you can grow where you want to go in your career. And yes to making an impact here in ways you never thought possible.

VEG is a 2025 and 2026 certified Great Place to Work®.

THE JOB

You are passionate about helping people and their pets and thrive on creating a welcoming environment, where customers feel cared for from the moment they come through the door. Beyond ensuring every customer's experience is exemplary, you’ll handle day-to-day operations with efficiency and care, maintaining all aspects of the hospital and empowering your team to make a real difference in the lives of pets and their families.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • General hospital maintenance: keeping the reception desk tidy and refreshment center fully stocked, cleaning, laundry, stocking, and inventory
  • General customer assistance and support, including handling phone inquiries and call transfers, ensuring customers and their pets are greeted promptly upon arrival, and managing wait times
  • Ensure that customer/patient information is entered accurately in company software and payments are processed correctly

WHAT YOU NEED

  • Ability to stand for prolonged hours, kneel, and work on the floor as well as ability to lift up to 25 kg on own and able to support up to 40 kg with assistance

  • Availability to work nights, weekends, and holidays on a rotating or as needed basis based on hospital needs
  • Work well in a fast-paced environment with people from all backgrounds and different personality types

WHO YOU ARE

  • Empathetic, instinctively taking a people-centric approach, whether supporting your colleagues or making an effort to understand different perspectives
  • Have a sense of humility; acknowledging mistakes, sharing credit with others, and lifting up your team’s’ accomplishments
  • Feel a strong sense of ownership over your work, taking responsibility for outcomes and staying committed to achieving long-term, impactful results
  • Curious by nature; you ask insightful questions and continuously seek out opportunities to learn and grow your skills and knowledge

HOW WE INVEST IN YOU

  • Competitive compensation, including base and 401K match
  • Comprehensive health and wellness benefits that start on day one, including QPR training and access to free therapy or counseling
  • Based on your role, you may be eligible for equity after one year of full time, active employment with VEG, so you can share in our growth and success
  • A BIG focus on learning and growth, from VEG-created clinical and leadership programs to unlimited ER CE + travel stipend (no really!). Full-time credentialed VEGgies receive a $2,500/year travel stipend. Full-time uncredentialed VEGgies receive a $1,000/year travel stipend.
  • Clinical student loan repayment so you don’t need to worry about your student debt

  • Flexible work schedules to support your life outside of work
