title: SAP HCM/SuccessFactors & FI/CO Consultant
description:
Join the SAP team of a global automotive supplier and become the go-to person for SAP HCM and SuccessFactors – and, over time, for Finance and Controlling too. You’ll keep HR, Finance and Controlling processes running smoothly in SAP, work closely with business users and help shape how the systems evolve.

You don’t need to be an FI/CO expert on day one. Strong SAP HCM / SuccessFactors experience, curiosity and a collaborative attitude matter most – we’ll invest in your growth in FI/CO.

What you’ll do:
  • HR systems – run and improve SAP HCM (PA, OM, Time, payroll integration) and SuccessFactors modules such as Employee Central, Recruiting, Onboarding, Performance & Goals and Compensation.
  • Finance & Controlling – be the local IT contact for SAP FI/CO, coordinating with key users, central IT and external partners on incidents, changes and testing. Deep FI/CO customizing is not expected.
  • Support & change – resolve incidents and requests, turn business needs into specifications, and test and roll out changes through the change process.
  • Integrations – monitor and troubleshoot data flows between SAP, SuccessFactors, payroll providers and other systems (IDocs, APIs).
  • Administration – manage user roles and authorizations (incl. segregation of duties), background jobs and transports, with audit-ready documentation. Complex Basis topics go to central IT and hosting partners.
  • Projects – support S/4HANA rollouts, upgrades and digitalization (testing, migration, cutover).
What you can expect:
  • Real ownership – be the primary SAP HR expert and the local SAP contact for Finance & Controlling.
  • Room to grow – training and development, including a path into SAP FI/CO.
  • International environment – work with global HR, Finance, IT and business teams in a dynamic setting.
  • Interesting projects – S/4HANA transformation and ERP harmonization initiatives.



Requirements

  • 4+ years of SAP experience, including solid hands-on work in SAP HCM and/or SuccessFactors.
  • Good understanding of HR master data and of integrations between SAP HCM and SuccessFactors.
  • Working knowledge of SAP roles and authorizations; basic SAP Basis is enough.
  • Interest in SAP S/4HANA and Finance & Controlling processes, and willingness to learn SAP FI/CO.
  • A proactive, hands-on approach and good communication with business users, vendors and global teams.
  • Fluent Polish and good English; degree in IT, business information systems, HR, finance or a related field.
Nice to have:
  • Employee Central and other SuccessFactors modules.
  • FI/CO user support.
  • S/4HANA project exposure.
  • SAP Integration Suite (CPI).
  • automotive or manufacturing background.
  • SAP certifications.

Benefits

  • Employment based on UoP or B2B.
  • Hybrid work model.
  • Opportunity to broaden your SAP expertise into FI/CO.
  • Participation in strategic SAP transformation projects.
  • Private healthcare & sports card.
  • Training and certification support.

title: Associate Director, Customer Engineering & Delivery
description:

What makes iLink Systems' offerings unique is the fact that we use pre-created frameworks, designed to accelerate software development and implementation of business processes for our clients. iLink has over 60 frameworks (solution accelerators), both industry-specific and horizontal, that can be easily customized and enhanced to meet your current business challenges.



Requirements

People & Organizational Leadership

● Proven, substantial experience managing large client accounts/portfolios, including account P&L ownership, revenue growth, and gross margin optimization.

● Experience handling both Fixed Bid (FB) and Time & Material (T&M) engagement models.

● Work experience with Angular, React, or equivalent modern web/cross-platform frameworks.

● Work experience with .Net or equivalent server side technologies.

● Work experience with both data engineering/analytics concepts and product/application engineering concepts.

● Work experience with cloud platforms (Microsoft Azure and/or AWS) at a solutioning/decision-making level.

● Work experience with agentic AI concepts and frameworks (e.g., Microsoft Agent Framework, LangChain) at a solutioning/decision-making level.

● Excellent presentation and communication skills, including the ability to present data visuals, numbers, and technical architecture clearly to business audiences.

title: Home Depot Lead Generator
location: John C. Cassidy Air Conditioning, Inc.
description:
Home Depot Lead Generator

John C. Cassidy Air Conditioning & Plumbing

Department: Retail / Home Depot Program
Reports To: Home Depot Program Manager
Location: Assigned Home Depot Store


Description


Overview:

John C. Cassidy Air Conditioning & Plumbing is seeking outgoing and motivated Home Depot Lead Generators to represent our company inside local Home Depot stores.


This is a customer-facing, in-store position focused on starting conversations with Home Depot customers and generating qualified leads for our home comfort services. Lead Generators engage shoppers, identify potential HVAC and home-service needs, explain how Cassidy can help, and connect interested customers with our team for the next step.


This is not a technician position and does not require HVAC experience. We are looking for friendly, dependable people who are comfortable approaching customers, building rapport, and working toward individual and team performance goals.

Responsibilities

  • Represent John C. Cassidy Air Conditioning & Plumbing professionally inside an assigned Home Depot location.
  • Proactively engage Home Depot customers in friendly, natural conversations.
  • Identify homeowners who may have a need for air conditioning, heating, indoor air quality, or other applicable home services.
  • Educate customers on available services and help them understand the next steps for receiving additional information or scheduling an appointment.
  • Generate and accurately enter qualified customer leads according to program procedures.
  • Meet established expectations for customer engagement, lead generation, and lead quality.
  • Maintain an active presence within designated areas of the store throughout scheduled shifts.
  • Build positive working relationships with Home Depot associates and store leadership.
  • Maintain knowledge of current Cassidy services, promotions, and program offerings.
  • Participate in training, coaching, and regular performance discussions with the Home Depot Program Manager.
  • Follow all Cassidy and Home Depot policies, procedures, dress standards, and customer-service expectations.
  • Communicate customer feedback, frequently asked questions, and opportunities to improve the program to management.
  • Maintain dependable attendance and arrive prepared for all scheduled shifts.

Qualifications

  • Bi-Lingual (Spanish or Creole) Preferred.
  • Previous experience in retail, customer service, sales, hospitality, promotions, lead generation, or another customer-facing role is preferred.
  • Comfortable proactively approaching and speaking with customers.
  • Friendly, energetic, and professional communication style.
  • Ability to quickly build rapport with different types of customers.
  • Goal-oriented and motivated by achieving measurable results.
  • Dependable with strong attendance and punctuality.
  • Ability to work independently while remaining part of a larger regional team.
  • Comfortable using a tablet, smartphone, or other technology to enter customer information.
  • HVAC or home-services experience is not required; training will be provided.
  • Ability to stand and walk for extended periods during scheduled shifts.
  • Must be available to work a flexible retail schedule, including evenings and weekends, based on store and program needs.

What We're Looking For

The ideal Lead Generator is someone who enjoys talking to people and isn't afraid to start a conversation. You do not need to be an HVAC expert or perform a hard sales close. Your job is to create a positive first impression, recognize potential customer needs, generate quality opportunities, and connect homeowners with the Cassidy team.

What We Offer

  • Competitive hourly pay
  • Performance-based incentive opportunities
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance for eligible employees
  • 401(k)
  • Paid time off for eligible employees
  • Paid training
  • Opportunities for advancement
  • Support and coaching from dedicated program leadership
  • Career opportunities within a growing home-services organization

About John C. Cassidy Air Conditioning & Plumbing

John C. Cassidy Air Conditioning & Plumbing has proudly served South Florida homeowners for decades. Our Home Depot partnership gives customers a convenient way to connect with a trusted local home-services provider while they shop.

John C. Cassidy Air Conditioning & Plumbing is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

title: Senior Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning Engineer
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning Engineer based in United States .

This is a senior, hands-on engineering role focused on designing and delivering production-grade agentic AI systems for enterprise environments. You will build autonomous AI agents using an established enterprise AI stack, combining Glean with OpenAI/GPT Enterprise and cloud infrastructure on AWS or GCP. You will own solutions end to end, from architecture and development through production deployment, monitoring, evaluation, and continuous improvement. The role requires treating AI agents as reliable software systems, with careful attention to retrieval, reasoning, permissions, actions, security, and observability. You will work on technically complex initiatives where reliability, scalability, and maintainability are essential. This is an opportunity to apply advanced LLM and agentic AI expertise to high-impact enterprise use cases while working alongside experienced technology professionals.

Accountabilities

  • Design and develop production-grade agentic AI systems that can reliably support real enterprise users and business workflows.

  • Build autonomous agents using Glean as the agent platform and OpenAI/GPT Enterprise as the reasoning layer, deployed within AWS or GCP environments.

  • Own AI agents throughout their full lifecycle, including architecture, implementation, production deployment, monitoring, evaluation, troubleshooting, and iteration.

  • Design robust agent workflows incorporating triggers, retrieval, multi-step reasoning, tool and function calling, actions, permissions, and memory.

  • Implement retrieval-augmented generation and enterprise search capabilities while ensuring high-quality retrieval and appropriate runtime permission enforcement.

  • Establish evaluation frameworks and measurable quality standards to assess agent performance systematically rather than relying solely on manual inspection.

  • Optimize AI systems for reliability, security, maintainability, cost efficiency, and latency at enterprise scale.

  • Apply strong observability and production engineering practices to identify issues, improve system performance, and support continuous iteration.

    • Requirements:

    • Bring 3+ years of hands-on experience building and operating LLM-powered systems in production environments used by real customers or users.

    • Demonstrate practical experience designing agentic AI workflows, including tool and function calling, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), multi-step orchestration, and memory.

    • Have deep hands-on experience with the OpenAI API and GPT Enterprise, including model selection, prompt engineering, structured outputs, function calling, cost and latency optimization, and enterprise data-handling controls.

    • Demonstrate strong prompt-engineering discipline and an evaluation-first mindset, with experience using measurable evaluations to assess and improve agent quality.

    • Have direct, hands-on production experience with Glean, including Agent Builder, Apps, Actions, Model Hub, connectors, and permission-aware retrieval; this is a mandatory requirement for the role.

    • Possess working knowledge of enterprise search and RAG architectures on Glean, including indexing, connectors, retrieval quality, and runtime permission enforcement.

    • Understand how to approach AI agents as production software, with strong awareness of reliability, security, observability, scalability, and maintainability.

    • Demonstrate strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, combined with the ability to work independently on technically complex AI engineering challenges.

    • Communicate effectively with technical and business stakeholders and collaborate within a global, multidisciplinary engineering environment.

      • Benefits:

      • Work alongside highly skilled technology professionals in a collaborative, friendly, and open-door environment.

      • Contribute to large-scale projects with global impact while expanding your expertise in advanced AI and machine learning technologies.

      • Access tailored learning opportunities, including internal meetups, conferences, workshops, Udemy courses, language training, and company-paid certifications.

      • Explore internal mobility opportunities across diverse domains and projects to build hands-on experience with emerging technologies.

      • Benefit from healthcare coverage, Basic Life Insurance, and short- and long-term disability insurance in accordance with the applicable benefits plans.

      • Work remotely from Canada while contributing to enterprise-scale AI initiatives and innovative technology projects.

title: Mechanisms Technician II, First Shift
description:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known.

Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us.

About the Team:

The Stage Manufacturing team turns design into reality, owning the build of Terran R’s primary structures. This isn’t about turning the same bolt every day; it’s about building the systems to build the rocket. Engineers and technicians work side by side, with deep collaboration and real-time feedback, to shape how we build better and faster. With a manifest and a launch date, it’s up to the team to deliver on Terran R: solving challenges in real time, optimizing for scale, and constantly improving processes. As the vehicle evolves, so will the factory, with opportunities to apply automation, machine learning, and advanced technologies. What we build here sets the blueprint for the future of scaled launch.

This is a first-shift position with a standard schedule of Monday through Friday, 5:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. PT. The role is structured around a 50-hour workweek, including 10 guaranteed overtime hours each week.

About the Role:

  • Collaborate with engineering teams on building the 1st Terran R mechanism assemblies
  • Follow precise work instructions to successfully complete build operations
  • Assemble and test complex electro-mechanical assemblies using a variety of hand tools and test equipment
  • Work closely with a team of technicians to successfully execute daily operations

About You:

  • 2+ years of aerospace mechanical experience or related field
  • Demonstrated ability to work in fast paced environments with flight hardware
  • Proficient in using calibrated tools such as torque wrenches and precision inspection equipment
  • Experience in the building and testing of electro-mechanical systems
  • Experience in wiring, harnessing, and avionics
  • Proficiency of relevant aerospace industry standards and specifications, showcasing strong attention to detail and concern for product quality

Nice to haves but not required:

  • Experience with electrical testing, high and low voltage
  • Experience troubleshooting electrical mechanical assemblies
  • Airframe and Powerplant license

title: Director, Talent Management-HR Talent Development & Learning-Mount Sinai Health System-Hybrid-Full Time-Days
description:
Position Title:

Director, Talent Management-HR Talent Development & Learning-Mount Sinai Health System-Hybrid-Full Time-Days

Position Summary:

The Director, Talent Management, provides strategic leadership for Mount Sinai Health System's enterprise performance management program and the development of related talent management practices. The Director establishes program direction, governance, standards, and the long-term roadmap for goal setting, performance reviews, continuous feedback, talent discussions, and development planning.

Working closely with Human Resources, Digital and Technology Partners, operational leaders, and other enterprise stakeholders, the Director ensures that performance and talent practices are practical, consistent, equitable, and aligned with organizational priorities. The Director oversees leader enablement, communications, change management, program evaluation, and the team responsible for implementing and continuously improving these practices.

The Director partners with the leaders and functions accountable for succession planning, leadership development, employee engagement, employee relations, HR technology, and workforce analytics to strengthen connections across the broader talent ecosystem without assuming ownership of those portfolios.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Establishes and advances the strategy, governance, standards, and multiyear roadmap for enterprise performance management and related talent management practices.
  • Leads the design and continuous evolution of performance management practices, including goal setting, performance reviews, calibration, continuous feedback, talent discussions, and development planning.
  • Translates organizational priorities and leadership expectations into practical performance and talent management approaches that can be implemented consistently across a large and complex health system.
  • Provides strategic direction and oversight for annual performance management cycles, leader enablement, communications, change management, and program implementation.
  • Chairs or supports appropriate governance and decision-making forums, clarifying roles, decision rights, standards, escalation paths, and accountability for program success.
  • Advises HR and operational leaders on performance and talent management strategy, program design, adoption, and effectiveness, while referring individual employee relations matters to the appropriate HR function.
  • Builds alignment among HR partners, DTP, People Analytics, Talent Development and Learning, operational leaders, and other stakeholders whose work affects or is affected by performance and talent practices.
  • Partners with succession planning, leadership development, employee experience, and other talent functions to create appropriate connections while respecting established ownership and accountability.
  • Defines program outcomes and measures of success and partners with HRIS and People Analytics to establish data, reporting, dashboard, and evaluation requirements.
  • Uses program data, stakeholder feedback, workforce insights, and external practices to identify risks, recommend priorities, and guide program improvements.
  • Oversees relevant vendor relationships, budgets, resources, and technology requirements in partnership with procurement, finance, DTP, HRIS, and other accountable functions.
  • Leads, develops, and evaluates the talent management team, ensuring clear priorities, strong execution, effective collaboration, and continuous capability development.

Supervisory Responsibilities

  • Directly supervises the talent management team and may oversee vendors, consultants, and cross-functional project teams

Education Requirements:

Bachelors degree required. Masters degree preferred in Organizational Development, Industrial Organizational Psychology, Human Resources, Business Administration, Education, or a related field.

Experience Requirements:

Eight or more years of progressive experience in performance management, talent management, organizational development, human resources, or a closely related discipline, including experience leading enterprise performance management or comparable large-scale talent programs. Prior people leadership and experience working in a complex, matrixed organization are required. Healthcare experience is preferred.

General Skills and Competencies:

  • Deep expertise in enterprise performance management and strong knowledge of related talent management practices.
  • Demonstrated ability to design governance, standards, programs, and implementation roadmaps for a large, complex organization.
  • Strong strategic judgment and the ability to balance ambition, operational feasibility, stakeholder needs, and organizational readiness.
  • Excellent executive communication, consultation, presentation, facilitation, and influence skills.
  • Ability to build alignment and lead through influence across HR, technology, analytics, operations, and other stakeholder groups.
  • Strong change and program leadership capabilities, including experience guiding enterprise adoption and continuous improvement.
  • Ability to interpret workforce and program data, identify implications, and translate findings into decisions and recommendations.
  • Strong people leadership skills, including setting direction, developing talent, managing performance, and building an accountable and collaborative team.

The Mount Sinai Health System (MSHS) provides salary ranges that comply with the New York City Law on Salary Transparency in Job Advertisements. The salary range for the role is $140,000.00 - $230,000.00 Annually. Actual salaries depend on a variety of factors, including experience, education, and operational need. The salary range or contractual rate listed does not include bonuses/incentive, differential pay or other forms of compensation or benefits.

title: Test Technician II
description:

The Electrical Field Test Technician is responsible for the safe and efficient installation and testing of electrical power distribution equipment for customers in the assigned territory. In this role, you will travel approximately 25% of the time, working both independently and with a crew, and handle the performance and management of routine, moderately complex, and complex tasks and projects, record-keeping, evaluation of test data, and preparation of field service reports.

Position Summary

Pay: $45.00-$50.00. The pay listed is the base hourly rate + plus available paid overtime.

The pay listed is the salary range for this position. A specific offer will vary based on applicant’s experience, skills, abilities, geographic location, and alignment with market data.

title: Senior Program Manager, Missile Warning & Tracking
description:
About the role

Muon Space seeks a Senior Program Manager to lead delivery of next-generation satellites for national security missions, including missile warning and tracking. This is a high-visibility, high-impact role at the intersection of payload engineering and rapid-cycle space vehicle development.

The Senior PM is the accountable owner for delivering the program on cost, schedule, and technical performance. You will manage a multi-disciplinary internal team, subcontractors, and a critical-path vendor base for EO/IR payloads, algorithm development, avionics, and space vehicle builds. The role spans the full program lifecycle: design reviews, hardware build, integration and environmental test, launch, and on-orbit operations.

This position is hybrid and requires working on-site in our San Jose, CA office three days per week.

Responsibilities

  • Program Execution
    • Own the integrated master schedule, cost baseline, and risk register
    • Drive the program through preliminary and critical design reviews, payload and spacecraft integration, environmental test, launch, and on-orbit demonstration, meeting customer milestones and contract deliverables
    • Manage scope, cost, and period of performance against contract milestones and payment events
    • Lead day-to-day execution of the program team to the contract, running the weekly program cadence, internal design reviews, and readiness reviews; provide status and briefing content to the Mission Manager, who is the customer interface
    • Own the preparation and quality of contract deliverables, including status reports, design review packages, technical and cost data, test plans, and final reports, for delivery to the customer
    • Partner with the Mission Manager and Muon's Capture and Business Development teams on follow-on strategy
  • Subcontractor and Vendor Management
    • Manage program subcontracts, including mission data processing and algorithm development
    • Coordinate critical-path vendors for detectors, focal plane arrays, cooler assemblies, and optics across long-lead procurements
    • Keep subcontract scope, cost, and schedule aligned with prime contract commitments
  • Technical Leadership and Risk Management
    • Partner closely with the lead systems engineer and technical leads (payload design, AI&T, optics, electronics, software, mechanisms, thermal, mission systems) to drive technical decisions
    • Own and actively work the program risk register, including supply chain, integration, launch, and demonstration risks
    • Resolve cross-functional issues quickly and escalate to functional and program leadership when needed
  • Compliance and Reporting
    • Ensure program execution complies with contract requirements, including U.S.-only performance, ITAR/EAR export controls, technical data rights, security requirements, and CUI handling
    • Coordinate with Contracts and Finance on subcontract changes, invoicing, and program financial reporting

Required Qualifications

  • 8+ years of professional experience in program or technical management of complex technical system development, deployment, and operations
  • 5+ years of hands-on technical experience, preferably in an engineering or similar capacity, or direct ownership of a hardware development effort through design reviews to a tested product
  • Direct experience with space, defense, or aerospace program planning and execution
  • Demonstrated experience managing programs with multiple subcontractors and a complex critical-path supply chain
  • Experience executing rapid-acquisition or prototype agreements for government customers, with familiarity navigating the government program lifecycle, technical data rights, and contract deliverables
  • Active Secret U.S. security clearance
  • U.S. citizenship required (Clearance required and program is ITAR-restricted)
  • Excellent written communication skills; you will author or approve the program's contract deliverables

Preferred Qualifications

  • Active Top Secret or TS/SCI clearance
  • Prior experience on a missile warning, missile tracking, missile defense, or similar space-based infrared program
  • Working knowledge of EO/IR sensor architectures, focal plane arrays, and cryocooler integration
  • Working knowledge of missile warning data products and techniques for detection and tracking
  • Experience managing programs through environmental test campaigns (TVAC, vibration, EMI/EMC)
  • Experience with launch integration and early on-orbit operations

Salary

The salary range for this role is $206,000 - $232,000, plus a competitive equity grant and comprehensive benefits package. Final compensation will be determined based on skills, qualifications, experience, and geographic location as assessed during the interview process.

About Muon Space

Founded in 2021, Muon Space is an end-to-end Space Systems Provider that designs, builds, and operates LEO satellite constellations delivering mission-critical data. Our revolutionary, integrated technology stack enables customers to optimize every dimension of their missions for faster time-to-orbit and superior constellation remote sensing performance. Our state-of-the-art facility in the heart of Silicon Valley is optimized for manufacturing spacecraft and rapid, flexible payload integration at scale. From climate monitoring to national security, Muon Space is dedicated to delivering Earth Intelligence for a safer and more resilient world.

Taking Care of Our Team

At Muon salary is only part of our total compensation package. In addition to salary, full-time employees receive equity compensation as well as benefits including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401k retirement plan, short & long term disability and life insurance. We also offer three weeks paid vacation for new employees, along with 12 paid holidays, unlimited sick time and paid parental leave.

Our mission embraces the entire planet and we believe our team should too. Muon is dedicated to creating a diverse and dynamic company and workforce. We believe in equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, age, national origin, citizenship, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, or gender identity. We value diversity in the workplace, and that starts with our applicants. We encourage you to apply, even if you don't check all the boxes, and we look forward to reviewing your application! In addition, if you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know.

Muon is currently registered and able to hire in the following states:
AL, AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, FL, GA, IL, IA, ID, MD, MA, MI, MN, MO, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OR, PA, TN, TX, VT, VA, WA

ITAR/EAR Requirements

This position requires access to export controlled information. To conform to U.S. Government export regulations applicable to that information, applicant must either be (A) a U.S. person, defined as a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (green card holder), (iii) refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, (B) eligible to access the export controlled information without a required export authorization, or (C) eligible and reasonably likely to obtain the required export authorization from the applicable U.S. government agency. The Company may, for legitimate business reasons, decline to pursue any export licensing process.

title: Product Manager, Inventory & Listing Experience
description:
Who we are

At CarGurus (NASDAQ: CARG), our mission is to give people the power to reach their destination. We started as a small team of developers determined to bring trust and transparency to car shopping. Since then, our history of innovation and go-to-market acceleration has driven industry-leading growth. In fact, we’re the largest and fastest-growing automotive marketplace, and we’ve been profitable for over 15 years.

What we do

The market is evolving, and we are too, moving the entire automotive journey online and guiding our customers through every step. That includes everything from the sale of an old car to the financing, purchase, and delivery of a new one. Today, tens of millions of consumers visit CarGurus.com each month, and ~30,000 dealerships use our products. But they're not the only ones who love CarGurus—our employees do, too. We have a people-first culture that fosters kindness, collaboration, and innovation, and empowers our Gurus with tools to fuel their career growth. Disrupting a trillion-dollar industry requires fresh and diverse perspectives. Come join us for the ride!

Role overview

CarGurus is seeking a customer-obsessed, data-driven Product Manager to join our growing Dealer Product team.

Once a dealer acquires a vehicle, a critical set of work is required to get it retail-ready: creating accurate listings, merchandising the vehicle with compelling content, and distributing inventory across the marketplaces and channels where dealers advertise. In this role, you will own the product strategy and experience that empowers auto dealers to optimally move inventory seamlessly from vehicle acquired to retail-ready and advertised.

You will work closely with dealers and cross-functional partners in Engineering, Design, Analytics, Data Science, and Go-To-Market (GTM). Because the inventory managed through our dealer tools directly powers the shopping experience on CarGurus, you will also collaborate closely with Consumer Product teams to ensure dealer workflows result in complete, accurate, and high-quality listings for shoppers.

We are looking for a PM who excels at navigating ambiguity, turning complex operational workflows into intuitive product experiences, and shaping the future of inventory management at CarGurus.

Are you ready for the ride?

What you'll do

  • Strategy & Roadmap: Own the strategy and roadmap for dealer merchandising and syndication, establishing clear priorities from initial listing creation through distribution across CarGurus and third-party channels.
  • Customer Insights & Discovery: Spend time with auto dealers to deeply understand their workflows, pain points, and unmet needs. Translate these qualitative insights and behavioral data into clear user problems, product requirements, and iterative delivery plans.
  • Listing & Workflow Excellence: Define what constitutes a complete,correct, and optimal listing (photos, options, condition, trim, descriptions) and build experiences that transform raw vehicle records into high-quality, publish-ready listings without redundant data entry.
  • Consumer Experience Alignment: Partner closely with Consumer Product teams to ensure dealer-created inventory translates into accurate, compelling listings that drive shopper engagement on CarGurus.
  • Ecosystem & Platform Growth: Evaluate build, buy, partner, and integration opportunities across merchandising, syndication, and the broader inventory management ecosystem.
  • Cross-Functional Execution: Lead end-to-end product development—from discovery and design through launch, measurement, and optimization—in tight alignment with Engineering, Design, Analytics, and Data Science.
  • Data & Syndication Quality: Partner with technical teams to build reliable listing data, quality signals, destination-level monitoring, and performance insights that maximize distribution reliability.
  • AI & Automation Innovation: Identify and evaluate high-impact opportunities to integrate artificial intelligence, machine learning, and automated capabilities to streamline dealer operations, deliver data-driven intelligence, and elevate the quality, speed, and effectiveness of inventory merchandising and distribution.
  • GTM & Adoption: Collaborate with Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success to support successful launches, drive dealer adoption, and gather ongoing operational feedback.
  • Measurement & Iteration: Define success metrics, monitor usage and listing performance, and use quantitative data alongside dealer feedback to evaluate releases and guide future investments.

What you'll bring

  • 4+ years of product management experience, ideally building B2B SaaS, workflow, marketplace, or inventory-related products. Proven track record of owning product areas from problem definition through launch and iteration.
  • Experience with automotive retail, dealer inventory management, vehicle merchandising, content management, or marketplace syndication is a strong plus.
  • Experience or comfort working with APIs, third-party integrations, white label partnerships, data feeds, workflow orchestration, or technology partners.
  • Strong quantitative skills with the ability to define success metrics, interpret product usage data, and connect feature delivery to measurable business outcomes.
  • Ability to navigate ambiguity, turn complex operational problems into clear roadmaps, and make thoughtful tradeoffs across customer value, technical complexity, and speed.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with strong customer empathy, stakeholder management, and the ability to build alignment across interconnected B2B and Consumer product teams.
  • Practical experience utilizing Generative AI to streamline workflows and/or rapidly develop prototypes with tools such as Claude Code (preferred).

The displayed range represents the expected annual base salary / On-Target Earnings (OTE) for this position. On-Target Earnings (OTE) is inclusive of base salary and on-target commission earnings, which applies exclusively to sales roles.

Individual pay within this range is determined by work location and other factors such as job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

This annual base salary forms part of a comprehensive Total Rewards Package. In addition to benefits, this role may qualify for discretionary bonuses/incentives and Restricted Stock Units (RSUs).

Position Pay Range
$123,000—$154,000 USD


Working at CarGurus

We reward our Gurus’ curiosity and passion with best-in-class benefits and compensation, including equity for all employees, both when they start and as they continue to grow with us. Our career development and corporate giving programs, as well as our employee resource groups (ERGs) and communities, help people build connections while making an impact in personally meaningful ways. A flexible hybrid model and robust time off policies encourage work-life balance and individual well-being. Thoughtful perks like daily free lunch, a new car discount, meditation and fitness apps, commuting cost coverage, and more help our people create space for what matters most in their personal and professional lives.

CarGurus may require in-person interviews as part of our hiring process, particularly for positions based in our Boston and Dublin offices. Candidates selected for an in-person interview will be notified in advance. Please be aware that travel expenses are the responsibility of the candidate.

We welcome all

CarGurus strives to be a place to which people can bring the ultimate expression of themselves and their potential—starting with our hiring process. We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, gender identity, or sexual orientation. We foster an inclusive environment that values people for their skills, experiences, and unique perspectives. That’s why we hope you’ll apply even if you don’t check every box listed in the job description. We also encourage you to tell your recruiter if you require accommodations to participate in our hiring process due to a disability so we can provide the appropriate support. We want to know what only you can bring to CarGurus. #LI-Hybrid

title: Quality Lead II - Production | 3 Day Work Week | Thurs - Sat - 7am - 7pm
description:
JOIN OUR OUTSTANDING TEAM!

3 day work week to assist with a better work-life balance!

Thursday-Saturday (Days) - 7 am to 7 pm

Climate Controlled Facility!

Paid Weekly, pay range for this position is $19.00 - $21.00 depending on shift and experience.


SUMMARY

Responsible for testing equipment, product, inspecting materials, work in process, final product, and accurately recording the findings according to procedures, instructions, engineering drawings, and training. Must evaluate rejects and product defects and make decisions regarding the status of the product based on the inspection criteria. Must report failures or non-conformance processes to Production Manager or Quality Supervisor.


PRIMARY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  1. Act as a quality auditor throughout the production process and in the final product testing phase. Partners with quality and engineering teams to do verification tests, product review checks and validation tests, including, but not limited to all areas of production assembly and product development.
  2. Functions as part of the team with Production Leads/Supervisors to verify first articles are approved prior to the beginning of cell work set-up. Must make sure the part is to customer specifications and engineering drawing.
  3. Follow applicable procedures, instructions, engineering drawings, and training.
  4. Test and/or inspect the quality of the equipment, materials, work in process, and final product in a timely manner according to established written Quality Department procedures, engineering drawings, and documentation. This includes critical inspection items that may affect the function of the product.
  5. Evaluate rejects and product defects and make decisions regarding the status of the product based on the inspection criteria. This includes evaluating the severity of the rejects.
  6. Able to do product testing, validation, life studies, and calibrations. This could include the preparation of any paperwork associated with such tasks.
  7. Interface with supervision and/or management to ensure quality rejects and/or problems are brought to the attention of responsible personnel. This may include interfacing with employees in other departments.
  8. Repeatedly test existing products or prototypes under real-world conditions in order to determine how long a product will last, what parts will break down first and how to improve durability.
  9. Complete all documents and records required.
  10. Fill-in and work as an effective member of the team as an Inspector or Lab Technician as needed.
  11. Keep work areas clean, organized and well maintained to ensure a safe work environment.
  12. Mentor employees as needed in terms of the products and/or processes.
  13. Other duties and responsibilities may be assigned as required.

AUTHORITY

  1. Reject nonconforming product.
  2. Approve all finished products by confirming specifications and conducting required tests.
  3. Request necessary supplies and resources required to complete the jobs assigned.
  4. Interface with other departments to ensure all quality rejects and/or problems are brought to the attention of responsible personnel.
  5. Suggest improved or alternative methods of inspecting and/or testing product.
  6. Audit throughout production floor to ensure production standards are met.

QUALIFICATIONS

  1. High School Diploma or equivalent required.
  2. Able to correctly inspect and test product according to instructions, engineering drawings, and training.
  3. Able to correctly use required tools, fixtures, rulers, testing equipment, etc. involved in the testing and inspection processes.
  4. Able to read and understand the product criteria on engineering drawings and blueprints.
  5. Able to recognize quality problems with equipment, materials, work in process, and final product, and to inspect for critical items that may affect the function of the product.
  6. Able to inspect product and perform all other required duties in a timely manner as outlined by department supervision and management.
  7. Able to mentor employees as needed throughout the production process.
  8. Able to work and communicate well with others as well as keen attention to detail.
  9. Able to complete necessary documents and records as required.
  10. Able to read and write English.
  11. Good work attendance and dependability.

title: Data Engineer
description:
Als ervaren Data Engineer werk je aan uitdagende data-oplossingen binnen moderne cloudomgevingen. Je ontwikkelt schaalbare data pipelines en helpt organisaties hun data optimaal te benutten. In een hecht team krijg je volop ruimte om jezelf verder te ontwikkelen en impact te maken.

Ben jij een Data Engineer die energie haalt uit complexe datavraagstukken en toe is aan een volgende stap? Bij Centennium krijg je de kans om te werken met de nieuwste technologieën binnen een omgeving waar kennisdeling en persoonlijke groei centraal staan.

Als Data Engineer bij Centennium ben je verantwoordelijk voor het ontwerpen, bouwen en optimaliseren van data-oplossingen binnen diverse klantomgevingen. Je werkt met moderne cloudplatformen zoals Azure, AWS of Google Cloud en ontwikkelt robuuste data pipelines en datawarehouses. Daarnaast denk je mee over data-architecturen en draag je bij aan innovatieve oplossingen. Je werkt nauw samen met collega’s en klanten om data om te zetten in waardevolle inzichten.

  • Ontwikkelen en optimaliseren van ETL-processen en data pipelines
  • Ontwerpen en implementeren van datawarehouse-oplossingen
  • Ontsluiten en integreren van diverse databronnen
  • Meedenken over en uitwerken van data-architecturen
  • Werken in agile teams binnen complexe data-omgevingen

Wat maakt deze functie perfect voor jou?

Deze rol is ideaal voor een ervaren Data Engineer die zichzelf verder wil ontwikkelen binnen een professionele en innovatieve omgeving. Je hebt minimaal vijf jaar ervaring binnen BI- en datawarehousingprojecten en hebt uitgebreide kennis van cloudplatformen, bij voorkeur Azure. Je bent analytisch sterk, communicatief vaardig en denkt proactief mee met klanten. Daarnaast krijg je energie van het werken in complexe omgevingen en het oplossen van uitdagende datavraagstukken. Je combineert technische expertise met consultancyvaardigheden en weet impact te maken.

Wat bieden wij jou

  • Leaseauto, laptop en telefoon (LLT-regeling)
  • 25 vakantiedagen en een goede pensioenregeling
  • Ruime ontwikkelmogelijkheden via specialistengroepen
  • Persoonlijke begeleiding bij jouw groeipad
  • Informele werksfeer met teamuitjes en kwartaalmeetings

Waar ga je werken?

Centennium is een gespecialiseerde data-organisatie met een hecht team van circa dertig professionals. Binnen de organisatie staan kennisdeling, samenwerking en persoonlijke ontwikkeling centraal. Je werkt in een informele, platte organisatie waar ruimte is voor initiatief en innovatie. Samen met collega’s werk je aan uitdagende projecten binnen uiteenlopende sectoren zoals overheid, finance en energie.

title: Surmasis Pharmaceutical- Quality Lead II |Mon-Wed 7am - 7pm | $20.00 per hour
description:
SUMMARY

The Quality Lead ensures that all products are manufactured in accordance with current Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and meet all internal specifications. This position will spend the majority of its time in the Surmasis cleanroom/manufacturing areas providing oversight and guidance to manufacturing personnel in the performance of their duties. This position is also responsible for performing a number of quality assurance checks on in-process products and finished goods. This position is responsible for reviewing documents to ensure that they were completed in accordance with current GMP and site SOPs. Strong organizational skills and the ability to prioritize work and respond to customer demands in a timely fashion are critical requirements of this position.

Responsibilities include leading department employees to complete assigned duties in a timely manner while working safely as an effective member of the team. Leads must have good math skills, an attention for detail and the ability to work independently with minimal supervision. The Lead must also ensure accurate completion of associated documents and records. Requires the ability to direct and train employees as well as monitor multiple processes simultaneously.


PRIMARY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  1. Leads a team of people by example in the areas of attitude, work quality, work ethic, dependability, and communication.
  2. Supports batch manufacturing activities by performing quality verifications and sampling plans.
  3. Reviews documents to ensure they meet GMP and site SOP requirements.
  4. Identifies, investigates, and prepares reports on quality issues.
  5. Performs line clearance, inspections, and physical testing in manufacturing areas.
  6. Interprets generated data and communicate results to Quality management.
  7. Maintains effective communication and partnership with manufacturing and quality systems department.
  8. Maintains quality standards in all tasks performed.
  9. Adapts to changes in the work environment and must be able to change shifts or work overtime and/or weekends as needed.
  10. Handles fast pace working environment which may require switching between multiple manufacturing rooms within a single day.
  11. Leads employees and provide direction to complete required tasks.
  • Follows applicable procedures, instructions, engineering drawings and training.
  • Trains employees according to departmental training requirements
  • Monitors employees in their jobs and assist as necessary.
  • Answers employee questions involved with the Lead’s respective area.
  1. Interfaces with supervision and/or management to ensure assigned duties are completed accurately. This may include interfacing with employees in other departments.
  2. Works as an effective member of the team.
  3. Ensures area is clean, organized and well maintained.
  4. Completes all documents and records required.
  5. Participates in investigations on non-conforming product, as necessary.
  6. Raw material receipt verification, sampling, and CofA generation.
  7. Raw material kit verifications for kit going to/from manufacturing room.
  8. Maintains 5S, especially regarding cleanliness and organization of work cell.
  9. Trains and mentors other leads.
  10. Reads, follows, and understands standard operating procedures.
  11. Other duties and responsibilities may be assigned as required.

AUTHORITY

  1. Trains lower-level employees in the Lead’s respective area.
  2. Interfaces with other departments as necessary.
  3. Works on continuously improving the organization and function of the department by suggesting procedural improvements.
  4. Stops manufacturing line should a quality defect be identified and need addressed.

QUALIFICATIONS

  1. High school diploma or equivalent required.
  2. Able to lead and influence others by example in the areas of attitude, work quality, work ethic, dependability, and communication.
  3. Able to read and understand the product criteria on engineering drawings.
  4. Able to direct and train employees.
  5. Able to supervise multiple activities or jobs simultaneously in an accurate manner.
  6. Able to work and communicate well with others.
  7. Able to read and write English.
  8. Good work attendance and dependability.
  9. Excels in working independently and maintaining self-motivation to complete work.
  10. Knowledge of various controls and procedures such as error rates, shortages, and cycle counting.
  11. Must be able to work with minimal supervision.
  12. Must be able to pass a background check.
  13. Must be able to complete a position assessment test.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to stand, walk, sit, and operate a computer. The employee is regularly required to use hands to grasp, finger or handle objects and reach with hands and arms. The employee is frequently required to talk and hear. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, and color determination. This employee must occasionally lift and /or exert force from 25 up to 75 pounds. Push and/or pull up to 300 pounds.


WORK ENVIRONMENT

Majority of time spent working in the manufacturing floor.


Benefits:

At Surmasis, we’re proud to offer a comprehensive benefits package, including:

  • Medical Insurance – PPO & HMO plans
  • Dental and Vision Coverage
  • Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
  • Life Insurance Options
  • Short-Term and Long-Term Disability (STD/LTD)
  • 401(k) Retirement Plan

title: Fitness Director
description:
Villa Sport offers exciting and fulfilling career opportunities for those who thrive in a fast-paced, energizing environment. Our portfolio includes clubs across multiple states, including California, Texas, Colorado, Idaho, and Oregon. Our resort-style clubs are more than just gyms; they are communities where fitness, family, and fun come together. We are on a mission to create energizing environments where you can thrive and grow with us.

If you're a high-performing, outgoing, service-oriented superstar looking for a chance to make a difference, you've found your home. At Villa Sport, we offer a fantastic work environment, competitive wages, and a 401(k) plan with a company match of up to 4% of your compensation. Ready to join a team that’s going places? Your journey starts here!

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Fitness Director leads a team of fitness professionals in providing 5-star service to all Villa Sport members in the fitness center and in delivering high quality fitness training services, small group training programs, and educational seminars that help members achieve their health and personal goals. The Fitness Director ensures that all members feel knowledgeable and comfortable in the fitness center and that all Fitness Staff are genuinely friendly, outgoing, approachable, helpful and credible. The Fitness Director ensures that new members are properly integrated so they can exercise effectively and safely, are informed about all the program offerings and complimentary services available and are advised as to the fitness programs and services that would best meet their needs and goals. The Fitness Director is responsible for achieving or exceeding departmental budget expectations and for ensuring that all fitness equipment is properly maintained, operational and safe.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS INCLUDE:

  • $83,600-$88,000 annual base salary based on experience.
  • Monthly bonus and commission opportunities.
  • PTO.
  • Benefits package.
  • 401K with dollar for dollar match up to 4%.
  • Complimentary club membership.
  • Discounts on club products and services.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Club and/or hospitality industry experience (high-end, resort-style, family-oriented facilities) preferred
  • Relationship-based selling/servicing skills and training/presentation skills
  • Word, Excel and PowerPoint basic proficiency
  • Budgeting and analysis skills
  • Knowledge and expertise in individual and group training protocols and standards; current fitness trends; and anatomy/physiology (a plus but not required)
  • In customer engagement and retention
  • In directing a revenue-generating department or business
  • In managing and achieving a budget
  • In leading a team of 25+ people (2 years minimum preferred)
  • In developing and delivering educational workshops and seminars
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills; great listening skills
  • Comfortable with striking up conversations with members, with approaching members at the club, with providing advice and assistance, with calling members on the phone, and with handling and resolving member complaints
  • Excellent customer service and people skills
  • Skilled at rapport and relationship-building
  • Calm under fire; maintains composure
  • Healthy lifestyle habits
  • First Aid/CPR certification required prior to hire date
  • College Degree preferred
  • Occasional bending and kneeling, and infrequent lifting of weights up to 50 lbs.
  • Frequent standing, walking, reaching.
  • The noise level is usually moderate to high

Villa Sport and/or any affiliated entities (collectively, the “Company” or “we”) provide this California Privacy Notice (“Notice”) to describe our privacy practices with respect to our collection of Personal Information as required under the California Consumer Privacy Act (“CCPA”) as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act (“CPRA”). For purposes of this Notice, when we refer to Consumers, we mean you only to the extent you are a job applicant who resides in California.

1. Information We Collect From or About Job Applicants

title: Finishing Supervisor
description:
sg360° partners with Fortune 1000 brands to pursue unmatched direct marketing performance. We leave no stone unturned in our efforts to drive smarter targeting, stronger messaging and improved ROI. Everything we do - audience analytics, strategic planning, creative development, production and distribution - we do in the pursuit of performance.


When you join us, you gain access to a comprehensive benefits package, including paid time off, holiday pay, health, dental, and vision insurance, life insurance, an education assistance program, short- and long-term disability, wellness resources, identity theft protection, and a 401k with employer match. Be part of a legacy of excellence and growth with sg360°!


Position Summary

sg360° is looking for a Finishing Supervisor to lead daily production activities and employees within our Finishing Department. Under the direction of the Shift Manager, this position is responsible for keeping production on schedule while maintaining high standards for quality, accuracy, safety, and productivity.


The Supervisor will provide hands-on leadership, assign work, adjust staffing and priorities, troubleshoot production issues, communicate job status, and support the training and development of production employees. This position may oversee one or more finishing operations, including: Folding, Cutting, Attaching, Imaging, Inserting, Die-Cutting, Shrink Wrapping.


Responsibilities Include:

Production & Operations

  • Monitor daily production schedules and adjust priorities to support on-time completion.
  • Assign and adjust staffing to effectively utilize available employees and maximize productivity.
  • Review job tickets and ensure revisions and updates are completed accurately.
  • Communicate job status, production quantities, issues, rework, staffing needs, and other important information to the Shift Manager.
  • Review requirements for non-routine jobs and provide clear direction to production employees.
  • Ensure packaging requirements are completed according to customer specifications.
  • Record accurate production information, including job numbers, equipment used, and crew assignments.
  • Monitor waste, employee downtime, supplies, and other resources to help control production costs.

Quality & Accuracy

  • Monitor production to ensure finished products meet customer specifications.
  • Work closely with Quality Control to identify and resolve quality issues.
  • Review, approve, and sign Quality Control time pulls.
  • Monitor and approve production samples.
  • Verify that the correct inkjet files are loaded on the appropriate equipment.
  • When assigned to Cutting, review rule-up sheets and cutting samples for proper setup and accuracy.
  • Ensure applicable USPS requirements are followed for finished products entering the mail stream.

Employee Leadership & Development

  • Provide daily direction and support to production employees.
  • Train employees on job responsibilities, equipment operation, production procedures, safety requirements, and company policies.
  • Provide coaching, recognition, and performance feedback.
  • Address performance or attendance concerns and communicate potential employee issues to the Shift Manager.
  • Support employee development and help build a strong, productive team.

Safety & Housekeeping

  • Promote and enforce a safe work environment and established safety procedures.
  • Ensure permanent and temporary employees follow required safety practices.
  • Maintain acceptable housekeeping standards throughout assigned production areas.
  • When assigned to the Clean Room, enforce applicable procedures and restrict access to authorized personnel.

Operational Support

  • Ensure necessary supplies, equipment, postal tray tags, and other resources are available to support production.
  • Coordinate with other departments to maintain an efficient flow of materials and work.
  • Stage materials, supplies, and postal materials for upcoming jobs when time and space permit.
  • Provide hands-on support with setups and troubleshooting when assigned to Imaging.
  • Communicate temporary staffing needs for upcoming shifts when needed.
  • Order USPS supplies when assigned.
  • Approve jobs beginning during the assigned shift when delegated by the Shift Manager.
  • Perform other duties and assignments as directed.

title: Retail Store Supervisor
description:
Join Our Team as a Retail Store Supervisor!

At DOCOMO PACIFIC, we believe in connection—bringing people, innovation, and opportunity together to shape a brighter future for our island communities. Rooted in the values of excellence, respect, trust, and teamwork, we are powered by the spirit of Ina’fa’maolek—working together for the greater good.

We are looking for a Retail Store Supervisor who will provide direct support to our Retail and Support Teams in achieving departmental and company goals, identifying operational efficiencies, and ensuring an unmatched customer experience in our retail locations. This role serves as a leader within the store, driving sales performance, coaching team members, maintaining operational excellence, and supporting the day-to-day management of retail operations.

What You'll Do

As a Retail Store Supervisor, you'll play a key role in supporting the success of our retail operations while creating exceptional experiences for both customers and employees.

Revenue & Customer Experience

  • Support the achievement of store revenue targets and key performance indicators.
    • Engage customers and assist in understanding, demonstrating, and selecting products and services.
    • Track, compile, and report weekly revenue performance against targets.
    • Identify and communicate challenges while assisting in the development of solutions.
    • Maintain a high level of customer satisfaction and support achievement of customer experience goals, including Net Promoter Score (NPS) targets.
    • Ensure customers receive friendly, knowledgeable, and professional service.
    • Maintain store appearance, cleanliness, organization, and visual merchandising standards.
    • Ensure promotional materials, displays, and products are accurately presented and merchandised according to company standards.
    • Troubleshoot, research, escalate, and resolve customer concerns and service-related issues.

Operations

  • Conduct interviews and assist with recruitment efforts to fill open positions.
    • Review and approve credit adjustments and customer transaction exceptions within delegated authority.
    • Submit inventory requests and monitor stock levels to support business needs.
    • Receive inventory and ensure items are accurately reflected in company systems.
    • Review inventory discrepancies and support resolution efforts.
    • Compile and submit weekly retail reports.
    • Report customer and employee feedback and assist in identifying solutions.
    • Support the day-to-day maintenance and operations of retail facilities, including coordinating vendors, appointments, service requests, and facility repairs.
    • Assist in managing retail facility budgets and ensuring service contracts remain current.
    • Maintain accountability for store inventory and company assets.
    • Process payments, point-of-sale transactions, reconciliations, deposits, and end-of-day reporting.
    • Conduct physical inventory counts and audits.
    • Complete required training and stay informed on operational updates, product changes, and company initiatives.
    • Perform other duties as assigned.

Leadership Responsibilities

  • Coach, counsel, train, and develop team members.
    • Evaluate employee performance and provide ongoing feedback.
    • Assist with staff scheduling and workload distribution.
    • Ensure compliance with company policies, procedures, and customer service standards.
    • Motivate and support employees in achieving sales and operational goals.
    • Respond to customer concerns and escalations in a timely and professional manner.
    • Identify opportunities for sales growth and operational efficiencies.
    • Directly support the Retail Store Manager in overseeing all aspects of store operations.

What We're Looking For

We are seeking a motivated leader who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys working with people, and is passionate about delivering outstanding customer experiences. If you:

  • Enjoy coaching and developing others.
    • Take ownership and accountability for results.
    • Are customer-focused and solution-oriented.
    • Communicate effectively and professionally.
    • Can balance operational priorities while maintaining excellent customer service.
    • Are self-motivated and empowered to make decisions.

...then you'll be a great fit for our team!

Qualifications

  • Minimum High School Diploma or GED required.
    • Minimum of two (2) years of related retail, sales, customer service, or leadership experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
    • Knowledge of DOCOMO PACIFIC products, services, and competitive offerings preferred.
    • Working knowledge of billing systems and retail operations.
    • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and other business applications.

title: Principal Storage Architect
description:
About Graphcore

Graphcore is a leading innovator in artificial intelligence computing. We develop hardware, software, and data center infrastructure that provide the specialized processing and systems capabilities needed to advance AI while improving the efficiency required for broad adoption.

As part of SoftBank Group, Graphcore works alongside companies developing advanced technologies. Our teams bring together AI researchers, silicon designers, hardware and software engineers, and systems architects to solve complex technical problems across the computing stack.

The Opportunity

As Principal Storage Architect, you will define the high-performance storage architecture for Graphcore's AI computing and data center infrastructures. You will lead the design of local and distributed storage tiers that provide the throughput, availability, and predictable tail latency required for large-scale training and inference.

Working within Advanced Architecture, you will address storage requirements for saving model states, offloading key-value caches, large datasets, and high-speed data-loading pipelines. You will combine hands-on performance engineering with Principal-level technical leadership across hardware, software, networking, systems engineering, automation, supply chain, and external technology partners.

What You Will Do

  • Define the end-to-end architecture and technology roadmap for local, disaggregated, and distributed storage across Graphcore AI server and data center platforms.
  • Design storage topologies that optimize PCIe lane allocation, network-domain placement, and data paths among CPUs, AI accelerators, memory, and storage systems.
  • Lead the architecture of storage control-plane and data-plane solutions, evaluating commercial and open technologies against performance, resilience, manageability, and lifecycle requirements.
  • Profile and tune the Linux storage stack, block layer, I/O schedulers, direct I/O paths, file systems, and drivers to improve IOPS, bandwidth, and 99.99th-percentile latency.
  • Optimize storage for AI workloads, including model checkpointing, key-value cache offload, data ingestion, and direct data movement between NVMe storage and accelerator memory.
  • Set the technical direction for NVMe SSD lifecycle management, including qualification, provisioning, health monitoring, firmware rollout, failure handling, and warranty-return automation across E1.S, E3.S, U.2, and U.3 devices.
  • Define telemetry and alerting requirements for direct-attached and distributed storage, including endurance, wear, drive writes per day, thermals, capacity, performance, and latency anomalies.
  • Provide architecture requirements and technical guidance to automation teams building frameworks that characterize storage performance, reliability, and compatibility across AI platforms.
  • Lead root-cause analysis for complex storage failures and performance degradation across Linux kernels, drivers, PCIe, networks, SSD firmware, and third-party storage systems.
  • Partner with storage vendors, supply chain, networking, systems engineering, and product teams to select, integrate, and deploy storage components and platforms.
  • Evaluate emerging storage, interconnect, and memory-tiering technologies and translate relevant developments into platform requirements and future system designs.

What You Will Bring

  • A bachelor's or equivalent experience or master's degree in computer science, computer engineering, information technology, electrical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Extensive hands-on experience in storage engineering and architecture for AI, high-performance computing, hyperscale, or large data center environments, including technical leadership at Principal, Staff, or Lead Architect scope.
  • Deep knowledge of NVMe, PCIe Gen5 or Gen6 architecture, NAND flash behavior, SSD form factors, endurance, firmware, and device lifecycle management.
  • Deep operational knowledge of Linux storage internals, including the block layer, I/O schedulers, direct I/O, kernel and driver behavior, and file systems such as XFS, ext4, or ZFS.
  • Hands-on experience with storage benchmarking and profiling tools such as fio, blktrace, iostat, and perf, including the ability to design representative workload models and isolate bottlenecks.
  • Programming and automation skills in Python and Bash, with experience using structured data formats and REST APIs to build monitoring, validation, or lifecycle workflows.
  • Demonstrated ability to diagnose complex hardware and software interactions, including kernel failures, PCIe errors, network issues, performance regressions, and SSD firmware defects.
  • Experience defining telemetry signals, alert thresholds, dashboards, and operational response criteria for storage health and performance at fleet scale.
  • Proven ability to lead cross-functional architecture decisions, influence senior engineers and leaders, and communicate technical risks, tradeoffs, and recommendations clearly.

Preferred Qualifications

These qualifications are helpful, not required. We encourage you to apply even if you do not meet every preferred qualification.

  • Experience implementing, testing, or troubleshooting GPU Direct Storage or comparable direct accelerator-to-storage technologies.
  • Experience designing or operating NVMe over Fabrics deployments using RoCEv2 or TCP.
  • Experience with the Storage Performance Development Kit or other user-space storage frameworks.
  • Familiarity with high-performance parallel and distributed file systems such as Weka, VAST Data, Lustre, DAOS, DDN, or comparable platforms.
  • Knowledge of Compute Express Link and its implications for future memory and storage tiering in AI servers.

United States Benefits Overview

Benefits vary by work location, employment status, scheduled hours, and plan eligibility and are subject to the terms of the applicable plans and company policies. This overview is not a contract or guarantee of benefits.

title: Haven Certification Engineer
description:
Vast is developing next-generation space stations and space infrastructure using an incremental, hardware-rich, and low-cost approach. title: Principal Engineer, AI Cloud Software
description:
Firmus Technologies

Firmus Technologies is a global leader pioneering the development and operation of efficient AI infrastructure across Asia Pacific.

Founded in Australia in 2019, our mission is to create the most efficient AI infrastructure by combining cutting-edge technology with a steadfast commitment to sustainability.

At Firmus, we are unique in our approach. We design, build, and operate a new class of digital infrastructure – the AI Factory. Through our model-to-grid technology approach, we have pushed the boundaries of multi-generational liquid cooling systems, energy management, AI software orchestration, and construction. For our customers, this approach allows us to make every watt count and deliver low-cost AI tokens globally.

Firmus AI Cloud

Our large-scale GPU cloud platform, Firmus AI Cloud, is purpose-built to deliver energy-efficient AI compute at scale to customers.

It empowers developers, enterprises, educational institutions, and government users to train and deploy AI models with unmatched efficiency and cost savings. With an ever-growing suite of services and applications, we are committed to delivering a cloud experience that is market-leading, proprietary, and built to scale.

ROLE SUMMARY

Firmus Technologies is seeking a Senior AI Infrastructure Engineer, Observability, to join our Engineering and Technology team. You will establish how we measure, validate and communicate the health of GPU infrastructure used for customer and internal workloads. You will define trusted health signals and service-readiness criteria, and turn them into reusable dashboards, alerts, queries, diagnostic checks and operational guidance. Your work will help commissioning, infrastructure and operations teams bring capacity online safely, identify degradation early and recover from failures quickly. You will also make knowledge self-service by publishing clear reference implementations, runbooks and AI-ready operational knowledge that other teams can use and extend.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • The Health Standard
    Define GPU and host health criteria for customer and internal workloads, and the service-readiness gates that repair and capacity workflows depend on. Cover what stops or corrupts AI jobs: GPUs falling off the bus, XID events, ECC and memory faults, NVLink/NVSwitch degradation, thermal and power capping, NCCL and collective failures, silent data corruption, and stragglers running below fleet baseline.

  • Reference Implementations
    Publish golden dashboards, alerts, PromQL/LogQL queries and health checks that other teams adopt and extend. Your output is the standard and the examples. The alerts must be specific, low-noise, and with a clear next action.
  • Diagnostics with Real Pass/Fail Criteria
    DCGM checks, NCCL and bandwidth tests, stress and burn-in, and validation jobs that confirm a server matches expected performance. Others must be able to run them without you.

  • Fault Isolation
    Separate a bad GPU from a cooling, host, network or power-limit problem using host and BMC/management-interface telemetry together, including when the same signature appears across many servers. A clean management view means nothing if the host is throwing faults.
  • Detection of the Failures that Don't Crash

Rising correctable ECC counts, NVLink retries, thermal slowdown, XID patterns, wrong results with no error. Keep the knowledge current: what each signal means, what to do next on the machine, and where the operation team must make the final decision.

  • Partnership and Escalation
    Work with commissioning on bring-up and acceptance, operations on break-fix, infrastructure on what healthy hardware looks like, and the telemetry owners on making your signals production-grade. Run technical sessions with customer teams on the telemetry they need. Join GPU and host incidents, including debugging on the server and convert every finding into a reusable check, alert or runbook. Give engineering leadership a straight read on fleet health and risk.

SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 7+ years in GPU, HPC, AI infrastructure or closely related large-scale systems engineering environments, including ownership of health monitoring or diagnostics used by customers or internal teams.
  • Experience with production GPU fault diagnosis. You've found genuine faults through XID events, ECC/memory errors, NVLink issues, power or thermal limits and caught at least one before the job died.
  • Strong Linux and server fundamentals. You can debug on the machine and reason across GPU, CPU, memory, PCIe, power and cooling. You automate in Python or similar.
  • Hands-on with GPU diagnostics and validation such as DCGM, NCCL/collective tests, stress testing and you've turned them into checks other people run.
  • Experience analysing infrastructure telemetry, building trusted dashboards and alerts. Savvy with PromQL, LogQL, Grafana or comparable tooling. Able to follow an unexpected signal until there is a cause and can turn that into an alert or check others will trust.
  • Uses AI tools as a normal part of analysis and build work. Can structure health knowledge and build AI skills so operation team with AI assistants can use it effectively to recover from incidents.
  • Willing to take part in the incident-response on-call rotation.
  • Willing to travel overseas occasionally when the role requires it.
  • Clear and effective written and verbal communication in English.

Highly Desirable Experiences

  • Production experience on large GPU systems with tight GPU-to-GPU interconnect.
  • Multiple sites or GPU generations, especially preparing health monitoring before a new GPU class entered production.
  • Background at an AI cloud, GPU cloud or HPC centre running customer workloads.
  • Experience working with data or ML engineers on GPU/host failure prediction from health signals.
  • Built a structured operational knowledge so AI assistants can use it effectively during incident recovery.

Location & Reporting

  • Location: Singapore
  • Report to: Senior Manager, Platform Engineering

Employment Basis

Full-time

Diversity

At Firmus, we are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds who are passionate about creating a more sustainable future through innovative engineering solutions.

Join us in our mission to revolutionize the AI industry through sustainable practices and cutting-edge engineering. Apply now to be part of shaping the future of sustainable AI infrastructure.

description:
