WHY ARVA

  • Direct mentorship from the CFO and visibility with the board and investors
  • Broad scope across capital markets, strategy, and operations
  • A chance to help build a company at the intersection of agriculture, energy, and climate

COMPENSATION

Competitive base salary of [$150,000] plus annual bonus and equity. Work arrangement: on-site in Houston, TX.

title: Principal AI Engineer, Machine Learning Operations
description:
Principal Machine Learning Operations Engineer

About Us:

BlackSky is a real-time intelligence company. We own and operate the world's most advanced space-based intelligence platform and provide customers satellite imagery, automated analytics and high-frequency monitoring of strategic locations, economic assets and events from around the globe. BlackSky is trusted by the most demanding allied military and intelligence organizations and commercial companies to deliver foresight into critical matters that affect national security and the economy. BlackSky's data enables governments and businesses to see, understand and anticipate change as it happens, giving them the ultimate strategic advantage so they can act quickly. Our global team works with cutting-edge technology to make a difference around the world and prides itself on being people-first, customer-focused and fun.

BlackSky is looking for a Principal AI Engineer, MLOps to pioneer the next generation of space-based intelligence and real-time geospatial analytics. Reporting directly to the Director of Innovative Solutions, you will serve as the technical authority responsible for designing, scaling, deploying, and automating state-of-the-art computer vision (CV) and machine learning (ML) architectures.

In this role, you will bridge the gap between cutting-edge remote sensing research and high-performance, production-ready software. You will lead the charge in utilizing modern AI methodologies to extract actionable intelligence from satellite imagery, optimizing edge and cloud compute environments, and delivering resilient capabilities. While we would strongly prefer candidates near either our Herndon, VA or Seattle, WA offices, we are open to strong remote candidates.

Responsibilities:

  • End-to-End Model R&D: Leading full-lifecycle model engineering from initial problem formulation and dataset curation to training, validation, deployment, and error analysis.
  • Model Robustness & Domain Adaptation: Driving model resilience against challenging real-world satellite conditions, including off-nadir angles, low light, seasonal variations, weather distortions, dense environments, and cross-sensor domain shifts.
  • Production Integration: Ensuring models are reliably trained, versioned, deployed, monitored, and maintained in production.
  • Technical Leadership & Strategy: Communicating technical progress, risks, and stack to cross-functional leadership and Product partners while contributing to proposals and white papers.
  • Mentorship & Engineering Culture: Providing technical mentorship, spearheading design reviews and experiment planning, and fostering a culture of technical excellence across the engineering team.
  • Other job-related duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications:

  • Minimum of 12 years of hands-on software engineering experience, including at least four years developing computer vision or machine learning solutions for geospatial, remote sensing, or similarly complex imagery.
  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, mathematics, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Expert-level proficiency in Python and demonstrated experience developing deep learning systems using PyTorch or comparable modern ML frameworks.
  • Proven experience designing, training, evaluating, and deploying production-grade computer vision models for tasks such as object detection, segmentation, change detection, image classification, or time-series analysis.
  • Strong experience working with remote sensing imagery and the unique challenges associated with geospatial data, including varying spatial resolutions, viewing geometries, sensors, and environmental conditions.
  • Hands-on experience building geospatial data and CV pipelines using tools such as Rasterio, GDAL, GeoPandas, Shapely, xarray, Zarr, or similar technologies.
  • Demonstrated experience taking CV capabilities from experimentation through production, including model evaluation, deployment, and performance optimization.
  • Experience developing and operating ML workloads in AWS, including GPU-based training and inference.
  • Strong technical communication skills with the ability to communicate architecture decisions, experimental results, tradeoffs, risks, and recommendations to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated ability to provide technical leadership and mentorship across engineering teams without requiring direct management authority.
  • The work this role supports requires holding US citizenship.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree or Ph.D. in computer science, engineering, mathematics, machine learning, remote sensing, or a related quantitative field.
  • At least 15 years of hands-on software engineering, computer vision, or machine learning experience.
  • Experience working with imagery from multiple commercial and government remote sensing sources, such as BlackSky, Sentinel, Airbus, Planet, or WorldView.
  • Demonstrated experience optimizing ML systems for production constraints, including inference latency, throughput, memory utilization, GPU efficiency, and cost.
  • Experience rapidly developing prototypes or proof-of-concept applications and communicating results through customer demonstrations, proposals, white papers, or other technical materials.
  • Strong experience with modern MLOps practices, including experiment tracking, dataset and model versioning, reproducibility, automated evaluation, and production monitoring.
  • Experience applying foundation models, vision-language models (VLMs), multimodal approaches, or self-supervised learning to geospatial or remote sensing problems.
  • Experience adapting models across sensors, geographic regions, resolutions, collection conditions, or other significant domain shifts.

Life at BlackSky for full-time US benefits eligible employees includes:

  • Medical, dental, vision, disability, group term life and AD&D, voluntary life and AD&D insurance
    • BlackSky pays 100% of employee-only premiums for medical, dental and vision and contributes $100/month for out-of-pocket expenses!
  • 15 days of PTO, 11 Company holidays, four Floating Holidays (pro-rated based on hire date), one day of paid volunteerism leave per year, parental leave and more
  • 401(k) pre-tax and Roth deferral options with employer match
  • Flexible Spending Accounts
  • Employee Stock Purchase Program
  • Employee Assistance and Travel Assistance Programs
  • Employer matching donations
  • Professional development
  • Mac or PC? Your choice!
  • Awesome swag

The anticipated salary range for candidates in Seattle, WA is $185,000-$215,000 per year. The final compensation package offered to a successful candidate will be dependent on specific background and education. BlackSky is a multi-state employer and this pay scale may not reflect salary ranges in other states or locations outside of Seattle, WA.

BlackSky is committed to hiring and retaining a diverse workforce. We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, protected veteran status or any other characteristic protected by law.

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. #LI-Remote

title: Category Analyst - Costco
description:
BUILT ON FLAVOR. FUELED BY PEOPLE.

What’s it like to work at Kinder’s? Well, there’s a lot of snacking and geeking out over what we all cooked over the weekend. Beyond that, there’s also plenty of hard work. Because we don’t just like flavor, we’re obsessed with it.

With over 100 products sold nationwide, we’re now a top-five brand in multiple flavor categories at Costco, Walmart, Whole Foods, and more. We’re not your typical CPG company. Privately held and founder-led, we like to think of ourselves as a pirate ship in a sea of cruise ships. Our crew is adventurous and fearless. We chart our own course and chase big ideas to make food unforgettable.

As we expand globally and approach $1 billion in revenue, we need more smart-and-scrappy, flavor-obsessed people to come aboard. If you’re looking for a place where you can see the real impact of your work... this is it! Every day, you’ll be part of a journey to add flavor to millions of meals and lives.

About the Role:

The Category Analyst will support sales analytics across key customer accounts and provide actionable insights to drive brand and category growth. They will work closely with the Sales team to develop strategies around assortment, marketing, customer presentations, and more. The ideal candidate will have very strong analytic skills and can craft effective stories with data. If you are passionate about driving growth through actionable insights, we want to hear from you!

Key Responsibilities Include:

Customer Analytics

  • Lead analytics for Kinder’s rapidly growing Costco businesses.
  • Track and report sales performance of Kinder’s key initiatives, such as innovation launches or in-store marketing programs.
  • Advance regional and store-level analysis to drive growth for Costco & Kinder’s.
  • Utilize variety of data sources to answer key business questions including innovation success, promotional strategy, assortment opportunities, etc.
  • Develop expertise in Costco CRX, Circana, and Numerator to lead analyses and guide Kinder’s strategy and tactics.

Data Storytelling

  • Build comprehensive presentations with strong data visualization. Share insights, findings, and recommendations across Kinder’s organization, and externally in buyer meetings.
  • Lead recurring Costco performance review highlighting performance differences across items and regions.
  • Partner with broker team to monitor and manage item inventory levels at the regional store-level
  • Support sales operations with the development of marketing event forecasts and post promotional analysis
  • Monitor rest of market performance and leverage cross-account data to develop regional case studies that support the sales team with rotational assortment recommendations

What Success Will Look Like:

  • Category analyst becomes a trusted partner for Kinder’s Costco team.
  • Lead internal sales, assortment, and innovation reporting.
  • Own cross functional communication of analytic findings and opportunities.
  • Partner with sales, marketing, supply chain, etc. to deliver internal and external sales targets.

Skills & Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in marketing, market research, or related field.
  • 2-4 years of experience in category management, sales analytics, insights, or related field within the CPG industry.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to analyze complex data sets and derive actionable insights.
  • Experience with syndicated data (e.g., Circana, NIQ, SPINS) and household panel data (e.g., Circana, Numerator).
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to distill complex information into clear and concise insights and tell stories with data.
  • Strong project management skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and meet deadlines.
  • Proficiency in PowerPoint and Excel

Personal Characteristics:

  • Strategic thinker with the ability to connect insights to business strategy and decision-making.
  • Collaborative team player with strong leadership skills and the ability to influence cross-functional teams.
  • Business builder who owns and drives results.
  • Growth mindset with an excitement to learn (and teach).
  • Thrive in a dynamic, lean, and agile environment with proven record of completing projects on time in full through excellent cross functional team. management, leadership, communication and influence
  • Self-starter who takes initiative and speaks their mind.
  • Excited to be part of a fast-moving team with the ability to be a leader and a follower.
  • Enjoy making decisions and finding ways to say ‘yes’ as often as possible to impactful and important priorities.

Pay Transparency:

The expected starting salary range for this role is $105,000- $115,000 per year. The salary range posted for this role reflects the good-faith base pay range Kinder’s reasonably expects to offer at the time of posting and may vary based on the location of the role. Individual compensation within the posted range will be determined based on factors such as relevant education, experience, qualifications, skills, and business needs.

SEASONED FOR SUCCESS:

  • No two days here are the same.
  • We try to be good team members and good communicators, but we don’t live by hierarchy and structure – everyone is a difference maker here.
  • We make a lot of decisions in the face of incomplete information – our team embraces ambiguity and tries to make good decisions fast rather than great decisions slow.
  • We believe our job is to take smart risk, not to eliminate risk.
  • We believe in growing our skills and becoming a better company with more managerial expertise, but we are an entrepreneurial company at heart.
  • We aren’t trying to be average – we want to do exceptional things, and we are willing to work hard to achieve them.

BENEFITS THAT BRING MORE TO THE TABLE:

We offer a range of total rewards that may include paid time off, 401k, bonus / incentive eligibility, equity grants, competitive health benefits, and other family-friendly benefits, including parental leave. Kinder’s benefits vary based on eligibility and can be reviewed in more detail during the interview process.

OUR RECIPE FOR BALANCE:

We believe great culture starts with people. We’re a people-first company built on connection, collaboration, and balance. Most of our work happens in the office to spark creativity and community, but we also offer flexibility so team members have the autonomy to work outside the office when needed to support their work-life balance and personal commitments.

WHERE EVERY INGREDIENT MATTERS:

Kinder's is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, gender, citizenship, marital status, religion, age, disability, gender identity, results of genetic testing, veteran status, as well as any other legally-protected characteristic. If you have a disability under the Americans with Disabilities Act or similar law, and you need any accommodation during the application process or to perform these job requirements, please reach out to us at careers@kinders.com

INTERNAL CANDIDATE ELIGIBILITY

  • Regular employees

APPLICATION DEADLINE:

Open until filled. Applications should be received by October 30, 2026 to be considered for the first round of interviews. Resume and cover letter are reviewed and required. Incomplete applications will not be considered.


WHO WE ARE

Disability Rights California (DRC) defends, advances, and strengthens the rights and opportunities of people with disabilities.


DRC works for a world where all disabled people have power and are treated with dignity and respect. In this world, people with disabilities are supported, valued, included in their communities, afforded the same opportunities as people without disabilities, and make their own decisions.


DRC values all forms of human diversity. We are committed to a culture of belonging where all people are welcome. In order to be effective advocates for all people with disabilities, we must address discrimination in all its forms, including the unique challenges faced by people who experience the intersection of multiple systems of discrimination.

OFFICE OF CLIENTS’ RIGHTS ADVOCACY

DRC has a contract with the Department of Developmental Services (DDS), State of California, to provide Clients’ Rights Advocacy services for clients of each of the 21 regional centers located statewide. That contract funds the Assistant Clients’ Rights Advocate (ACRA) position. We are a team of zealous advocates and disability generalists who are building a culture of teamwork and working for a world where all disabled people have power, are treated with dignity and respect, and make their own decisions.


PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The ACRA assists and advocates for people with developmental disabilities who are regional center clients, including people who reside in state developmental centers and community facilities. The ACRA is primarily responsible for clerical and administrative support for the office, which provides information, advice, and representation on a wide range of legal topics impacting people who receive regional center services. Examples are special education, Social Security, IHSS, healthcare and insurance, and living in the community.


The ACRA works under the direct supervision of a Clients’ Rights Advocate and in collaboration with other OCRA advocates and attorneys in their advocacy and outreach efforts.


This position is in a location convenient to the regional center and is eligible for a hybrid schedule working both remotely and in-office. Currently the office is located at 1000 S. Fremont Avenue, Suite 3233, Alhambra, CA 98103. The ACRA may work remotely up to three days per week.


JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

Essential functions are the job responsibilities an employee must be able to perform, with or without reasonable accommodation. ACRA essential functions include:


Support and Advocacy – 85%

· Work in-person in the Alhambra office a minimum of two days per week, in collaboration with OCRA’s East Los Angeles Regional Center team.

· Greet callers and provide initial response to requests for help.

· Coordinate meetings and conference calls.

· Process incoming and outgoing mail.

· Apply screening guidelines to identify problems and determine appropriateness of advocacy services.

· Provide information and referral to individuals who do not qualify for representation or services.

· Process requests for materials and publications.

· Assist in client and caller interviews.

· Use electronic case management software to create case files, including recording required demographic data, and to maintain accurate and timely case information.

· Collect data and generate reports.

· Assemble evidence packets for use in administrative hearings and other proceedings.


Outreach / Training – 15%

· Develop and update community referral information.

· Strengthen and build relationships with local community-based organizations.

· Assist in scheduling, organizing, and conducting training activities, and developing and producing educational materials.

· Assist in the development and implementation of an outreach plan, including targeted outreach to traditionally underserved communities.


Other Duties

· Perform other duties as assigned.

title: Project Manager
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Project Manager based in Australia.

This is an opportunity to lead the delivery of major residential communities across North West Sydney.
You’ll manage complex, staged subdivision and land development projects from early planning and design through construction and completion.
The role combines hands-on project leadership with strong commercial, technical, and stakeholder management responsibilities.
You’ll work closely with Development Managers, consultants, contractors, councils, and approval authorities to deliver successful project outcomes.
You’ll take ownership of programme, cost, quality, construction milestones, and practical solutions to emerging project challenges.
The environment is collaborative and fast-paced, giving you autonomy to ask questions, solve problems, and influence outcomes.
With a mix of site, office, and remote work, this role offers variety and meaningful impact on the communities being built.

Accountabilities

  • Manage end-to-end delivery of major staged subdivision projects, covering planning, design, approvals, construction, and completion.

  • Partner closely with Development Managers to deliver project outcomes across programme, cost, quality, and construction milestones.

  • Coordinate and manage relationships with civil contractors, consultants, councils, approval authorities, and internal stakeholders.

  • Oversee project planning and execution, ensuring key activities remain aligned with agreed timelines, budgets, quality expectations, and development objectives.

  • Identify potential project and construction challenges early and develop practical, commercially sound solutions to keep projects progressing.

  • Work collaboratively across technical and commercial disciplines to resolve issues and maintain strong project momentum.

  • Monitor construction activities and project milestones, maintaining a strong presence across active development sites.

  • Contribute to effective project governance, communication, and decision-making throughout the project lifecycle.

  • Build productive relationships with a broad range of stakeholders and ensure clear communication across project teams.

  • Take a proactive, hands-on approach to project delivery, continuously looking for opportunities to improve outcomes and address risks.

    • Requirements:

    • Tertiary qualification in Civil Engineering or a relevant technical discipline.

    • 5+ years of relevant experience across civil engineering, design, construction, land development, subdivision, or project management.

    • Strong practical experience delivering land development and civil subdivision projects, ideally within a property developer environment.

    • Demonstrated experience working with local councils, approval authorities, consultants, and contractors.

    • Strong commercial and project management capabilities, with the ability to manage competing priorities and project constraints.

    • Current driver licence and willingness to spend a minimum of three days per week on project sites.

    • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across technical, commercial, and operational teams.

    • A curious and solutions-focused mindset, with the confidence to ask questions, challenge assumptions, and find practical answers.

    • Collaborative approach and strong relationship-building skills, with the ability to work across different disciplines.

    • Proactive, hands-on, and “can-do” attitude, with the resilience and adaptability to succeed in a fast-paced project environment.

    • Ability to work independently and take ownership of outcomes in a role with no direct reports.

      • Benefits:

      • Opportunity to contribute to the delivery of major residential communities across North West Sydney.

      • Varied working environment combining site-based, office, and remote work.

      • Minimum three days per week on site, one day at the head office, and flexibility to work from home one day per week.

      • High level of ownership over project outcomes, with the opportunity to influence programme, cost, quality, and delivery strategy.

title: (772) Senior Policy Analyst
description:
Company Summary

Arlo Solutions (Arlo) is an information technology consulting services company that specializes in delivering technology solutions. Our reputation reflects the high quality of the talented Arlo Solutions team and the consultants working in partnership with our customers. Our mission is to understand and meet the needs of both our customers and consultants by delivering quality, value-added solutions. Our solutions are designed and managed to not only reduce costs, but to improve business processes, accelerate response time, improve services to end-users, and give our customers a competitive edge, now and into the future.

Position Description:

The XE Senior Policy Analyst provides senior-level policy research, analysis, coordination, and project management support to DC3 Strategy and Partner Engagement (XE) functions. The role leads development of policy products, supporting materials, and stakeholder engagement artifacts; manages complex policy initiatives from initiation through delivery; and ensures DC3 policy artifacts remain current, compliant, and well-documented for Government review and decision-making. The Senior Policy Analyst operates in a strictly advisory/support capacity—providing recommendations, draft products, analysis, and coordination support—while policy decisions and approvals remain Government responsibilities.

Location: Onsite - Linthicum Heights, MD

Clearance: Active TS/SCI

Responsibilities and/or Success Factors:

Policy research, drafting, and lifecycle management

  • Conduct comprehensive research on policy issues and guidance originating from Presidential, National, Federal, International, DoW/DoD, DAF, and DC3 authorities; translate findings into clear, actionable draft policy language and coordination packages for Government review.
  • Draft, update, and maintain DC3 policy artifacts, ensuring accuracy of roles, responsibilities, and authorities;
    • maintain version control, change logs, and a policy repository aligned to Government standards.
  • Proactively manage the DC3 policy lifecycle to prevent policy non-compliance caused by outdated or unrevised internal policies; track review cycles, suspense dates, and coordination status;
    • flag risks early for Government awareness.

Tasking intake and coordination support

  • Monitor and manage taskings across designated channels (e.g., ETMS2, email, NIPRNet, SIPRNet, JWICS) as assigned; develop and maintain task trackers; coordinate inputs across DC3 directorates;
    • and draft responses for Government review and release.
  • Identify overdue/at-risk taskings;
    • provide early-warning status updates and recommended path-to-green recovery actions to Government leadership.
  • Support Action Officer program administration, including rosters, training record updates, and task execution onboarding/job aids.

Support agreement and interagency coordination support

  • Assist Government Support Agreement Manager with drafting/coordination of support agreements and related documentation, maintaining comment matrices, version control, renewal tracking, and supporting evidence packages (as directed).
  • Prepare draft annexes, MFRs, and crosswalks between agreement language and cost structures to enable Government certification/approval. Strategic analysis, planning integration, and executive communications enablement
  • Develop policy-to-strategy alignment narratives and mapping artifacts that link DC3 objectives, initiatives, and performance measures (KPIs) to higher-level guidance and stakeholder requirements.
  • Prepare backgrounders, talking points, read-aheads, and briefings supporting DC3 participation in working groups and senior leader engagements; capture actions/decisions and maintain trackers to closure.
  • Coordinate and consolidate multi-directorate inputs into executive-level products, ensuring they are logically structured, consistent, and formatted to DC3 standards for Government decision-making.

Project management and performance measurement

  • Plan and manage complex policy projects end-to-end: develop schedules, dependencies, stakeholder coordination plans, and progress reporting; maintain risks/issues and propose mitigations (recommendations only).

title: Specialist, QC Data
description:
Salary Range: $65,000.00 To $75,000.00 Annually

Village Farms International (Nasdaq: VFF) is a vertically integrated global leader in cannabis and plant-based consumer packaged goods, driven by sustainable innovation. As one of North America's longest-standing produce operators built on decades of expertise, we're a company where growers, innovators, and creators come together to shape the future of high-performing plant-based brands around the world.

Joining Village Farms means joining a global team built on purpose, integrity, and ambition. Here, we grow people, ideas, and possibilities.

The Opportunity

As our QC Data Specialist, you will own and manage the stability testing program for our cannabis product portfolio, providing the scientific foundation for shelf-life determination, expiry dating, and international regulatory submissions. You will also own tracking, trending, and reporting of all analytical testing data from our internal and external laboratories, including the identification of Out of Trend (OOT) and Out of Specification (OOS) results and regular reporting through meetings, presentations, and formal reports. As the internal subject matter expert on stability science and laboratory data trending, you will work across Research & Lab, Quality Assurance (QA), Regulatory Affairs (RA), and Operations, exercising a high degree of technical judgment, accountability, and independence in a regulated GPP/GACP/EU-GMP environment

What You'll Do

Stability Program Management

  • Own and manage the end-to-end stability program for all cannabis product categories (dried flower, trim, extracts, novel formats), including study design, sample scheduling, data collection, trend analysis, and formal reporting; ensure all required studies are planned, initiated, and executed on the annual schedule
  • Design and maintain stability protocols aligned with ICH Q1A(R2), ICH Q1E, and applicable GPP/GACP/EU-GMP requirements, adapting them as new product formats or market requirements are introduced
  • Serve as the primary internal subject matter expert on stability science, providing technical guidance to QA, RA, Product Development & Innovation, and Operations on shelf-life, storage conditions, and product performance, and establishing and maintaining expiry dating and retest date rationale for all registered and in-development products
  • Identify and **escalate** OOT/OOS results and lead or support the resulting investigations and CAPAs; prepare and own stability summary reports for batch release, regulatory submissions, and partner/customer requests; and manage stability chambers and storage units (IQ/OQ/PQ, calibration, temperature/humidity monitoring, deviation management)

Sampling & Testing Coordination

  • Coordinate and physically prepare samples for stability time-points, GPP/ GACP/EU GMP batch release, compliance and research studies in accordance with SOPs, regulations, and good laboratory practices
  • Coordinate with third-party laboratories to ensure testing is accurate, in scope, and on time; manage Certificate of Analysis (COA) receipt, review, and filing; and review laboratory reports for accuracy, initiating and circulating Laboratory Investigation Reports (LIRs) and tracking resolution
  • Maintain accurate records in the Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system and SharePoint, including Chain of Custody (COC) documentation, sampling and requisition forms, and sample labels

Data Management, Trending & Reporting

  • Build, own, and continuously improve the laboratory and stability data management system (databases, trackers, dashboards), ensuring data integrity in accordance with ALCOA+ principles
  • Track and monitor all analytical testing data generated across the internal laboratory and external / third-party laboratories, spanning stability, batch release, in-process, and research testing, to maintain a consolidated, current view of laboratory quality data
  • Trend results over time and identify OOT/OOS patterns across products, cultivars, sites, processing routes, and testing stages; elevate emerging signals to QA, the QAP, and relevant stakeholders; and provide trend context and historical analysis to support investigations and CAPAs
  • Build and maintain data visualizations, graphs, and dashboards, and establish and maintain the cadence, format, and content standards for routine reporting, ensuring outputs are traceable, reproducible, and aligned with ALCOA+ principles
  • Deliver regular laboratory data reporting through recurring meetings, presentations, and formal written reports to QA, RA, Research & Lab, Operations, and management; maintain SOPs, work instructions, and forms governing stability, sampling, and testing; and support QA and RA during inspections, audits, and technical dossier preparation

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner with Product Development & Innovation on new products to establish stability-informed specifications and shelf-life targets, and provide stability data to RA for international submissions (e.g., EU- GMP, TGA, NZ MPI, IMCA)
  • Coordinate with Operations and Supply Chain on inventory and sample allocation for stability commitments, and prepare customer and wholesale partner samples per purchase order and SOPs

What You Bring

  • BSc or MSc (preferred) in chemistry, pharmaceutical sciences, biochemistry, life sciences, or a related field
  • Minimum 3–5 years in a laboratory, QC, QA, or regulatory role in a Health Canada-regulated environment (cannabis, pharmaceutical, or natural health products), including direct experience managing a stability program; EU GMP/GPP facility experience strongly preferred
  • Working knowledge of ICH stability guidelines (Q1A(R2), Q1B, Q1D, Q1E) and their application to shelf-life determination, with experience in stability chamber qualification and temperature/humidity monitoring
  • Demonstrated experience compiling, trending, and reporting laboratory or quality data from multiple sources (graphs, dashboards, formal reports); experience contributing to regulatory submissions incorporating stability data is an asset
  • Strong working knowledge of GPP/GACP/EU-GMP quality standards and ALCOA+ data integrity principles, applied to cannabis or pharmaceutical manufacturing
  • Demonstrated ability to design, execute, and interpret cannabis or pharmaceutical stability studies, including statistical and trend analysis of stability data and ICH Q1E approaches
  • Ability to consolidate, trend, and monitor analytical data from multiple internal and external sources, and to distinguish routine variability from meaningful OOT/OOS signals
  • Proficiency in data visualization and reporting tools (e.g., Power BI, advanced Excel) to build graphs, dashboards, and trend reports; proficient with MS Office, ERP systems, and LIMS or equivalent
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills with exceptional attention to detail; able to critically evaluate COAs, laboratory reports, and regulatory guidance and to present clear technical reports to cross-functional audiences
  • Able to lift and transport samples and laboratory materials up to 20 kg, and work in a controlled-access facility environment including donning and doffing appropriate PPE
  • Able to work independently with a high degree of accountability while collaborating across departments; must be able to obtain and maintain a valid security clearance (RCMP criminal record check)

Life at Village Farms

  • At Village Farms International, you're part of something bigger — a global organization where you can grow your career across brands, functions, and countries.
  • We believe It Takes A Village®, and we mean it.
  • Our values guide every decision we make: Versatility | Innovation | Leadership | Loyalty | Accountability | Grit | Entrepreneurship
  • What you do here matters — to our people, our products, and the customers we serve around the world.
  • We've got you covered with company-paid comprehensive benefits and education assistance to support your continued growth.
  • We embrace meaningful opportunities, collaboration, and continuous improvement as we expand our global footprint.

title: Head Of Data
description:
About Fundraise Up

We're Fundraise Up, a global fundraising platform built to make donating to nonprofits fast, seamless, and accessible to all. Every month, our technology powers tens of millions of dollars in donations across the globe. Many of the world's leading nonprofits trust our platform, including UNICEF, the Alzheimer's Association, and a wide range of global NGOs, and we hold a 4.9/5 rating across top software review platforms. Our mission is to unlock the world's generosity potential by optimizing how people give.

About the Role

AI is only as good as the data underneath it. This role makes ours trustworthy.

As our Head of Data, you'll build and guarantee the data foundation the whole company builds on: the pipelines, the models, the definitions, and the contracts that let people and AI agents trust what they're looking at. You'll report to our CFO, which keeps you neutral to any single function and close to how the business actually runs and measures itself. This is a player-coach seat. You'll write code and do the hardest technical work yourself, ship a major internal AI-powered initiative every quarter alongside our AI Transformation team, and grow this into a full function as it proves its value.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the data infrastructure, hands-on. Design, build, and run the pipelines and ETL/ELT that feed our warehouse. Own freshness, reliability, and cost. Treat the infrastructure as never finished, and keep making measurable gains in coverage, latency, and reliability.

title: Quality Inspector, Receiving
description:
K2 is building the largest and highest-power satellites ever flown, unlocking performance levels previously out of reach across every orbit. Backed by over $1 billion in total funding from leading investors including Altimeter Capital, ICONIQ, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Redpoint Ventures, and T. Rowe Price — and with over $1 billion in signed contracts across commercial and US government customers, we're mass-producing the highest-power satellite platforms ever built for missions from LEO to deep space.

The rise of heavy-lift launch vehicles is shifting the industry from an era of mass constraint to one of mass abundance, and we believe this new era demands a fundamentally different class of spacecraft. Engineered to survive the harshest radiation environments and to fully capitalize on today's and tomorrow's massive rockets, K2 satellites deliver unmatched capability at constellation scale and across multiple orbits.

With multiple launches in 2027 and plans to scale to 100 satellites a year, we're Building Bigger — helping develop the solar system and build toward a Kardashev Type II (K2) civilization. If you are a motivated individual who thrives in a fast-paced environment and you're excited about contributing to the success of a high-growth Series D-funded company, we'd love for you to apply.

The Role

You will be responsible for performing receiving and in-process inspections of aerospace hardware supporting satellite production. You will work closely with Production, Supply Chain, Manufacturing Engineering, and Quality Engineering to ensure incoming hardware meets drawings, specification, documentation, and workmanship requirements while maintaining the pace required by a rapidly scaling production environment.

Responsibilities

  • Perform detailed incoming inspection of mechanical parts, electronic assemblies, harnesses, flight hardware, and other production material
  • Verify hardware against drawings, purchase requirements (QC), specifications, certifications, and applicable quality requirements
  • Perform dimensional inspection using calipers, micrometers, heigh gauges, pin gauges, thread gauges, and other precision inspection equipment
  • Review supplier documentation including certificates of conformance, material certifications, inspection reports, and FAIR documentation
  • Record inspection results and maintain hardware traceability within ERP, MES, and QMS
  • Identify, document, and initiate nonconformance records for discrepant hardware
  • Work directly with Supply Chain, Production, Design and Manufacturing Engineering to quickly disposition inspection issues
  • Support containment activities and supplier escape investigations
  • Help identify opportunities to simply inspection plans and improve receiving inspection throughput
  • Support in-process and final inspection activities as production priorities require

Qualifications

  • 3+ years of quality inspection experience in aerospace, precision machining, automotive, medical device, or another highly regulated manufacturing environment
  • Strong blueprint reading and GD&T fundamentals
  • Proficiency with precision measuring equipment and techniques
  • Familiarity with ERP/MES systems for tracking inventory and inspection results
  • Knowledge of ESD handling procedures and ITAR compliance requirements
  • Ability to independently make sound inspection decisions in a fast-paced production environment

Nice to Have

  • Aerospace receiving inspection experience
  • Familiarity with ISO 9001/AS9100 quality management systems
  • Ability to review drawings and identify improper callouts/datum structures, according to ASME Y14.5
  • Experience with receiving and inventory transactions in an ERP system
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs.

Additional Requirements

  • Willing to work overtime and weekends as needed
  • Must be able to stoop, bend, crawl, and maneuver in tight spaces
  • Must be able to lift and carry parts or equipment up to 50 lbs. unassisted

Compensation and Benefits:

  • Hourly pay range for this non-exempt role is $30 - $45 + equity in the company
  • Compensation will be based on several factors including, but not limited to: knowledge and skills, education, and experience level
  • Comprehensive benefits package including paid time off, medical/dental/vision coverage, life insurance, paid parental leave, and many other perks

If you don’t meet 100% of the preferred skills and experience, we encourage you to still apply! Building a spacecraft unlike any other requires a team unlike any other and non-traditional career twists and turns are encouraged!

If you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know.

title: Community Outreach Coordinator
description:
The Coordinator of Community Outreach reports to the Principal of the assigned CHP School. The Coordinator of Community Outreach is responsible to improve student achievement by assisting in the creation of community involvement in CHP Schools by assessing school, parent and other community needs and coordinating parent involvement, family support activities and community outreach programs at assigned schools in response to those needs and by assisting in the coordination of the planning, implementation, monitoring, communicating and evaluation of activities and services for parents and other community members at school facilities and in the community.

I. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

The following is an explanation of the duties of the Community Outreach Coordinator. It includes the major highlights of the requirements of the position. There should be a clear understanding that the duties outlined below are not all encompassing. Additional responsibilities may be assigned to the Community Outreach Coordinator as required.

  1. Working with school staff in developing, implementing and evaluating parent and community involvement and community outreach activities.

  2. Advocating for parents and promoting interest in schooling and enhancing sense of community and commitment.

  3. Coordinating parent and community involvement activities and services with other agencies and organizations.

  4. Acting as a liaison between parents and community members and other agencies and organizations.

  5. Serving as a resource to parents and community members regarding community agencies, events and activities.

  6. Identifying students with credit deficiencies and making referrals to alternative programs.

  7. Providing transportation to students and families to community resources for the receipt of social services.

  8. Assessing needs of parents and community members.

  9. Assisting school staff in the development, implementation, and evaluation of educational activities and programs, including family literacy programs offered at the school for parents and other community members.

  10. Encouraging parents of bilingual/bicultural students to upgrade their skills and knowledge of the educational process.

  11. Assisting in the recruitment and training of school volunteers.

  12. Helping school staff to develop and coordinate extended day, before and after school and intersession programs.

  13. Promoting school projects and programs to the community.

  14. Facilitating community involvement in school programs and activities.

  15. Assisting in coordinating community use of school facility.

  16. Assisting with recruitment, training, and monitoring of community members volunteering in student mentor program.

  17. Assisting school and other CHP Schools with home visits.

  18. May serve as interpreter during parent-teacher conferences, special education meetings, disciplinary referrals, and other school-based meetings as needed.

  19. Maintaining regular and consistent attendance and punctuality.

  20. Performing related duties consistent with job description and assignment.

II. Truancy Duties

  1. Enforces compulsory school attendance laws by counseling parents who are in violation.

  2. Maintain consistent communication through monthly school visits and home visits with families and provide ongoing support to students as needed.

  3. Network with school personnel to identify student’s needs and to identify resources available for students and their families at the individual school sites.

  4. Provide home and school visits to students and their families to assess barriers to school attendance and case management needs.

  5. Monitor school attendance and compliance with the recommendation made by School Guide.

  6. Provide link to parent education groups for the families of the student who are truant through the School Based Parent Program and Student Excellence Center.

  7. Holds truancy information sessions for the advisory committee and develops the plan for the student, parents, and the school to follow.

  8. Updates school principals and staff and provides recommendations.

  9. Presents truancy programs to the community and school groups.

  10. Prepares and writes reports and miscellaneous correspondence.

  11. Participates in and collaborates with a variety of committees, professional associations, boards, and/or other related groups.

  12. Become familiar with and stay current with available youth services in the community including programs in churches and community centers.

  13. Develop and maintain effective working relationships with individuals from a variety of cultural and ethnic backgrounds.

  14. Demonstrates awareness and acceptance of cultural differences of clients, staff and community contacts.

III. PROFESSIONALISM

  1. Interpersonal/Teamwork

  1. Maintains positive and professional relationships with colleagues, children and parents.

  2. Contributes as a team member and actively collaborates with others to meet the mission and goals of CHP Schools.

  1. Work Habits

  1. Knowledgeable and supportive of CHP Schools’ policies and procedures, including those in the Policy and Procedure Manual, and implements them consistently.

  2. Knowledgeable of laws, regulations, and standards pertinent to his or her work and demonstrates compliance.

  3. Demonstrates integrity by striving for safe and effective service delivery, as well as accurate, timely and complete documentation.

  4. Contributes to maintaining a ‘Culture of Safety’ for students, parents, colleagues and visitors.

  5. Reports to work, as well as all meetings and appointments, in a timely manner.

  6. Dresses appropriately and professionally based on scheduled activities of the given day. Strives to serve as a role model to clients.

  1. Professional Development

  1. Participates in individual supervision as scheduled by supervisor.

  2. Accepts and follows suggestions, directives, and requests to perform additional duties willingly and flexibly.

  3. Consults his or her supervisor or others, as appropriate, for collaborative problem solving.

  4. Exercises sound judgment, knowledge, and creativity in decision making.

  5. Takes on personal development and building a learning environment.

  6. Completes and demonstrates competency in all mandatory trainings as identified by the organization including knowledge of child and adolescent growth and development.

  7. Participates in additional trainings as identified in supervision or by external licensing, contractual, and accreditation organizations.

title: Senior Product Manager, Roblox Conversational Platform
description:
Every day, tens of millions of people come to Roblox to explore, create, play, learn, and connect with friends in 3D immersive digital experiences– all created by our global community of developers and creators.

At Roblox, we’re building the tools and platform that empower our community to bring any experience that they can imagine to life. Our vision is to reimagine the way people come together, from anywhere in the world, and on any device. We’re on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and looking for amazing talent to help us get there.

A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.

At Roblox, we're building the tools and platform that empower our community to bring any experience that they can imagine to life. Our vision is to reimagine the way people come together, from anywhere in the world, and on any device. We're on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and looking for amazing talent to help us get there.

A career at Roblox means you'll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.

The Conversational Platform team builds the AI-powered support experiences that help players, parents and creators get answers and resolve issues quickly, along with the reusable platform that brings this capability to teams and creators across Roblox.

As Senior Product Manager for Roblox Conversational Platform, you will own the product for all Roblox support experiences and build the conversational intelligence layer that automates customer support at Roblox scale. You will turn that technology into reusable platform components that other teams across the company can adopt, and extend it to our creator community so developers can support their own players with bug reports, feature requests, refunds, and more. The same platform will also power support for creators on Creator Platform issues. You will lead large, cross-team initiatives, partnering deeply with Engineering, ML, Design, Data Science, Customer Support Operations, and Creator teams, and raise the bar for product excellence across the organization.

You will:

  • Define and own the end-to-end product strategy for Roblox support experiences across web, mobile, and in-experience surfaces, serving players, parents, and creators.
  • Build the conversational intelligence layer that automates customer support, including LLM-powered agents, intent understanding, knowledge retrieval, and secure integrations that let agents take action on a user's behalf, such as account recovery, purchase issues, and refunds.
  • Platformize the technology by designing reusable components such as agent orchestration, knowledge management, tool and action frameworks, evaluation and quality tooling, and human handoff, so other teams across Roblox can build their own conversational experiences on top of it.
  • Extend the platform to the creator community, giving developers the tools to support their own player base with bug reports, feature requests, refunds, and more.
  • Bring the platform to creator support, using it to resolve Creator Platform issues for the developers building on Roblox.
  • Set the quality bar and success metrics, such as automated resolution rate, accuracy, CSAT, time to resolution, and cost per contact, and build the evaluation and experimentation practices to improve them over time.
  • Partner deeply with Engineering, ML, Design, Data Science, Customer Support Operations, Trust & Safety, Legal, and Creator teams to deliver reliable, safe, and helpful support experiences.
  • Represent Conversational Platform in senior forums, driving alignment on strategy, tradeoffs, and platform adoption through clear written narratives and data-driven reviews.

You have:

  • 5-8+ years of product management experience, with significant time spent on conversational AI, customer support or CX technology, or AI/ML platform products.
  • Hands-on experience shipping LLM-powered products in production, such as AI agents, chatbots, retrieval-augmented generation, or classification systems, including how to evaluate and improve model quality over time.
  • A proven track record building platforms: reusable APIs, services, or components adopted by multiple internal or external teams.
  • Strong technical depth and experience partnering with ML and infrastructure engineers on system architecture, model tradeoffs across quality, latency, and cost, and integrations with backend systems.
  • Familiarity with customer support operations and tooling, including ticketing and case management, agent workflows, knowledge bases, and the metrics that drive them.
  • Experience operating at a senior scope, setting strategy for a major product area, leading cross-org initiatives, and influencing senior stakeholders.
  • Expert written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to build clear narratives, efficiently drive alignment across teams, and make thoughtful, data-informed decisions.
  • Bonus: experience building for developer or creator ecosystems, or for products used by younger audiences.

You are:

  • Customer-obsessed, with a deep understanding of what it feels like to be a player locked out of an account, a parent with a safety concern, or a creator whose experience is broken, and motivated to resolve their issues quickly and with care.
  • A platform thinker who designs for reuse and connects today's support needs to a long-term vision for conversational intelligence across Roblox.
  • Safety- and quality-minded, holding a high bar for accuracy, privacy, and responsible AI, and clear on when automation should hand off to a person.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity, able to bring structure and clarity to a fast-moving AI space without waiting for perfect information.
  • A trusted cross-functional partner who builds strong relationships with Engineering, ML, Design, Data, and Operations teams and works through complex tradeoffs together.
  • Calm and decisive under pressure, able to balance short-term execution with long-term strategic bets.

title: Chief Technology Officer
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Chief Technology Officer based in Canada.

This is a senior technology leadership opportunity focused on shaping the future of enterprise software that supports critical public-sector and justice systems. You will own the technology strategy, architecture, product development, and engineering direction across a complex software portfolio. The role combines long-term technical vision with hands-on organizational leadership, modernization, product thinking, and operational excellence. You will work closely with executive leadership and cross-functional teams to align technology investments with customer needs and business priorities. A major part of the mandate will be building a high-performing technology organization while advancing secure, scalable, reliable, and configurable platforms. You will also help identify emerging technologies and new opportunities, including the practical application of AI and data-driven capabilities.

Accountabilities

  • Develop and lead a multi-year technology strategy and roadmap aligned with long-term organizational goals, ensuring the technical vision is understood and adopted across the business.

  • Establish a customer-centric, problem-first product development approach that ensures teams understand user needs, business challenges, and desired outcomes before committing to technical solutions.

  • Identify emerging technologies, market opportunities, partnerships, and potential acquisitions that can strengthen existing products and create new sources of value.

  • Advise executive leadership on technology investments, build-versus-buy decisions, strategic partnerships, acquisitions, and other major technology initiatives.

  • Define the architectural vision and engineering principles for secure, scalable, configurable, modular, repeatable, and maintainable systems that can evolve as customer and business needs change.

  • Promote platform thinking through reusable services, APIs, shared components, and common capabilities that can support multiple products and business units.

  • Lead modernization of the technology portfolio by balancing investment in existing platforms with technical debt reduction, consolidation, modernization, and next-generation capabilities.

  • Lead the engineering organization with a culture centered on ownership, craftsmanship, continuous improvement, pragmatic decision-making, quality, reliability, and security.

  • Advance modern engineering practices while balancing speed of delivery with operational resilience, product quality, cybersecurity, and long-term maintainability.

  • Support the organization's transition toward Agile methodologies and Scrum-at-Scale, helping teams adopt effective delivery practices and continuous improvement.

  • Build strong partnerships across departments, creating alignment around technology priorities, timelines, resources, dependencies, and organizational goals.

  • Translate complex technical concepts into clear business language for executives and non-technical stakeholders while bringing business context and customer priorities back to technical teams.

  • Build, lead, and develop a high-performing technology organization through organizational design, leadership development, succession planning, workforce strategy, and recruitment of critical technical talent.

  • Establish and maintain appropriate standards for security, privacy, compliance, and data governance, including requirements relevant to government agencies, courts, and criminal justice environments such as CJIS.

  • Oversee technology investment, performance, operational resilience, and resource allocation to ensure systems remain reliable, scalable, secure, and prepared for business continuity.

  • Establish effective technology governance and risk-management practices in partnership with Security, Cloud Operations, IT, Legal, and business leadership to manage architectural, cybersecurity, regulatory, and third-party technology risks.

    • Requirements:

    • Bring 12+ years of software engineering experience, including at least 5 years in senior technical leadership positions such as CTO, VP of Engineering, Head of Engineering, or a comparable role.

    • Demonstrate proven experience leading and scaling engineering organizations and enterprise software platforms in complex technology environments.

    • Possess deep expertise in software and systems architecture, including distributed systems, cloud-native architecture, APIs, data platforms, scalability, security, and modern engineering practices.

    • Bring strong product judgment and experience making customer-driven product and technology decisions based on real user needs and business outcomes.

    • Demonstrate a track record of establishing compelling technical visions and successfully aligning engineering teams, executives, and other stakeholders around strategic priorities.

    • Have excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to engage effectively with executives, engineers, customers, partners, and non-technical stakeholders.

    • Experience in government technology, justice or court systems, legal technology, or other regulated public-sector environments is highly desirable.

    • Experience incubating new products or working within a startup, innovation lab, venture environment, or similarly entrepreneurial setting is preferred.

    • Hands-on experience applying artificial intelligence, machine learning, and data-driven technologies to real-world products is preferred.

    • Experience working in Agile environments or formal training in Scrum or Agile methodologies is expected.

    • Hold a bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical discipline; an advanced degree is considered an advantage.

    • Be comfortable operating as a strategic technology leader while remaining close enough to engineering, architecture, product, and customer needs to make informed decisions.

    • Candidates must be eligible to work in Canada without employer-sponsored visa or work authorization support.

title: Materials Characterization Technician II, Mechanical
description:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known.

Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us.

About the Team:

The Materials and NDE (Non-Destructive Evaluation) team plays a central role in enabling Terran R to fly, re-fly, and scale: developing, characterizing, and inspecting materials and processes across all parts of the vehicle. From welding and additive manufacturing to advanced composites, the team works at the intersection of innovation and execution, balancing performance and reliability with cost, quality, and schedule. As we move toward first flight and beyond, the challenges become more exciting, offering opportunities to shape how we design and develop for re-use. With ownership across products, systems, and disciplines, engineers gain broad exposure and drive key decisions across design, manufacturing, and operations.

About the Role:

  • Perform tensile, compression, hardness, fatigue, and other mechanical tests according to approved procedures
  • Prepare, measure, identify, and inspect test specimens to confirm they meet testing requirements
  • Set up test fixtures, grips, extensometers, and instrumentation appropriate for each test
  • Operate mechanical testing equipment and monitor tests for abnormal behavior
  • Record test conditions, observations, and results accurately while maintaining specimen traceability
  • Review data for completeness and flag unexpected results, equipment issues, or procedural deviations
  • Complete routine equipment checks and maintenance; verify calibration status before use
  • Troubleshoot common setup and equipment problems, escalating issues when needed
  • Work with engineers and other technicians to coordinate testing priorities and schedules
  • Support training of newer technicians on established procedures and safe equipment operation
  • Maintain a clean, organized laboratory and follow all safety requirements

About You:

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Typically two or more years of relevant experience in mechanical testing, materials testing, or a laboratory environment
  • Working knowledge of mechanical testing equipment, specimen preparation, and measurement tools
  • Ability to read technical drawings, work instructions, and applicable ASTM testing procedures
  • Understanding of basic material properties, including yield strength, tensile strength, elongation, and hardness
  • Ability to use testing software, enter data, and prepare clear test documentation
  • Strong attention to detail, communication, and problem-solving skills

Nice to haves, but not required:

  • Associate degree or technical certification in materials science, mechanical technology, or a related field
  • Experience with metallic materials, aerospace applications, and servo-hydraulic or electromechanical test systems
  • Familiarity with fatigue testing, extensometers, load cells, and data acquisition systems.

title: Quality Engineering Specialist
description:
Build bold. Deliver impact. Win together. At General Dynamics Mission Systems–Canada, we’re not just engineering technology — we’re shaping the future of defence and security. Our teams design and deliver advanced, mission-critical solutions that enhance national security, strengthen communities, and protect the people we serve. If you’re looking for meaningful work that contributes to a safer, more secure world, you’ll find purpose here. Every day, your skills will directly impact programs that matter.

Job Description

We are looking for an experienced Quality Engineering (QE) Specialist to join our Quality team in Ottawa, Halifax or Calgary. Reporting to the Quality Manager, the QE Specialist plays a key role within integrated project teams, ensuring compliance with internal processes and external standards including AS9100 and or ISO9001. This position supports both engineering development and product lifecycle activities, with a strong emphasis on software, quality compliance, and audit leadership.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Provide pre-contract quality support, including estimating the effort required to implement Quality Assurance (QA) activities and contributing to proposal documentation.
  • Prepare and implement project-specific QA plans and contribute quality-related inputs to broader project documentation.
  • Act as the quality lead for assigned projects, ensuring compliance with AS9100, and other relevant contractual or airworthiness standards.
  • Interface with the DND TAA (within DTAES), and customer quality representatives during software audits (e.g., SOIs).
  • Conduct independent process and product audits, identify non-conformances, issue corrective actions, and track them to closure.
  • Serve on Configuration Control Boards (CCB) and Material Review Boards (MRB); support design reviews and configuration audits.
  • Collaborate with Engineering, Supplier Quality, and Product Support to ensure quality considerations are embedded across all phases of development, sustainment, and supply chain interactions.
  • Monitor formal test activities (e.g., acceptance, qualification) for adherence to approved test plans and procedures; ensure evidence supports certification and compliance.
  • Lead and participate in project and quality review meetings, including setting agendas, facilitating discussions, documenting actions, and ensuring follow-up.
  • Lead quality-related reviews, investigations, and root cause analyses, and facilitate continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Use data and statistical analysis to monitor quality performance, identify trends, and support corrective/preventive action planning.
  • Report quality metrics and present findings during quality forums, project gates, and leadership reviews.
  • Engage in proactive risk identification, mitigation planning, and knowledge sharing throughout the project lifecycle.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned.

Qualifications

What You Need to Have to Succeed

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical discipline.
  • Minimum of 3 years’ experience in engineering or software development, with at least 1 year in a quality assurance role.
  • Strong working knowledge of AS9100.
  • A sound understanding of current engineering development / tools methodologies and standards.
  • Proven ability to conduct internal audits, lead investigations, and lead cross-functional teams to resolution.
  • Experience supporting software and systems development within a regulated aerospace or defense environment.
  • Excellent communication and reporting skills; ability to influence across functions and levels.
  • Familiarity with lean principles and continuous improvement methodologies.

What Makes You Stand Out

  • Membership in a professional quality body (e.g. ASQ).
  • Experience interfacing with government/defense QA authorities.
  • Knowledge of Systems Engineering and Engineering Development processes.
  • Proficiency in DOORs.
  • Experience working with or familiarity with AI/ML models.

It is a requirement that General Dynamics Mission Systems-Canada be registered with the Canadian Controlled Goods program and that all of its workforce be security assessed. Successful applicants must meet all applicable security requirements, including but not limited to the ability to obtain and maintain a Canadian government security clearance. Applicants may be required to meet additional security requirements in order to gain access to technical data, classified areas or information that is subject to international regulations. You must be eligible to work in Canada.

Additional Information

The expected hiring range for this position is $77,000 – $98,000 CAD annual.

Our goal is to provide a fair and competitive offer based on an assessment of internal equity and your qualifications, including:

  • Relevant experience
  • Technical and non-technical skills

Benefits

As a full-time employee at General Dynamics Mission Systems–Canada, you’ll enjoy a competitive total rewards package that supports your professional and personal well-being:

  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and eligible dependents from day one (no cost), including flexible benefits options (HCSA) emergency travel insurance, and 24/7 virtual care services.
  • Employee & Family Assistance Program (EFAP), onsite fitness facilities, and employee resource groups.
  • Defined Contribution Pension Plan with employer contributions after 3 months, RRSP access from day one, and financial planning support.
  • Flexible time off including vacation, holidays, parental leaves with top-up options, sick leave, and disability programs.
  • Career development through learning platforms, educational assistance, mentoring, and reimbursement of professional memberships.
  • Additional perks such as employee discounts, free onsite parking, social clubs, and an annual scholarship program for employees’ children.

Why join us?

  • Purposeful Innovation: You’ll work on innovations that genuinely make a difference. You’ll apply advanced thinking, design expertise, and practical problem-solving to help equip military and allied forces with leading-edge systems. You’ll be surrounded by some of the brightest minds in the defence sector, contributing to next-generation technologies in an environment that celebrates creativity, new ideas, and modern solutions.
  • Connection: We believe people do their best work when they feel they belong, and their ideas can flourish. Different perspectives, experiences, and ways of thinking help us innovate and grow. Strong relationships with our teammates help us unite, overcome challenges, and deliver the world-class quality we’re known for. Here, we are committed to inclusivity and ensures every individual feels valued, respected, and empowered.
  • Challenging and Rewarding Career Pathways: Your career path matters to us. From mentorship and regular check-ins with your leader to educational support, professional certifications, and continuous training, you’ll have the resources you need to thrive. We encourage internal mobility so you can explore different business areas, broaden your skillset, and expand your network. You’ll be working on high-profile, impactful projects that challenge your skills, expand your expertise, and allow you to both learn from mentors and guide others along the way.

Accommodation

If you require accommodation during any stage of the application process, please contact Human Resources via recruitment@gd-ms.ca.

Closing Date

We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if we receive sufficient applications for the role. Therefore, if you are interested, please submit your application as early as possible.

title: Geologic Technician / Core Cutter
description:
Position Summary

Based at our facility in Mariposa, California the Geologic Technician / Core Cutter supports the Exploration and Geology teams by safely processing diamond drill core and assisting with geological data. This position is responsible for core cutting, sampling, labeling, and maintaining a safe, organized core facility.

The role requires a strong commitment to safety, attention to detail, and the ability to work in a physically demanding mining and exploration environment.

Key Responsibilities

Core Processing & Sampling

  • Cut diamond drill core using core saws in accordance with geologist instructions and sampling protocols
  • Label, bag, and prepare samples for shipment following chain-of-custody and QA/QC requirements
  • Maintain sample integrity and accurate documentation
  • Photograph core and assist with core layout, orientation, and archiving
  • Ensure proper handling, storage, and security of drill core

Geological Support

  • Assist geologists with core handling, logging preparation, and sample selection
  • Record basic geological measurements and observations as directed
  • Support QA/QC programs including blanks, standards, and duplicates
  • Assist with core recovery tracking and reconciliation of samples

Health, Safety & Environmental Compliance

  • Work in compliance with Cal/OSHA, MSHA (where applicable), and site-specific safety requirements
  • Perform pre-operational inspections of core saws and equipment
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and hazard-free core shack or facility
  • Use required PPE at all times (eye protection, hearing protection, gloves, steel-toe boots, etc.)
  • Immediately report hazards, near misses, and incidents

General Duties

  • Perform routine cleaning and maintenance of core saws and related equipment
  • Assist with inventory management of sampling supplies and consumables
  • Support other exploration or geology-related tasks as assigned
  • Work collaboratively with geologists, drillers, and contractors

Required Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license
  • Familiarity with diamond drill core handling and sampling procedures
  • Ability to safely perform physical work, including lifting and moving core boxes
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to follow written and verbal instructions
  • Basic computer skills for data entry and sample tracking

Preferred Qualifications

  • Post-secondary education in Geology, Earth Sciences, or a related field
  • Experience as a core cutter, geologic technician, or exploration laborer
  • Cal/OSHA/MSHA safety training, First Aid/CPR
  • Experience with geological databases, logging software, or core photography systems

Work Environment

  • Work will occur in a core facility but may require field work or travel to an underground mine site.
  • Exposure to water, dust, noise, vibration, and varying temperatures
  • Shift work, weekends, or rotational schedules may be required

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs
  • Ability to stand, bend, kneel, and perform repetitive tasks for extended periods
  • Ability to work safely around industrial equipment

Compensation

The pay range for this position will be $20.00 - 25.00 per hour, depending on qualifications and experience. This position is non-exempt and eligible for overtime.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Keystone Mines Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all applicable California employment laws. We are committed to maintaining a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace.
